name: Wes Moore
subject: I'm asking you to support a fellow Airborne officer today
body:
He’s not a Democrat. Here’s why I’m backing him.
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2128%2E1086043%2EHLLKvc)
Peter,
I want to tell you about someone I'm supporting for the United States Senate. He isn't a Democrat. I'm not asking him to become one. But I am asking you to help him anyway.
His name is Seth Bodnar, and he's running as an Independent in Montana. **[Today, I’m asking you to split a donation between our campaigns to help him win this Senate seat.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261016-2.FTASZb&refcode=em-20261016-2&t=2&akid=2128%2E1086043%2EHLLKvc)**
Before I was Governor of Maryland, I was a captain in the United States Army, with the 82nd Airborne Division in Afghanistan. Seth was an officer in the 101st Airborne who led an infantry platoon in Mosul, Iraq, and later served as a Green Beret.
We both went to Oxford as Rhodes Scholars. We both came home believing the same thing: that this country works best when people serve something bigger than themselves.
In the Army, nobody asks the soldier next to you what party they belong to. Your tribe isn’t red or blue; it’s red, white, and blue. **Your job is to show up for the person next to you when it counts.** Seth showed up for nineteen years in uniform, and then for eight years leading the University of Montana. Now, he is showing up for his state, when it would have been a lot easier not to.
The Republican nomination in Montana was handed to Kurt Alme eight minutes before the filing deadline. There was no real primary. No other Montanan got a say. Seth's answer was to collect nearly 30,000 signatures from voters in 52 counties and earn his place on the ballot the honest way. **Then a Trump-aligned Super PAC started spending millions attacking him.**
Seth is now gaining momentum faster than any candidate in that race. He's doing it without a party backing him. And in a Senate that's forgotten how to put country first, I'd like to see someone like Seth help us get back to solving the serious problems facing working people in this country.
**[So I’m asking: will you split a $10 donation between my campaign and Seth's to send a fellow Airborne officer to the United States Senate?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261016-2.FTASZb&refcode=em-20261016-2&t=3&akid=2128%2E1086043%2EHLLKvc)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261016-2.FTASZb&amount=5&refcode=em-20261016-2&t=22&akid=2128%2E1086043%2EHLLKvc)**
Montana deserves a senator who answers to Montana. I'm a Democrat, and I'm proud of it. But I'm prouder of the idea that service comes before party, and I'll back anyone who lives it.
With gratitude,
Wes Moore
Governor of Maryland

And in a Senate that's forgotten how to put country first, I'd like to see someone like Seth help us get back to solving the serious problems facing working people in this country. Montana deserves a senator who answers to Montana. I'm a Democrat, and I'm proud of it. But I'm prouder of the idea that service comes before party, and I'll back anyone who lives it. With gratitude, Wes Moore Governor of Maryland

| Peter,
It's not just a far-fetched hypothetical anymore.
A new explosive report from Axios reveals that Trump's top allies are openly discussing martial law if MAGA loses big in the upcoming midterm elections.
On a livestream for MAGA election activists, Trump's childhood friend and attorney, Peter Ticktin, said it plainly: "There would have to be martial law in the event... [of] another rigged election."
He did not stop there. He told Axios that officials need to commandeer ballots and voting machines. Another speaker on the same call said he wants the election paused entirely. A third floated using emergency powers to force states to change how they count votes.
---
| | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001eMqAJUiW0l7BpoQKHGkxia_pS1mlQWR9bgALI_UZl6dtupPzc-vLV18nbJhda_6_GLaqbRlLcFz4hCy80sCZD1cr1gtD5DEM59XcBV1I_wlYI1O04US6MnA7VDf3f7TyO27uQDBMPEA3sNDGoECRvNkZvf0XblItIkgYfmSEYPaHQkwCdRUghvc-qnMAUIdzjipU9waBcLtcOIKCgJkrxQXINtzfks2C&c=Pm7TTxLC7gQe72tENz7WhH1XGcQsZzq0xLrrRN-1hSg1XCiS9JcfsA==&ch=f6nmm-7h4lefo0Mgkv1damXdWUJBicN3YybCXJLNNbyyNn609LS1_g==)
---
These are not just random people on the internet. These are some of Trump's closest allies, with direct access to the Oval Office.
Tina Peters, who was convicted of crimes tied to breaching election equipment, met with Trump privately in the Oval Office this month. She and Ticktin were both at the White House in June.
What they are plotting is illegal as hell. Trump has no authority to delay a federal election or seize ballots and voting machines. But if his presidency has taught us anything, it is that he has no problem breaking the law.
That is why it is up to our courts to stop him. The Constitution is clear: states run elections, not the feds. And when Trump comes for our ballots, state courts will be the first and last line of defense against his coup.
This is exactly why Defend Our Courts exists. We're building a firewall of state courts to protect elections, and turning Dems out in battleground states with key House and Senate races. With only 18 days until the election, we need the support of Dems everywhere to defend and build pro-democracy majorities on key state courts in Michigan, Montana, and North Carolina.

clean_body: What they are plotting is illegal as hell | | | | | == | Peter, It's not just a far-fetched hypothetical anymore. A new explosive report from Axios reveals that Trump's top allies are openly discussing martial law if MAGA loses big in the upcoming midterm elections. On a livestream for MAGA election activists, Trump's childhood friend and attorney, Peter Ticktin, said it plainly: "There would have to be martial law in the event... [of] another rigged election." He did not stop there. He told Axios that officials need to commandeer ballots and voting machines. Another speaker on the same call said he wants the election paused entirely. A third floated using emergency powers to force states to change how they count votes. | | == These are not just random people on the internet. These are some of Trump's closest allies, with direct access to the Oval Office. Tina Peters, who was convicted of crimes tied to breaching election equipment, met with Trump privately in the Oval Office this month. She and Ticktin were both at the White House in June. What they are plotting is illegal as hell. Trump has no authority to delay a federal election or seize ballots and voting machines. But if his presidency has taught us anything, it is that he has no problem breaking the law. That is why it is up to our courts to stop him. The Constitution is clear: states run elections, not the feds. And when Trump comes for our ballots, state courts will be the first and last line of defense against his coup. This is exactly why Defend Our Courts exists. We're building a firewall of state courts to protect elections, and turning Dems out in battleground states with key House and Senate races. | | | Oregon didn't just adopt vote-by-mail. We INVENTED it. **So when President Trump signs an executive order restricting mail-in ballots, understand what that means: ** No state has more on the line than Oregon. This order isn't aimed at some abstract "voting system." **It targets how every single Oregonian votes.** Here's what Trump’s USPS order does. It orders the Postal Service to deliver ballots only to voters on a federal list — a list built by THIS administration. Their postmaster already said the quiet part out loud: states that don't hand over their voter data likely won't have mail ballots delivered at all. Now here's what I know. **I'm Oregon's chief elections officer. We have taken this administration to court — over their demand for your voter data, and over their first election order. We won.** _**They still are not stopping. **_ **The Constitution hasn't changed**. States run elections. Not presidents. Not postmasters. And this November, Oregon will run the same safe, fair, accurate vote-by-mail election we've run for 25 years — and I will use every power of this office to make sure of it. **[But fighting them in court is only one way to defend our elections. We must have the resources to communicate about what’s at stake — every lawsuit, every rule change, every attempt to rewrite how Oregon votes. That’s why I’m using my campaign to help travel around the state and talk directly to voters too. Chip in to help us keep fighting.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141539913/653895766/-569431239?refcode=261016-invented-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNmNkMjVhMy02NmM5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=2o2sl6h6dq6N2aLRE56eYGROwSAiUfbWIFf-DhAenAA=)**

Peter, Last year, on live TV, Mike Lawler promised that he would not cut Medicaid. **Then he was the deciding vote on Trump’s One Big Ugly Bill that kicked nearly half a million New Yorkers off their healthcare.** But this year, he’s been campaigning on the exact opposite. He’s claiming that there have been NO Medicaid cuts at all. Meanwhile, hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers have already lost care. Mike Lawler is the worst kind of politician: self-serving and corrupt. No amount of spin can change that simple fact. Every American should have the right to access affordable healthcare. **Growing up, my dad worked as a construction worker, where his ability to earn a living depended upon his ability to stay healthy, but he could not always afford health insurance.** When it comes to ensuring working Americans like my dad can live with dignity, we need to have a strong floor and no ceiling. That means protecting and strengthening Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid. These are non-negotiable programs we must protect. It also means lowering the cost of healthcare by taking on Big Pharma and insurance companies, and leading the charge for a public option to bring down premiums. I will fight for all of that and more when I get to Congress—because my mission is to make life easier for you. But first, we need to take on Lawler and flip this district. subject: One number could help save a child
body:
Put a rescue hotline where someone who needs help can see it.

| | | |
---
| |
---
| | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
|
---
| | | Friend,
---
**One number could help save a child.** **833-599-3733** But first, someone needs to see it. That's why I am writing to you today. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I am the producer of the film _Sound of Freedom_ and founder of the **Sound of Freedom Foundation. **Years ago, I learned what traffickers do to innocent children. It broke my heart. I knew I could not look away. I have said before: **" When good people keep quiet or look away, they become part of the problem."**I decided not to stay quiet or look away. Friend, I am asking you to join me.
---
[ Yes, I'll carry the number](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT2P3CAQhn8N7s7iw4vtgiLSyt2liCKlRGMYbHRgHD42yr-PvHtlqith3nlePZpf7_odfPDH9h0iqlydzkWnA48WV8wmtWB3DGeBB4LZNadcvjH6xqQGU_0D9QCdVdZYYKZDxcaZs9vMheh2xThdBUjBJwarvE0zG8fJoRB0tiAldF5dPEaZZAOlfOrlzI27jWxASmdpLRkoBMy1z3i2NXgDR4Xy4VI22JsUu6D2Ws9CxDfCF8KXgqZl7Etqh03OZUSborteUH06-pS3K5WcNpDz35fl00qD-U3EUlLLBrVJFom4__i5sGEaBCVcthp1ROtbJOKOEXz4_HytEHHfIVsoH0_Sa2QgnuC3g4j7_zo_UxXzxeyysucfH4IvciQD3a6Op2X94mEeiv8LAAD__yBIodI)
---
We have created a special pack of _**Carry the Number**_ stickers printed with a rescue hotline number.
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT2P3CAQhn8N7s7iw4vtgiLSyt2liCKlRGMYbHRgHD42yr-PvHtlqith3nlePZpf7_odfPDH9h0iqlydzkWnA48WV8wmtWB3DGeBB4LZNadcvjH6xqQGU_0D9QCdVdZYYKZDxcaZs9vMheh2xThdBUjBJwarvE0zG8fJoRB0tiAldF5dPEaZZAOlfOrlzI27jWxASmdpLRkoBMy1z3i2NXgDR4Xy4VI22JsUu6D2Ws9CxDfCF8KXgqZl7Etqh03OZUSborteUH06-pS3K5WcNpDz35fl00qD-U3EUlLLBrVJFom4__i5sGEaBCVcthp1ROtbJOKOEXz4_HytEHHfIVsoH0_Sa2QgnuC3g4j7_zo_UxXzxeyysucfH4IvciQD3a6Op2X94mEeiv8LAAD__yBIodI)
---
When you make your first gift of **any amount** to the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** , we will send you a sticker pack so you can help put this important number into your community. Put one in your car. Share one with your church. Ask a local business to display one. Help make this number visible. Why? Because trafficking hides in darkness. A person may see something that does not seem right but not know where to turn. Someone in danger may desperately need a way to reach out. You can help someone in the grip of a trafficker who wants to break free. This 24/7 hotline provides real people waiting for that call. This visible hotline could facilitate a victim's safe and secure exit from the life of enslavement, and the next steps to begin a new life journey.All calls are 100% confidential.
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT2P3CAQhn8N7s7iw4vtgiLSyt2liCKlRGMYbHRgHD42yr-PvHtlqith3nlePZpf7_odfPDH9h0iqlydzkWnA48WV8wmtWB3DGeBB4LZNadcvjH6xqQGU_0D9QCdVdZYYKZDxcaZs9vMheh2xThdBUjBJwarvE0zG8fJoRB0tiAldF5dPEaZZAOlfOrlzI27jWxASmdpLRkoBMy1z3i2NXgDR4Xy4VI22JsUu6D2Ws9CxDfCF8KXgqZl7Etqh03OZUSborteUH06-pS3K5WcNpDz35fl00qD-U3EUlLLBrVJFom4__i5sGEaBCVcthp1ROtbJOKOEXz4_HytEHHfIVsoH0_Sa2QgnuC3g4j7_zo_UxXzxeyysucfH4IvciQD3a6Op2X94mEeiv8LAAD__yBIodI)
---
A child, teen, or young adult trapped in trafficking may be searching for a way out. Seeing that number could give them the courage to make one call -- **a call that could be their first step toward freedom.** Something as small as a sticker can carry such an important message. **You are not alone.** **There is a number to call.** **There are people willing to act.** That's also why I believe awareness must lead to action. The film _Sound of Freedom_ brought the horror of child trafficking before millions of people. But a movie alone cannot end this evil. So we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** to carry this mission forward. We work to help prevent exploitation, support intervention efforts, educate parents and communities, spread information, and influence policies that protect children.
---
[ Yes, I'll carry the number](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT2P3CAQhn8N7s7iw4vtgiLSyt2liCKlRGMYbHRgHD42yr-PvHtlqith3nlePZpf7_odfPDH9h0iqlydzkWnA48WV8wmtWB3DGeBB4LZNadcvjH6xqQGU_0D9QCdVdZYYKZDxcaZs9vMheh2xThdBUjBJwarvE0zG8fJoRB0tiAldF5dPEaZZAOlfOrlzI27jWxASmdpLRkoBMy1z3i2NXgDR4Xy4VI22JsUu6D2Ws9CxDfCF8KXgqZl7Etqh03OZUSborteUH06-pS3K5WcNpDz35fl00qD-U3EUlLLBrVJFom4__i5sGEaBCVcthp1ROtbJOKOEXz4_HytEHHfIVsoH0_Sa2QgnuC3g4j7_zo_UxXzxeyysucfH4IvciQD3a6Op2X94mEeiv8LAAD__yBIodI)
---
And beneath everything we do is one truth I will never stop saying: **GOD 'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE.** Jesus said: _" As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you. Now remain in my love."_ (John 15:9) Every child has God-given worth. Every child deserves protection. And every one of us can choose whether we look away or act. Friend, today I am asking you to act. Make your first gift to the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Your generosity helps fuel our larger mission to protect vulnerable children and fight exploitation. [**And with your gift of $10, $15, $25 or whatever you can do today, we'll send you a ****_Carry the Number_**** sticker pack.**](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT2P3CAQhn8N7s7iw4vtgiLSyt2liCKlRGMYbHRgHD42yr-PvHtlqith3nlePZpf7_odfPDH9h0iqlydzkWnA48WV8wmtWB3DGeBB4LZNadcvjH6xqQGU_0D9QCdVdZYYKZDxcaZs9vMheh2xThdBUjBJwarvE0zG8fJoRB0tiAldF5dPEaZZAOlfOrlzI27jWxASmdpLRkoBMy1z3i2NXgDR4Xy4VI22JsUu6D2Ws9CxDfCF8KXgqZl7Etqh03OZUSborteUH06-pS3K5WcNpDz35fl00qD-U3EUlLLBrVJFom4__i5sGEaBCVcthp1ROtbJOKOEXz4_HytEHHfIVsoH0_Sa2QgnuC3g4j7_zo_UxXzxeyysucfH4IvciQD3a6Op2X94mEeiv8LAAD__yBIodI) Then I want you to do something important with it. **Carry it. Share it. Put the number where it can be seen.** Imagine thousands of ordinary people doing the same thing. Thousands of cars, churches, businesses, and community spaces carrying a simple message: We see these children. We will not be silent. And we will not surrender them to darkness. **CARRY THE NUMBER.**
**SHARE THE NUMBER.**
**HELP BRING A CHILD HOME.**

[ Yes, I'll carry the number](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT2P3CAQhn8N7s7iw4vtgiLSyt2liCKlRGMYbHRgHD42yr-PvHtlqith3nlePZpf7_odfPDH9h0iqlydzkWnA48WV8wmtWB3DGeBB4LZNadcvjH6xqQGU_0D9QCdVdZYYKZDxcaZs9vMheh2xThdBUjBJwarvE0zG8fJoRB0tiAldF5dPEaZZAOlfOrlzI27jWxASmdpLRkoBMy1z3i2NXgDR4Xy4VI22JsUu6D2Ws9CxDfCF8KXgqZl7Etqh03OZUSborteUH06-pS3K5WcNpDz35fl00qD-U3EUlLLBrVJFom4__i5sGEaBCVcthp1ROtbJOKOEXz4_HytEHHfIVsoH0_Sa2QgnuC3g4j7_zo_UxXzxeyysucfH4IvciQD3a6Op2X94mEeiv8LAAD__yBIodI)

clean_body: Put a rescue hotline where someone who needs help can see it. | | | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | | Friend, One number could help save a child. 833-599-3733 But first, someone needs to see it. That's why I am writing to you today. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I am the producer of the film Sound of Freedom and founder of the Sound of Freedom Foundation. Years ago, I learned what traffickers do to innocent children. It broke my heart. I knew I could not look away. I have said before: " When good people keep quiet or look away, they become part of the problem."I decided not to stay quiet or look away. Friend, I am asking you to join me. We have created a special pack of Carry the Number stickers printed with a rescue hotline number. When you make your first gift of any amount to the Sound of Freedom Foundation , we will send you a sticker pack so you can help put this important number into your community. Put one in your car. Share one with your church. Ask a local business to display one. Help make this number visible. Why? Because trafficking hides in darkness. A person may see something that does not seem right but not know where to turn. Someone in danger may desperately need a way to reach out. You can help someone in the grip of a trafficker who wants to break free. This 24/7 hotline provides real people waiting for that call. This visible hotline could facilitate a victim's safe and secure exit from the life of enslavement, and the next steps to begin a new life journey.All calls are 100% confidential. A child, teen, or young adult trapped in trafficking may be searching for a way out. Seeing that number could give them the courage to make one call -- a call that could be their first step toward freedom. Something as small as a sticker can carry such an important message. You are not alone. There is a number to call. There are people willing to act. That's also why I believe awareness must lead to action. The film Sound of Freedom brought the horror of child trafficking before millions of people. But a movie alone cannot end this evil. So we created the Sound of Freedom Foundation to carry this mission forward. We work to help prevent exploitation, support intervention efforts, educate parents and communities, spread information, and influence policies that protect children. And beneath everything we do is one truth I will never stop saying: GOD 'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE. Jesus said: " As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you. Now remain in my love." (John 15:9) Every child has God-given worth. Every child deserves protection. And every one of us can choose whether we look away or act. Friend, today I am asking you to act. Make your first gift to the Sound of Freedom Foundation. Your generosity helps fuel our larger mission to protect vulnerable children and fight exploitation. Then I want you to do something important with it. Carry it. Share it. Put the number where it can be seen. Imagine thousands of ordinary people doing the same thing. Thousands of cars, churches, businesses, and community spaces carrying a simple message: We see these children. We will not be silent. And we will not surrender them to darkness. CARRY THE NUMBER. SHARE THE NUMBER. HELP BRING A CHILD HOME. Please join us today. Because God 's children are not for sale. With gratitude and prayer, Eduardo Verastegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For the Sound of Freedom Foundation P. O. Box 131727, Houston, TX 77219-1727 Ensure the mission continues. **FRIDAY, OCTOBER 16, 2026**
He was eleven. For five months, we had fed the chickens, cleaned their space, cuddled them, and laughed at their antics. We had raised them for food. The time came, and my son knew the task was his. We had studied _shechitah_ ; the rules were in place.
For three hours, he prayed and cried. Then he carried out the task.
He has prayed every time since. The tears belonged to that first experience alone.
There is a difference between accepting the weight of a responsibility and making an exception to escape it. The test of a principle is not whether it costs us, but whether we remain faithful to its purpose when it does.
When an exception is made, we must ask: does it honor the principle, or merely excuse us from it?
**Pause.**
**Breathe.**
**Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

body:
People often ask...how did I get that name?

| [](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMTZfUVctWUIuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDYwMTE1LTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDE2X1FXLVlCLjExMDExN190MjA2MDExNS0yMDY4In0/Nja5a37m6Sv6QykBikQbEw)
---
That’s a picture of me from when I flew H-46 and H-3 helicopters in the U.S. Navy. If you look to my left, you can see my call sign...**Blossom.**
People often ask...how did I get that name?
Well, my roommate in flight school and I went on a bit of a “girl power” kick one day and bought old bathtub non-skid flower stickers from the store, cut out that flower shape in reflective tape from our squadron, and stuck those reflective flowers on our helmets.
There is very little room for making a Navy flight suit more “feminine,” but on cruise we were able to be a little more creative and came to love those girly flowers on our helmets.
Although the helicopter community doesn’t use call signs as much as some of the fixed wing squadrons, the “Blossom” stuck and was painted on the side of a CH-46 for part of my first cruise. Made for a great photo and story!
It was my experience in the Navy that helped instill in me the importance of service.
Far too often, our elected officials today forget that their job is to SERVE. They think it is their job to tell everyone what to do and why everyone else is wrong....but that’s not service.
As a Navy veteran and nurse practitioner, I got so frustrated and decided to run for Congress because I wanted to actually SERVE my country and my community.
**While for some it is all about power, for me it is all about service.**
Sadly, this has made me some enemies in Washington.
No one is going to buy me off or tell me what to do...I’m going to keep serving the people I represent, not serve some “master” in Washington, D.C.
If you are also tired of leaders who care more about power than service, [I’m asking you to send me some help today.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMTZfUVctWUIuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDYwMTE1LTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDE2X1FXLVlCLjExMDExN190MjA2MDExNS0yMDY4In0/oL5_g2wAH1SptYslOnview)
Because I’m a veteran and not a career politician, I need all the help I can get to support my fight against the Democrats.
---
| [RUSH SUPPORT TO JEN](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMTZfUVctWUIuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDYwMTE1LTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDE2X1FXLVlCLjExMDExN190MjA2MDExNS0yMDY4In0/gd6p9ohL3iYW6MCTK9YceA)
---
I know this was a longer message than you are probably used to getting, but I want you to know where I’m coming from and why I need your help. Whether it’s $100 or just $10, anything you can contribute will help this Navy veteran keep fighting back business as usual in D.C.
It’s time we support leaders who truly want to serve our country, and that’s what I promise to always do...are you with me, Peter?
With the courage to fight,

-Jen

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: I need to be blunt about this war
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
We need a Congress willing to take a stand against this forever war

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3055%2E4032634%2ERjWO8Y)
---
Forever wars don’t just happen. They’re enabled. By a president who starts a war, profits off of it, and refuses to end it. By lawmakers who could hold him accountable but choose to look away. And by a system where those who decide to go to war don’t ultimately pay the price. Trump’s war in Iran has dragged on for more than six months. Thousands of people have been killed. Families have spent months fearing for their loved ones. And the consequences of this unnecessary war will be felt for years, even generations. The bleak truth is that wars cost money — and those funds come from American pockets. Last month, the Pentagon told lawmakers the war has cost $45.1 billion. That's billions of taxpayer dollars spent on a war that keeps driving up costs for families already struggling to get by. CNN reports that the war has cost about $2,000 per American household so far, with another $50 added every week it continues. Gas is averaging $4.34 a gallon. Diesel, which powers the trucks, tractors, and trains that keep our economy moving, is near record highs. Homes using heating oil are expected to pay 21% more for the fuel than last winter. And while working families are stretching every paycheck, Trump’s largest oil and gas holdings gained an estimated $1.5 million to $4.4 million in the war’s first six months. Families are paying more. Trump’s oil and gas interests are making more. And the war just keeps going. This cannot continue. Congress has both the power and the responsibility to stop this war. Under the War Powers Act, lawmakers can force a vote on ending unauthorized U.S. military involvement in Iran. But Republicans have allowed Trump to prolong this conflict instead of using their power to bring it to an end. I know many of you are angry about what this administration is doing. I am, too. I grieve for everyone killed in this conflict, and I think about the families at home trying to understand why their loved ones are being sent into a war with no clear end in sight. They deserve answers. They deserve accountability. And they deserve a Congress willing to use every tool it has to end this war. We can end this war. And I’ll keep fighting to make sure we do. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

**FROM EVIDENCE TO ACTION**
* **THE FACTS:** What does Philadelphia's academic performance reveal, and what can Mississippi's remarkable progress teach us?
* **THE STANDARD:** What should every child know, understand, and be capable of doing before entering adulthood?
* **THE SOLUTIONS:** What actually builds success, and what roles must parents, educators, pastors, and community leaders play?
* **THE REALITIES:** An honest conversation about the streets, the system, and the obstacles facing Philadelphia's young people.
* **THE ACTION:** _Philadelphia, What Now?_ An opportunity for attendees to help identify practical next steps for our homes, schools, and communities.

This is where you become part of the conversation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a2398720-12d9-450e-b672-bc8d5e6c4677?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We're not bringing people together simply to listen to experts. We're bringing people together to learn from one another, challenge assumptions, raise expectations, and identify what we can begin doing in our own homes, schools, and communities.
**[Because the future of our children is too important to leave to government.](https://substack.com/redirect/a2398720-12d9-450e-b672-bc8d5e6c4677?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Join us.
**Saturday, October 24, 2026 | 9 a.m. -2 p.m.**
📍 Braid Mill, 441 E. High Street, Germantown, Philadelphia
Doors open at 8:30 a.m. Caribbean fusion brunch included.
Tickets start at $35. **Pastors, teachers, and Germantown residents attend FREE.** Registration is required, and seating is limited.
[RESERVE YOUR SEAT TODAY](https://substack.com/redirect/a2398720-12d9-450e-b672-bc8d5e6c4677?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**If Mississippi can do it, surely Philadelphia can too.**
Let's get to work!

Election Day is 18 days away. Candidly, we're not where we need to be to meet my team's goal.
Here's what's at stake:

**[1]** Election Day is less than 3 weeks away. We need to register, turn out, and win over every single persuadable voter across Kentucky before my opponent Andy Barr gets to them first.
**[2]** The path to flip the Senate runs through this race. Mitch McConnell is retiring, and this seat is open. It's our once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to flip Kentucky BLUE and loosen MAGA's grip on our state.
**[3] Right now,** Andy is relentlessly attacking me on the airwaves. Meanwhile, he's too cowardly to even debate me face to face. I need to retaliate through my grassroots efforts, but that takes resources.
I don't have corporate PACS or billionaires funding my campaign. I only have Democrats like you who believe Kentucky deserves better than Mitch 2.0.
So if you're with me, I'm counting on you to step up before it's too late.

Thank you, thank you, thank you.
Charles Booker

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

#### **['OH, SHUT UP!' Troy Jackson Snaps at Susan Collins in Explosive Final Maine Senate Debate](https://substack.com/redirect/d726f5f1-834f-44e8-921a-d7c8b32ec4bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Collins and Jackson's fourth and final debate, at Husson University's Gracie Theatre in Bangor, had a live audience, which meant it also had a heckler from the climate cult. While Collins was talking, a protester started yelling that AI data centers are "destroying our climate" and "poisoning our water," and the moderators stopped while security dealt with it. Collins: "So this is obviously one of Troy's supporters." Jackson: "Oh, shut up... I don't even know that kid." As for the temper, it's not new. There's the 1988 Fort Kent police report in which a 19-year-old Jackson kicked through a door, grabbed a man by the throat and hit him, all in a dispute over the affections of Jackson's second cousin. And who can forget the plastic water bottle he allegedly threw during a 2021 argument with another lawmaker?

#### **[Lewiston Shooting Families Demand Answers as Records Show Nearly $2 Million Went to Nonprofits Without Mandatory Full Spending Reports](https://substack.com/redirect/1574250c-a533-4960-a1ae-d2ab78ec909a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
People gave about $6.6 million after the Lewiston shootings. The Maine Community Foundation sent $4,696,067 of it to 162 victims, families and survivors, and $1,900,132 to 29 nonprofits at $65,522 apiece. In a February fact sheet, the foundation acknowledged it never required those nonprofits to file full reports on how they spent the money. Survivors and families gathered at Veterans Memorial Park on Wednesday to ask, again, for an independent review. Jennifer Zanca, who was shot at Schemengees, says she got $93,000 in hospital bills her insurer wouldn't cover. "The FBI, Homeland Security came to my home and told me I would never have to worry about hospital bills," she said. "Except I did." Attorney General Aaron Frey (D) ruled in September that the Legislature's watchdog can't investigate because it's private charity money. Amy Sussman says 57 survivors and relatives filed a complaint with his office in April, and it was declined. The third anniversary of Maine's worst mass shooting is Oct. 25.
#### **[Suspect Allegedly Rams Into ICE Vehicle During Sanford Operation](https://substack.com/redirect/aaa533d6-1921-4401-92c0-d2c55363689c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
ICE agents boxed in a car on Brook Street in Sanford around 9:19 a.m. Thursday to arrest a man they say is an illegal immigrant. ICE agents told police he threw it in reverse and rammed the ICE vehicle behind him, with a one-year-old in the car who reportedly wasn't properly secured in a car seat. The tot was taken to the hospital as a precaution, and Chief Eric Small later said the child was fine and the damage was minor. Then, police say, officers learned the man's two other kids, ages 2 and 9, had been left home alone nearby, and child protective services was called. The man's name, nationality and the reason for the arrest still haven't been released.
#### **[Maine Fraternal Order of Police Endorses Susan Collins in U.S. Senate Race](https://substack.com/redirect/369dbdfb-6d0c-4b63-a10b-175c54470d54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The state's largest police union, with more than 1,000 members across about 50 agencies, is backing Collins for a sixth term. The union pointed to the Social Security Fairness Act, which Collins co-wrote with Democrat Ohio Sen. Sherrod Brown and which restored benefits to more than 25,000 Mainers, cops and teachers included. Her office says she has steered $46.4 million to Maine law enforcement and public safety projects since 2021. "To our knowledge, she has never voted for an anti-law enforcement bill during her entire time in office," said the union's Joel Wilkinson. The same union endorsed Paul LePage in September.
#### **[Reports of Gunfire in Rumford Lead to Shelter-in-Place Order and Warrant Execution as Police Continue Search for Armed Suspect](https://substack.com/redirect/9d6c4969-f69e-4ae4-91b5-ed509f7468b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Neighbors on Waldo Street had been telling Rumford police that people tied to a first-floor apartment were firing guns off now and then, on top of tips about drug dealing out of the place. After another gunfire call early Wednesday, police set up a perimeter, issued a shelter-in-place order and brought in the State Police tactical team. They went in around 1 p.m. and found the apartment empty; police think the suspects left hours earlier. They're now looking for Blake LaChance, 21, of Lewiston, wanted for aggravated assault, criminal threatening and reckless conduct, all with a dangerous weapon. Police say he may be armed and dangerous.
#### **[Man Wanted for Theft from Sporting Goods Store Arrested While Wandering in South Portland Traffic](https://substack.com/redirect/b8dde3dc-74b2-43b1-8a3c-dad1e177eb8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Callers reported a man dressed in black, apparently intoxicated, walking in traffic on Maine Mall Road around 6 p.m. Wednesday. South Portland officers recognized Joshua Maloney, 30, as their suspect in two felony thefts from Dick's Sporting Goods over the past week. He was already out on bail on cocaine and fentanyl possession charges, and police say he had a liquid on him that field-tested as either a fentanyl compound or meth -- mystery drug juice! He's charged with two counts of felony theft, drug possession and violating bail. Bail conditions remain undefeated.
#### **[Suspect Flees Auburn Traffic Stop Before Sustaining Serious Injuries During Crash](https://substack.com/redirect/932e9bc1-a6ca-4c52-963c-dab58195de5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
An Androscoggin deputy tried to pull over a car for a traffic violation at 10:42 Monday night. The driver kept going into Auburn on Minot Avenue and crashed in the 1600 block. A woman in the car went to Central Maine Medical Center and was then moved to Maine Medical Center with serious injuries. Police haven't named the driver or said whether charges are coming. The Maine Wire continues to receive tips on this one: tips@themainewire.com

**Jackson finally files** : Troy Jackson's campaign filed its first FEC report at about 6:15 p.m. Thursday, the deadline day, after promising it for Wednesday morning. It covers July 7 through Sept. 30: $19.4 million in contributions, $20.4 million in total receipts, $16.5 million out the door, just under $4 million in cash, and $1.03 million in debts. A separate filing shows J Street PAC bundled $155,511 for him. Collins raised $3.9 million in the quarter and spent about $10.8 million; her own filing shows about $17.7 million raised for the cycle with $5.4 million cash on hand. Republican-aligned groups have spent or reserved $151 million on ads to Democrats' $111 million, according to FEC reports and FCC public file records.
**Next FEC deadline** : pre-general reports, covering Oct. 1-14, are due **Thu., Oct. 22**. (cc Troy Jackson's finance team)
**Ethics Commission deadline** : the 11-day pre-general campaign finance reports are due **Fri., Oct. 23**.

Hey everyone, Matt here.
Before we get into the numbers, take a look at my [Ohio Congressional Campaign Finance Tracker](https://substack.com/redirect/d5c60b10-1503-4691-aa25-545757843456?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). You can compare candidates, explore their campaign finances, and see the outside money coming into these races.
The latest financial reports have dropped. We are less than three weeks from the midterm elections, and while another reporting deadline is coming before Election Day, these third-quarter reports give us a substantial look at the money behind the campaigns.
These numbers cover July through September, with cash balances as of September 30.
And in Ohio's 7th District, **Brian Poindexter** absolutely crushed Max Miller in fundraising.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3e35db6f-328e-4c34-aca3-0099d5383ab3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
## Ohio's 7th: Poindexter Raised Nearly 17 Times as Much
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/14c32997-25c8-4716-914a-b5216cbbb86f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Brian Poindexter raised **$2,461,285 in contributions** during the third quarter.
Max Miller raised **$145,525**.
That is a difference of **$2,315,760**. Poindexter brought in nearly **17 times** as much in contributions as Miller.
Miller also loaned his campaign **$1 million of his own money**. That pushed his total receipts to approximately $1.15 million, but we need to be clear about what that means. A personal loan does not represent people opening their wallets to support your campaign.
It represents you opening your own.
And the change from the previous quarter is striking.
Poindexter's contributions increased from approximately $466,000 to $2.46 million, a **428% increase**.
Miller's fell from approximately $405,000 to $146,000, a **64% decline**.
That is a dramatic shift in fundraising momentum.
The cash position is also very different from what I initially thought. They did not end the quarter with roughly the same amount available, and Miller was not ahead.
**Poindexter ended September with $1,066,833 in cash. Miller had $122,835.**
That put Poindexter ahead by approximately **$944,000**.
Miller **spent** heavily during the quarter, about **$2.40 million** , compared with Poindexter's **$1.72 million**. So Miller outspent him by approximately $688,000 while ending with substantially less money available. Miller's committee also reported approximately **$1.965 million in debt**.
**The fundraising gap is enormous. The question now is how that translates into votes.**
* * *
## Small Contributions Tell Another Part of the Story
Looking at where the money came from, there is an interesting difference between percentages and actual dollars.
Among reported individual-contribution dollars, Miller received approximately **$41,635** from unitemized contributions and itemized contribution entries of $200 or less.
Poindexter received approximately **$659,863** in that same category.
That matters. A high small-contribution percentage can sound impressive until you look at the size of the fundraising base underneath it.
Poindexter also received approximately **$981,619** in individual contribution entries of $2,000 or more, representing **43.4%** of his individual-contribution dollars.
His fundraising surge included substantial money at both ends.
These categories measure contribution amounts, rather than each donor's total giving. Somebody making repeated smaller contributions can ultimately give much more than $200.
* * *
## Who Gave to Miller and Poindexter?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ea7dc45d-04c7-4d93-9bd2-488ae63908e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Don Henley Welcome to the Hotel OH-7**
There are some recognizable names in these reports.
Selected individual contributions to **Max Miller** included:
* **Daniel Loeb: $3,500.** Founder and CEO of investment firm Third Point. The contribution was marked as earmarked through AIPAC.
* **Gila Milstein: $3,500.** Cofounder of the Adam and Gila Milstein Family Foundation. Her contribution was also marked as earmarked through AIPAC.
* **Keith Mardak: $1,000.** Former Hal Leonard music-publishing executive and philanthropist.
* **Michelle Primm: $1,000.** Cascade Auto Group managing partner and a National Automobile Dealers Association board member.

Selected individual contributions to **Brian Poindexter** included:
* **JB Pritzker: $3,500.** The Illinois governor.
* **Robert Rubin: $3,500.** Former U.S. Treasury secretary.
* **Penny Pritzker: $1,314.81.** Former U.S. Commerce secretary.
* **Allen Blue: $3,500 in technology services.** The LinkedIn cofounder's contribution was reported as in-kind.
* **Phoebe Gates: $3,500.** Phia cofounder and daughter of Bill Gates.
* **Mark Clein: $7,000 across two contributions.** Cofounder of Precision Medicine Group.
* **Roger Altman: $3,500.** Founder of investment bank Evercore.
* **Blair Effron: $3,500.** Cofounder of investment bank Centerview Partners.
* **Marta Kauffman: $3,500.** Cocreator of _Friends_.
* **Don Henley: $3,500.** The Eagles musician.
* **Bonnie Raitt: $1,000.** The singer-songwriter.

Those are individual contributions. Listing someone's business background does not mean the business itself donated.
But the names show how much national attention this race is attracting.
* * *
## The Outside Money Is Pouring Into Ohio's 7th
Then there is the money being spent outside the campaigns.
These expenditures do not go into Miller's or Poindexter's campaign accounts. Outside organizations pay for their own advertising, canvassing, mail, and other activity supporting or opposing candidates.
The latest identified notices include approximately:
* **Congressional Leadership Fund: $2.24 million opposing Poindexter.** This is a major House Republican outside-spending organization.
* **Your Community PAC: $1.98 million opposing Miller.**
* **House Majority PAC: $1.60 million opposing Miller.** A major organization working to elect House Democrats.
* **Ready for the Fight: $1.47 million opposing Miller.** JB Pritzker serves as its honorary chair.
* **Jobs & Prosperity PAC: $580,712 opposing Poindexter and $116,337 supporting Miller.** A pro-Miller super PAC whose disclosed funders include Brian Colleran, RMS Investment Group, and members of the Haslam family.
* **Retired Americans Action: $177,424 opposing Miller.**
* **Stand Up for Ohio: $140,280 supporting Poindexter and $66,450 opposing Miller.**
* **Progressive Turnout Project: $138,753 supporting Poindexter.**

There are other notable interests involved, too.
**Elon Musk-backed America PAC** reported approximately **$64,029 opposing Poindexter** and **$17,654 supporting Miller**.
**America First Agriculture Action** , which has received cannabis-industry funding, reported approximately **$54,895 opposing Poindexter** and **$51,502 supporting Miller**.
**SEIU COPE** reported approximately **$14,688 supporting Poindexter** and another **$14,688 opposing Miller**.
Earlier processed spending also included approximately **$570,204 supporting Poindexter from Jobs and Democracy PAC** , associated with the Public First AI-policy network, and **$198,019 from BDA PAC** , Blue Dog Action's political committee. Both of those amounts reflected primary spending.
That timing matters. Money spent to help someone win a primary should not be presented as though it all arrived for the general election.
The recent notices remain provisional because amendments, estimated costs, and reporting issues still need reconciliation. I am not adding them together and calling the result a verified grand total.
What is clear is that national party organizations, wealthy donors, labor, and industry interests are paying attention to Ohio's 7th.
* * *
## Where the Campaigns Are Spending
The campaigns themselves are putting substantial money into advertising.
Miller reported approximately **$2.02 million to Strategic Media Placement for media buys**.
Poindexter reported approximately **$1.02 million to LC Media for advertising and video production** , plus approximately **$275,516 to Kinetic Strategies for advertising and digital fundraising**.
Poindexter also reported approximately **$81,109 to the Ohio Democratic Party** for coordinated campaign, payroll-related, and administrative costs, along with **$50,800 for polling**.
These are campaign expenditures, separate from the outside spending above.
This is going to be a very interesting race. The fundraising momentum is clearly behind Poindexter, even in a district that has favored Republicans.
His union background, the concentration of organized labor in Cuyahoga County, and Miller's high profile all help explain why this race is getting attention. Miller's messy divorce has also been part of the public conversation.
* * *
## Ohio's 9th: The Iron Babushka Has the Advantage
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dc3c5f42-e83b-4d9a-ba7c-b325bef862dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Marcy Iron Babushka Kaptur
Marcy Kaptur's race against Derek Merrin is another one worth watching.
Kaptur raised **$1,220,236 in contributions** during Q3. Merrin raised **$398,608**.
That is approximately **three times as much** for Kaptur.
She also spent heavily: approximately **$3.53 million** , compared with Merrin's **$299,366**.
At the end of September, Kaptur had **$1,246,370 in cash** , while Merrin had **$787,056** , giving her an advantage of approximately **$459,000**.
Democrat Marcy Kaptur represents a Republican-leaning district, yet she has faced numerous challengers over the years and has always come out on top.
* * *
## Ohio's 10th: Knickerbocker Out Raised Turner
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/93c2da94-a15e-4f27-af6f-c0c2f14dd74c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In Ohio's 10th District, Democrat **Kristina Knickerbocker** raised **$509,992 in contributions** , compared with Republican **Mike Turner 's $338,385**.
Knickerbocker outraised Turner by approximately **$172,000** , or about **51%**.
Turner still had the cash advantage at the end of September: **$588,342** , compared with Knickerbocker's **$303,192**.
That makes this a different financial picture from Ohio's 7th. The Democratic challenger led in quarterly contributions, but the Republican incumbent retained more money.
This is another potential red-to-blue opportunity that deserves attention. I do not think it should get lost simply because the 7th has attracted a larger fundraising surge and a higher-profile political fight.

## Ohio's 14th: What Happens When Your Race Gets Less Attention
The Angry Ohioan
[Ohio's 14th Congressional District: Maria Jukic vs. Dave Joyce](https://substack.com/redirect/2bbf37ec-3912-437e-a09b-68705a1d513d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

2 months ago * 3 likes * 3 comments * The Angry Democrat
Ohio's 14th shows a very different situation.
Republican **Dave Joyce** raised **$243,219 in contributions** during Q3. Democrat **Maria Jukic** raised **$42,052**.
Joyce ended September with approximately **$2.33 million in cash**. Jukic had approximately **$25,141**.
To me, this illustrates the power of national party attention and the fundraising networks that come with it. When your race becomes a priority, the resources can change dramatically. When it does not, raising enough money to compete can be a constant struggle.
I know what that feels like.
In my race against Miller, he raised around $3 million while I raised around $300,000. I spent days and nights on the phone trying to bring money in.
Then you see what happens when the party and national donors "decide" a race is worth investing in. The difference is startling.
* * *
## Ohio's 13th: The Opposite Picture
In Ohio's 13th District, Democrat **Emilia Sykes** raised **$719,122 in contributions** during Q3.
Republican **Carey Coleman** raised **$39,426**.
Sykes ended September with **$1,102,523 in cash**. Coleman had **$60,684**.
Sykes had approximately **18 times as much in quarterly contributions and cash on hand**.
My read is that Coleman is not attracting the financial support you would expect for a serious push to flip the seat. It looks like a race where Republicans are allowing their candidate to fall far behind.
The numbers alone do not prove a formal decision to abandon him. But financially, this is a dramatically lopsided contest.
* * *
## Two Other Races Worth Noting
In **Ohio 's 1st District**, Democrat **Greg Landsman** raised **$868,506 in contributions** , compared with Republican **Eric Conroy 's $455,107**.
Landsman ended September with approximately **$1.50 million in cash**. Conroy had approximately **$303,000**.
In **Ohio 's 11th District**, Democrat **Shontel Brown** raised approximately **$285,183 in contributions** and ended September with approximately **$1.20 million in cash**. This is a very safe Democrat seat.
* * *
## Follow the Money, Then Watch the Results
The biggest story in these reports is Ohio's 7th.
Poindexter raised nearly $2.5 million in contributions. Miller raised approximately $145,000 and put another million dollars of his own money into the campaign.
That is a substantial difference in the support flowing into their campaign accounts.
Across Ohio, the reports also show where resources are concentrating and where candidates are being left to compete with much less.
I will be talking more about these races as we get closer to Election Day. In the meantime, explore the [Ohio Congressional Campaign Finance Tracker](https://substack.com/redirect/d5c60b10-1503-4691-aa25-545757843456?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and take a look at the money behind the candidates asking for your vote.

Before we get into the numbers, take a look at my . You can compare candidates, explore their campaign finances, and see the outside money coming into these races. The latest financial reports have dropped. We are less than three weeks from the midterm elections, and while another reporting deadline is coming before Election Day, these third-quarter reports give us a substantial look at the money behind the campaigns. These numbers cover July through September, with cash balances as of September 30. And in Ohio's 7th District, Brian Poindexter absolutely crushed Max Miller in fundraising. | | ---|---|--- Ohio's 7th: Poindexter Raised Nearly 17 Times as Much | | ---|---|--- Brian Poindexter raised $2,461,285 in contributions during the third quarter. Max Miller raised $145,525. That is a difference of $2,315,760. Poindexter brought in nearly 17 times as much in contributions as Miller. Miller also loaned his campaign $1 million of his own money. That pushed his total receipts to approximately $1.15 million, but we need to be clear about what that means. A personal loan does not represent people opening their wallets to support your campaign. It represents you opening your own. And the change from the previous quarter is striking. Poindexter's contributions increased from approximately $466,000 to $2.46 million, a 428% increase. Miller's fell from approximately $405,000 to $146,000, a 64% decline. That is a dramatic shift in fundraising momentum. The cash position is also very different from what I initially thought. They did not end the quarter with roughly the same amount available, and Miller was not ahead. Poindexter ended September with $1,066,833 in cash. Miller had $122,835. That put Poindexter ahead by approximately $944,000. Miller spent heavily during the quarter, about $2.40 million , compared with Poindexter's $1.72 million. So Miller outspent him by approximately $688,000 while ending with substantially less money available. Miller's committee also reported approximately $1.965 million in debt. The fundraising gap is enormous. The question now is how that translates into votes. Small Contributions Tell Another Part of the Story Looking at where the money came from, there is an interesting difference between percentages and actual dollars. Among reported individual-contribution dollars, Miller received approximately $41,635 from unitemized contributions and itemized contribution entries of $200 or less. Poindexter received approximately $659,863 in that same category. That matters. A high small-contribution percentage can sound impressive until you look at the size of the fundraising base underneath it. Poindexter also received approximately $981,619 in individual contribution entries of $2,000 or more, representing 43.4% of his individual-contribution dollars. His fundraising surge included substantial money at both ends. These categories measure contribution amounts, rather than each donor's total giving. Somebody making repeated smaller contributions can ultimately give much more than $200. Who Gave to Miller and Poindexter? | | ---|---|--- Don Henley Welcome to the Hotel OH-7 There are some recognizable names in these reports. Selected individual contributions to Max Miller included: Daniel Loeb: $3,500. Founder and CEO of investment firm Third Point. The contribution was marked as earmarked through AIPAC. Gila Milstein: $3,500. Cofounder of the Adam and Gila Milstein Family Foundation. Her contribution was also marked as earmarked through AIPAC. Keith Mardak: $1,000. Former Hal Leonard music-publishing executive and philanthropist. Michelle Primm: $1,000. Cascade Auto Group managing partner and a National Automobile Dealers Association board member. Selected individual contributions to Brian Poindexter included: JB Pritzker: $3,500. The Illinois governor. Robert Rubin: $3,500. Former U.S. Treasury secretary. Penny Pritzker: $1,314.81. Former U.S. Commerce secretary. Allen Blue: $3,500 in technology services. The LinkedIn cofounder's contribution was reported as in-kind. Phoebe Gates: $3,500. Phia cofounder and daughter of Bill Gates. Mark Clein: $7,000 across two contributions. Cofounder of Precision Medicine Group. Roger Altman: $3,500. Founder of investment bank Evercore. Blair Effron: $3,500. Cofounder of investment bank Centerview Partners. Marta Kauffman: $3,500. Cocreator of Friends. Don Henley: $3,500. The Eagles musician. Bonnie Raitt: $1,000. The singer-songwriter. Those are individual contributions. Listing someone's business background does not mean the business itself donated. But the names show how much national attention this race is attracting. The Outside Money Is Pouring Into Ohio's 7th Then there is the money being spent outside the campaigns. These expenditures do not go into Miller's or Poindexter's campaign accounts. Outside organizations pay for their own advertising, canvassing, mail, and other activity supporting or opposing candidates. The latest identified notices include approximately: Congressional Leadership Fund: $2.24 million opposing Poindexter. This is a major House Republican outside-spending organization. Your Community PAC: $1.98 million opposing Miller. House Majority PAC: $1.60 million opposing Miller. A major organization working to elect House Democrats. Ready for the Fight: $1.47 million opposing Miller. JB Pritzker serves as its honorary chair. Jobs & Prosperity PAC: $580,712 opposing Poindexter and $116,337 supporting Miller. A pro-Miller super PAC whose disclosed funders include Brian Colleran, RMS Investment Group, and members of the Haslam family. Retired Americans Action: $177,424 opposing Miller. Stand Up for Ohio: $140,280 supporting Poindexter and $66,450 opposing Miller. Progressive Turnout Project: $138,753 supporting Poindexter. There are other notable interests involved, too. Elon Musk-backed America PAC reported approximately $64,029 opposing Poindexter and $17,654 supporting Miller. America First Agriculture Action , which has received cannabis-industry funding, reported approximately $54,895 opposing Poindexter and $51,502 supporting Miller. SEIU COPE reported approximately $14,688 supporting Poindexter and another $14,688 opposing Miller. Earlier processed spending also included approximately $570,204 supporting Poindexter from Jobs and Democracy PAC , associated with the Public First AI-policy network, and $198,019 from BDA PAC , Blue Dog Action's political committee. Both of those amounts reflected primary spending. That timing matters. Money spent to help someone win a primary should not be presented as though it all arrived for the general election. The recent notices remain provisional because amendments, estimated costs, and reporting issues still need reconciliation. I am not adding them together and calling the result a verified grand total. What is clear is that national party organizations, wealthy donors, labor, and industry interests are paying attention to Ohio's 7th. Where the Campaigns Are Spending The campaigns themselves are putting substantial money into advertising. Miller reported approximately $2.02 million to Strategic Media Placement for media buys. Poindexter reported approximately $1.02 million to LC Media for advertising and video production , plus approximately $275,516 to Kinetic Strategies for advertising and digital fundraising. Poindexter also reported approximately $81,109 to the Ohio Democratic Party for coordinated campaign, payroll-related, and administrative costs, along with $50,800 for polling. These are campaign expenditures, separate from the outside spending above. This is going to be a very interesting race. The fundraising momentum is clearly behind Poindexter, even in a district that has favored Republicans. His union background, the concentration of organized labor in Cuyahoga County, and Miller's high profile all help explain why this race is getting attention. Miller's messy divorce has also been part of the public conversation. That's why I am writing to you today. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I am the producer of the film Sound of Freedom and founder of the Sound of Freedom Foundation. Years ago, I learned what traffickers do to innocent children. It broke my heart. I knew I could not look away. I have said before: " When good people keep quiet or look away, they become part of the problem."I decided not to stay quiet or look away. Friend, I am asking you to join me. We have created a special pack of Carry the Number stickers printed with a rescue hotline number. When you make your first gift of any amount to the Sound of Freedom Foundation , we will send you a sticker pack so you can help put this important number into your community. Put one in your car. Share one with your church. Ask a local business to display one. Help make this number visible. Why? Because trafficking hides in darkness. A person may see something that does not seem right but not know where to turn. Someone in danger may desperately need a way to reach out. You can help someone in the grip of a trafficker who wants to break free. This 24/7 hotline provides real people waiting for that call. This visible hotline could facilitate a victim's safe and secure exit from the life of enslavement, and the next steps to begin a new life journey.All calls are 100% confidential. A child, teen, or young adult trapped in trafficking may be searching for a way out. Seeing that number could give them the courage to make one call -- a call that could be their first step toward freedom. Something as small as a sticker can carry such an important message. You are not alone. There is a number to call. There are people willing to act. That's also why I believe awareness must lead to action. The film Sound of Freedom brought the horror of child trafficking before millions of people. But a movie alone cannot end this evil. So we created the Sound of Freedom Foundation to carry this mission forward. We work to help prevent exploitation, support intervention efforts, educate parents and communities, spread information, and influence policies that protect children. And beneath everything we do is one truth I will never stop saying: GOD 'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE. Jesus said: " As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you. Now remain in my love." Make your first gift to the Sound of Freedom Foundation. Your generosity helps fuel our larger mission to protect vulnerable children and fight exploitation. Then I want you to do something important with it. Carry it. Share it. Put the number where it can be seen. Imagine thousands of ordinary people doing the same thing. Thousands of cars, churches, businesses, and community spaces carrying a simple message: We see these children. We will not be silent. And we will not surrender them to darkness. CARRY THE NUMBER. | | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth just announced that our military’s cyber forces – the U.S. Cyber Command – will work with the Department of Homeland Security to defend our elections from any foreign interference. But Trump has gutted critical election security infrastructure since he entered the White House – including the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) that was designed to ensure our elections are free, fair, and safe. _As one expert put it:_ | | | _**“If the administration was serious about assisting state and local election officials, they shouldn’t have dismantled all of the federal government’s election cybersecurity capacity and fired all their experts in early 2025.”** \- Former DOJ Attorney David Becker_
---|---|---
This is the same administration that has pushed countless conspiracy theories about our election system – that Trump won the 2020 election, that our elections are "rigged" against him and MAGA Republicans, and that there's widespread voter fraud.

### At this year's AUSA Annual Meeting, we got a firsthand look at how AI, autonomous weapons, and a new generation of defense startups are transforming America's military.

This week, my partner Genine Fallon and I joined more than 30,000 military leaders, veterans, policymakers, and defense industry executives in D.C. for the[ Association of the United States Army's (AUSA) Annual Meeting](https://substack.com/redirect/eead54e5-e461-467f-976c-18e195c064ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), one of the largest gatherings of the Army community anywhere in the world.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8cfd8a4a-84b0-4264-a401-4adfb848c0b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
As a former Under Secretary of the Army and longtime AUSA Senior Fellow, I've attended plenty of these gatherings over the years. But this one felt different. The technologies transforming modern warfare are advancing at a remarkable pace, and the Pentagon is under growing pressure to keep up.
Artificial intelligence and autonomous weapons dominated the conversation, alongside a surge of private investment in defense startups. The wars in Ukraine and Iran have already demonstrated how quickly the battlefield is changing. Meanwhile, China's military buildup has raised the stakes considerably. The undercurrent of 'Peace through Strength' was palpable.
We had a great time reconnecting with old friends and meeting some of the entrepreneurs helping shape the next generation of American defense capabilities.
Here are a few of our biggest takeaways.
## **1\. Autonomous Warfare Has Already Changed the Battlefield**
One of the biggest developments at AUSA was the announcement of a new Autonomous Warfare Command, designed to accelerate the military's adoption of drones, AI, and unmanned systems across the Armed Forces.
The wars in Ukraine and Iran have offered the example of how dramatically warfare is changing. Relatively inexpensive drones can now threaten weapons systems worth millions of dollars, forcing militaries to reconsider how they deploy their forces and defend against attacks. The United States can no longer assume that having the most expensive equipment on the battlefield guarantees technological superiority.
The Pentagon wants to produce autonomous systems at a scale that would have been difficult to imagine just a few years ago, while making it easier for emerging defense companies to get their technology into the hands of American troops.
America cannot continue fighting with outdated equipment while simply adding a few drones to existing formations.
## **2\. America 's Defense Industrial Base Needs to Move Faster**
Having the world's most advanced military means little if we cannot produce enough weapons when we need them.
That's a problem the Pentagon has been grappling with for years. While private companies can develop groundbreaking technology in a matter of months, the military can spend years approving contracts and getting equipment into production. In a major conflict, those delays could have serious consequences.
At AUSA, Army leaders discussed efforts to speed things up, particularly when it comes to missiles and ammunition. Lt. Gen. Frank Lozano explained that under the traditional system, it could take roughly six years to expand a factory's production capacity and deliver additional missiles. New agreements aim to cut that timeline significantly by giving manufacturers the confidence to invest in new facilities before orders are fulfilled.
Recent conflicts have shown how quickly even large stockpiles of expensive weapons can be depleted. And replacing a missile isn't as simple as placing another order when factories are already operating at capacity.
We cannot afford a defense industrial base that moves at the speed of bureaucracy while our adversaries move at the speed of innovation.
## **3\. Defense Startups Are Changing the Game**
For decades, a handful of major defense contractors have dominated the Pentagon's business. Breaking into that world as a smaller company with a promising new technology was notoriously difficult, even when that technology could save American lives.
Fortunately, that's beginning to change. A new generation of defense entrepreneurs are attracting billions in private investment and challenging the way our military develops and purchases equipment.
I've been actively involved in supporting this growing industry, including through my work with[ Applied Energetics](https://substack.com/redirect/560a4336-0e66-4a9e-949d-65a8c1d6dbd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), an American company developing ultrashort-pulse laser technology designed to disable the sensors that drones rely on to navigate and identify targets. It's the kind of innovation that could fundamentally change how we protect American troops.
At AUSA, Army leaders made clear that they want to make it easier for emerging companies to test their technologies and compete for Pentagon contracts.
I'm particularly encouraged by the veterans helping lead this transformation. Many know firsthand what soldiers need because they've been the ones on the battlefield, dealing with equipment that didn't work as promised or waiting for capabilities that arrived too late.
We should be doing everything we can to help these innovators succeed. Some of the most important breakthroughs in American defense may come from companies most Americans have never heard of.
## **4\. Technology Still Can 't Replace the American Soldier**
With so much attention on AI and autonomous weapons, it's easy to forget that wars are ultimately fought by people. And no matter how sophisticated our technology becomes, the American soldier remains our greatest advantage.
Acting Army Chief of Staff Gen. Christopher LaNeve - a Pittsburgh native and former 82nd Airborne Commander - made that point powerfully at AUSA, reminding attendees that no algorithm can replicate the moral courage required of a soldier in combat.
He's absolutely right.
A drone might be able to identify a target or carry out a mission without putting a pilot in harm's way. But it cannot replace the human judgment required to make life-or-death decisions in close quarters combat, or the leadership needed when a mission goes wrong.
Army leaders also discussed the enormous challenges of preparing for a potential conflict with China in the Pacific, where American forces could be operating thousands of miles from home. Getting equipment to the battlefield is one challenge. Keeping troops supplied and their equipment functioning under enemy fire is another.
I learned during my time in uniform that even the best equipment is only as effective as the people using it.
Our goal should be to give American soldiers every technological advantage possible, without forgetting that they are the reason we invest in these technologies in the first place.
**Pennsylvania Connection**
There are three ways to become a commissioned officer in the US Army: West Point, Officer Candidate School, and ROTC. ROTC commissions about 5K each year or 70% of our officers and has commissioned over 715K since it was founded. Fifteen were inducted this year into the US Army [ROTC Hall of Fame](https://substack.com/redirect/7101c5d3-7111-4e0f-b86c-c69409ba17a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including Pennsylvania's own Brigadier General (retired) Maureen Weigl, a University of Pittsburgh ROTC grad and most recently Governor Josh Shapiro's Deputy Adjutant General of Veterans Affairs. Her thirty-plus years overseas, in business and being the champion for the over 800K of our brother and sister veterans here in Pennsylvania is well known.
Another connection is Uniontown, Pennsylvania native five-star general and former Secretary of State George Marshall - widely known for implementing the 'Marshall Plan' under President Truman after serving as Secretary of War in WWII. He has been the only soldier ever to receive the Nobel Peace Prize. AUSA grants their highest honor each year - the Marshall Award - and this year it went to Tunnel to Towers Foundation founder Frank Siller, who, after losing his heroic FDNY brother Stephen on 9/11 in the North Tower, devoted his life to helping the families of our fallen community and country's heroes with mortgage-free homes. In his eloquent acceptance speech, without a dry eye in the room, he cited something we should all take to heart from the Bible: 'Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.' \- John 15:13 (KJV)

With Brig. Gen. (PA) Maureen Weigl

name: Chad Bianco
subject: I ask for your support
body:
Your support stops this.

| | | | | |
---
| |

Friends,
The Riverside County Board of Supervisors has created an ad hoc committee to study new oversight options for the Sheriff’s Department, led by Supervisors Jose Medina and Karen Spiegel.
**Whether you agree with this or not** , the voters don’t get to have a say. They are making that decision for you.
**My position is clear** : the department already operates under extensive accountability—budget oversight by the Board, state inspections, the District Attorney, the Department of Justice, and more, making this committee **unnecessary**.
**Far-left activists are once again pressuring the Board** to create extra roadblocks to public safety. This is the same fight we have seen in Los Angeles County. In 2016, they imposed an ad hoc committee that has since caused division among the community and the department, **wasted taxpayer dollars** , enriched a lot of consultants and produced no meaningful improvement to public safety.
---
| | | | | [Support Bianco](https://us.list-manage.com/X6OLO3A2SjC?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)
---
| |
**Voters elect the Sheriff**. They do not elect activist committees or outside special interests that want ongoing influence over the day-to-day law enforcement decisions that keep our communities safe. The county currently operates on a deficit worth tens of millions, yet **my department operates within budget** because I believe government should respect the people’s tax dollars.
**Oversight committees have normally been voted on by the people** , as seen in San Francisco County. I only wish the Board of Supervisors weren’t going around the voters of Riverside for their own political agenda.
Previous attacks on my record as Sheriff have been answered by a strong grassroots response from everyday people like you.**This is just another one**.
Thank you for standing with law enforcement and with the voters who elected me twice.

Sheriff Chad Bianco
Riverside County

clean_body: Your support stops this. | | | | | | | | Friends, The Riverside County Board of Supervisors has created an ad hoc committee to study new oversight options for the Sheriff’s Department, led by Supervisors Jose Medina and Karen Spiegel. Whether you agree with this or not , the voters don’t get to have a say. They are making that decision for you. My position is clear : the department already operates under extensive accountability—budget oversight by the Board, state inspections, the District Attorney, the Department of Justice, and more, making this committee unnecessary. Far-left activists are once again pressuring the Board to create extra roadblocks to public safety. This is the same fight we have seen in Los Angeles County. In 2016, they imposed an ad hoc committee that has since caused division among the community and the department, wasted taxpayer dollars , enriched a lot of consultants and produced no meaningful improvement to public safety. | | | | | | | Voters elect the Sheriff. They do not elect activist committees or outside special interests that want ongoing influence over the day-to-day law enforcement decisions that keep our communities safe. The county currently operates on a deficit worth tens of millions, yet my department operates within budget because I believe government should respect the people’s tax dollars. Oversight committees have normally been voted on by the people , as seen in San Francisco County. I only wish the Board of Supervisors weren’t going around the voters of Riverside for their own political agenda. Previous attacks on my record as Sheriff have been answered by a strong grassroots response from everyday people like you.This is just another one. Thank you for standing with law enforcement and with the voters who elected me twice.
