The Supreme
Court just handed Trump another win. And once again, not a single justice
signed the order.

Just weeks before the midterms, the justices stepped in to make it cheaper
for Republicans to flood the airwaves with political ads.

Here’s how. By law, broadcasters can’t charge candidates more than their
cheapest rate as an election nears. In March, Trump’s FCC extended that
discount to political parties whenever they team up with a candidate on an
ad.

Just this week, the Supreme Court justices shut down a lower court’s
attempt to make the FCC defend this rule before Election Day, saying
nothing forces the FCC onto a schedule. By the time anyone weighs in, the
votes will already be counted. And it’s the second time this fall the
Court has protected this scheme.^1

Now, cash-rich Republican party committees get to keep buying airtime at
bargain rates and wipe out the fundraising lead Democratic candidates have
built in swing races.

The Court keeps tilting the scales of power toward the GOP, corporate
interests, and billionaire donors. By enabling wealthy committees to
saturate the airwaves, this ruling threatens to silence voters and
overwhelm local campaign messaging.

It’s absurd, and it won’t fix itself. We have to end the dominance of this
Court’s corrupt majority, and that starts with electing leaders this
November who will rein it in.

"Do you believe that statement's misleading?"
"All the clauses in there are patently false. And I told them so."
So reads an exchange from the deposition of Joseph Weissman, an ExxonMobil scientist with the company's former algae biofuels program. The "patently false" statement in question was a corporate press release claiming algae biofuel was a viable solution to climate change that the company would soon be producing at scale. Extensive reporting has already uncovered how ExxonMobil spent nearly half as much [advertising](https://substack.com/redirect/8ae0c0c8-6620-4ae4-98d3-3ef3a2373f73?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its algae research as it [spent](https://substack.com/redirect/59827b62-61fd-4cd2-b23b-0258c0408436?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on the research itself. But testimony like Weissman's shows just how clearly the company understood that this much-touted project was, in Weissman's words, a "dead end." The goal was not to create a viable alternative energy source, but simply, as one internal memo put it, to make consumers "[b]elieve ExxonMobil is committed to helping solve climate change."
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=220702728&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIwNzAyNzI4LCJpYXQiOjE3OTIxNjQ1NjcsImV4cCI6MTc5NDc1NjU2NywiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0._pkZ5eLteGf2F2oXu3bnBHhA-bX-jjl6yC1ILgn6InQ)
Weissman's deposition was taken by the Massachusetts Attorney General's Office as part of its lawsuit against ExxonMobil alleging consumer protection violations. In an under-the-radar [filing](https://substack.com/redirect/ff47ca28-469c-4181-8f95-f4610e1989b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in April, Massachusetts disclosed this deposition, as well as a [range of other documents](https://substack.com/redirect/abeeca16-0023-4914-8ed9-9e49d03c6ad3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it had uncovered, to demonstrate the relevance of additional investigative targets that ExxonMobil had been furiously attempting to shield from discovery. These newly released materials cover a range of topics and time periods, from memos on the company's more recent deceptive advertising campaigns to evidence of its decades-old climate knowledge.
One of the documents is a 1992 paper, "Climate Change Impacts on Northern Offshore Petroleum Operations," which analyzes how Exxon's operations in the Beaufort Sea would be affected by its predictions of a "much thinner ice sheet" and other anticipated effects of global warming caused by the use of its products. The upshot for Exxon: "[I]f ice conditions become less severe as predicted, then offshore petroleum operations will become easier and less costly." Papers like this, demonstrating ExxonMobil's sophisticated understanding of the realities of global warming, were produced at the same time the company was ramping up its public efforts to, in its own [words](https://substack.com/redirect/a874bbaa-4255-407c-830c-35861505ffd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "emphasize the uncertainty in scientific conclusions" on climate change in order to resist the "development of nonfossil fuel resources."
Needless to say, the contrast between oil companies' internal climate knowledge and external climate denial is profoundly damaging to the industry. This helps explain why it is going to such extraordinary lengths to attack these climate cases. These corporations are not just afraid of losing these lawsuits; they're also afraid of the damning evidence the suits will uncover.
This is the skeleton key for understanding _[Suncor v. Boulder](https://substack.com/redirect/623dc8f0-3045-4759-9862-b41a6b788d44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , the high-profile climate case the Supreme Court heard in early October _._
_Suncor_ began in 2018, when Boulder, Colorado, sued fossil fuel companies Suncor and ExxonMobil for damages from climate change and the companies' lies about their role in fueling it. After the Colorado Supreme Court rejected the defendants' motion to dismiss the case, Suncor and ExxonMobil--likely terrified of what would happen if Boulder were allowed to have its day in court--asked the U.S. Supreme Court to intervene, repeating a request the fossil fuel industry has made [again](https://substack.com/redirect/112d9fdd-95c8-4cea-9e17-570f569503d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [again](https://substack.com/redirect/0c8560e9-536d-4020-819e-1f4da551cb20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in recent years, alongside parallel efforts to lobby [Congress](https://substack.com/redirect/32334a80-d256-4aea-9d6e-51f4393f15ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [state legislatures](https://substack.com/redirect/2d3006fa-9649-49cb-b559-a0ea1c534298?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to grant it immunity from all climate-related liability.
There is a reason why oil and gas companies are so desperate to stop these cases by any means before they proceed any further. We have likely seen just a sliver of the evidence they have that shows they've spent decades knowingly deceiving the public about climate science, climate harms, and their commitment to climate action. How many more reports are they sitting on like the 1992 paper laying out ExxonMobil's projected opportunities for profiting off a melting Arctic? How many more internal communications like Weissman's saying that "all the clauses" in a 2018 press release about ExxonMobil's signature climate solution were "patently false?" The current offensive isn't just about defeating the cases. It's also about preventing the public from learning the extent and severity of the industry's wrongdoing. It's about fossil fuel CEOs' profound fear of sitting in front of a jury of 12 Americans and trying to defend their companies' deceptive conduct--because they know it's indefensible.
Regardless of how the Supreme Court rules in _Suncor_ , it's hard to imagine these companies can bury the evidence of their lies and escape accountability indefinitely. Whatever the onetime value of fossil fuels to the economy, their harms now massively outweigh their benefits, particularly since the vast majority of fossil fuel use can be replaced by cleaner, cheaper, safer forms of energy--and this has been true for a long time. Instead of adapting, the industry has clung tightly to a civilization-endangering business model and engaged in a massive deception campaign to do so. Along the way, its conduct has become some of the most harmful and culpable in human history. Eventually, it will be held to account.

| | | | | For more than 50 years, something has been quietly eating away at the real-world value of the U.S. dollar.

Weiss Ratings calls it **“Project Pyramid.”**

It began in 1971, when Washington decoupled the dollar from gold.

Since then, the supply of U.S. dollars has exploded.

At the same time, the cost of housing, healthcare, education, energy and everyday life has climbed dramatically.

And according to Gavin Magor, a senior research analyst at Weiss Ratings, this isn’t some temporary problem that Washington can easily reverse.

America is carrying enormous levels of debt.

Foreign nations are reducing their dependence on the dollar.

And policymakers continue relying on the same monetary system that helped create the problem in the first place.

So what can ordinary investors do?

The answer isn’t simply to pile up more cash.

It’s to potentially grow your investment capital [faster than the dollar loses its real-world value.](https://links.dpt.deepregimetrends.com/u/click?_t=4a25883d9bf54436b571b8aa9717dcca&_m=60efc8eba9b142cb9e2fa8300be78243&_e=EyUAmFECiRhl6UBb1fM4ezVCODzE1c5ybWwFnicdgT_8bdcT4QtwkjFaiqIcgwE1MXl8S80r6wE375W3nR3pfQdD8rtsGoNAMDMXD6aj6VNsotFnMj85zjPEv4jXvhQ8dJMbAmAfIb4pMcvTfjHSioyQZUYZ-f8O7JtRPgEIf5S4k0_A_SoDVjwAC7cEc6Q8H1hCRrMzU6ME7n72k4qHlrX_PulRJGmUQaK2N1Z7t0LqKV4ShmtifUR-5mBQSnHByj-uDFSCcF1xnStkLHz_cKuoPq2PxYZEuvtWo2aNHx1Ho0IFSEK19G0DiyPjS_5-WXFJ60E4pHo00aDm4rdN2VWD4jmSlHiKLcpOOXoQQu3xasCCplqHMrjyyaHrNv9_7lP9znkXE93Kv9NvFO58UdyBy4Xx7JVkVkwBWQO0BH1O9eeEuEa0tdYNQr34rKfHqyityTVtnsem-80nynuivc5tcMqr3i4ekvtlgs3bdZRmLOc2HtyG6UDSL4tNgh45lVKz_DFsPJpFVH3HtrDF1deMnNZK47lH2O1NJKqzdzk%3D)

Case File No DRT-ED-LEAK · Special File · The Slow Leak
Your Savings Account Says the Same Number It Did Last Year. Your Money Doesn’t Buy the Same Things.
Since Washington cut the dollar’s last link to gold in 1971, a dollar has lost close to 90% of its buying power. The national debt just passed $40 trillion. Prices are still rising. The leak hasn’t stopped, and cash is the asset it drains first.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
The trick of cash is that the number never goes down. Your balance says $10,000 today, and it will say $10,000 next year. What changes is what that $10,000 can buy, and since 1971 the answer has been: less and less, every single year.
The evidence board
| | Fifty-Five Years of the Same Story
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — 1971.** On a Sunday night in August, President Nixon cut the dollar’s last link to gold. It was announced as temporary. It was never reversed.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — your dollar.** Based on consumer prices, $1 from 1971 buys about what 12 cents did then. Prices have risen more than eightfold.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the debt.** On October 8, U.S. public debt hit a record of about $40.3 trillion, according to Treasury data.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit D — the rest of the world.** The dollar’s share of global central bank reserves fell from about 71% around 2000 to 57% in early 2026, according to the IMF.
| OUR THEORY
---
A government carrying $40 trillion in debt has every reason to let the dollar slowly lose value, because it makes that debt easier to carry. That’s not a conspiracy theory. It’s arithmetic. The cost lands on savers, retirees and anyone whose money sits still.
Why it matters to you
| | What Savers Get Wrong
---|---
| →| **Cash feels safe, but isn’t.** It’s the asset most guaranteed to lose buying power over time.
---|---
| →| **The problem isn’t temporary.** The forces behind it are bigger than ever: record debt, foreign buyers stepping back.
---|---
| →| **Retirement plans need rethinking.** The goal is growth that outpaces the dollar’s decline, not just a bigger balance.
---|---
| ClassificationOngoing
---
The forces that have been eating away at the dollar since 1971 haven’t gone away. They’re getting bigger. Waiting for Washington to fix it has never worked.

subject: You came through yesterday — two ways to help today
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Committee to Elect Enoch, Catherine Johnson, Treasurer
body:
| | | | | |
---
| | | | |

| | Hello Peter,
I have to start by saying thank you.
Yesterday, we asked for your help funding our digital ads and our text campaign, and you stepped up to the plate in a big way. Because of you, our message is reaching voters across Ohio's 8th District on their phones, in their feeds, and in their pockets. That is what a people-powered campaign looks like, and I am so grateful to be in this fight with you.
Today, I need to ask for one more push, and there are two ways you can help.
1\. Help us order our Election Day signs.
We have to place our yard sign order today. Sign printers need time to produce and ship, and if we wait even a few more days, we risk our signs arriving after voters have already made up their minds. Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, just 18 days away, and every yard, every corner, and every polling place without a sign is a missed chance to remind our neighbors that real change is on the ballot.
[Can you chip in $25 / $50 / $100 right now so we can place our order today?](https://us.list-manage.com/SFMHtL2ZD5h?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
---
| [Help us buy yard signs today!](https://us.list-manage.com/zn415cq9GhS?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
---
| |
2\. Help us put stamps on our postcards.
Our volunteers have been writing personal postcards to voters across the district, and those handwritten notes are some of the most powerful outreach we do. Now they need stamps to get in the mail.
You can help in whichever way works best for you:
• Donate a roll of Forever stamps. You can call the Campaign at 513-275-9724, and we can arrange to pick them up.• Give online and we'll buy the stamps for you. Just give at [https://enochforcongress.com/donate-now](https://us.list-manage.com/12aXn3TCrDv?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8) and note "stamps" if you'd like. A roll of stamps are $65. Two rolls are $130. We need thousands.
---
| | | | | [Donate $ for Stamps Now](https://us.list-manage.com/EyN74F46QRu?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
---
| |

You have already shown what this community can do when we come together. Let's finish strong.
With deep gratitude and hope,Dr.Vanessa Enoch
Democratic Candidate for Congress, Ohio's 8th District
P.S. Our sign order has to go in today to guarantee delivery before Election Day, and our postcards will ready to go as soon as they have stamps. Whether you give a few dollars or a roll of stamps, you'll help us reach thousands of voters.
Paid for by Committee to Elect Enoch, Catherine Johnson, Treasurer

**Friday, October 16, 2026 -**_****_
_**Yemen** : Ansarallah attack on presidential palace in Aden kills five, wounds 16. Saudi-led attacks kill at least 107, wound 278 across Yemen since September 3, 2026. UN Security Council condemns Ansarallah attacks on Saudi Arabia, demands cessation of Yemen hostilities._
_**Palestine** : Israeli attacks kill one Palestinian, wound five in Gaza. Israeli settlers tear through Palestinian olive groves, assault Washington Post journalist amid widespread attacks near Ramallah. Israeli settlers attack Palestinian olive harvesters across other areas of the occupied West Bank, injuring three. Record-breaking 200+ Israeli settler attacks on Palestinian olive harvest in West Bank, UN says. Israeli advertising firm helped place "zero-click" spyware on Al Jazeera devices._
_**Iran** : Iranian president accuses U.S. and Israel of "ecocide." Iranian navy reports oil tanker on fire after entering "restricted" waters near Hormuz. Bloomberg: Pentagon to delay report on Iran school bombing until after midterms._
_**Lebanon:** Israeli forces strike residential building, school, and religious seminary across southern Lebanon amid "ceasefire."_
_**U.S.** : Teen gunman kills four, including three children, at Oregon elementary school. President Donald Trump cancels livestream of firing-squad execution, reversing War Secretary Pete Hegseth. AOC gives $1 million to El-Sayed's Senate campaign._ _Democratic senators move to block U.S.-Saudi nuclear cooperation deal. Trump officials reviewed Rep. Ilhan Omar 's immigration file in 2019 and found no citizenship issues. DOJ sues California and LA County officials to stop counting ballots of 20,000+ alleged noncitizens. Rep. Andy Harris threatens reporter with prosecution for recording him after Maryland debate._
_**International:** Reuters: White House gave the order to limit Ukraine's SpaceX satellite access. Philippines rebukes Chinese ambassador over "thinly veiled threat." Poland scrambles jets as Russian strikes hit western Ukraine; Bulgaria asks NATO for military support. Ebola spreads to Congolese province bordering Central African Republic. Ethiopian forces deepen control over Tigray. Ethiopian PM announces temporary government for Tigray, promises election. Somalia announces 2027 elections. Two Syrian pipelines damaged; one attributed to sabotage. U.S. discussing "denuclearization" with Russia and China, Trump says. French police accused of excessive violence against youth protesters in multiple cases. El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele announces plan to release detainees._

* * *
# Yemen
* **Ansarallah attack on presidential palace in Aden kills five, wounds 16:** Five people were killed and 16 wounded Thursday in a missile and drone attack on the Al-Maashiq presidential palace complex of Yemen's Saudi-backed government in Aden, according to Yemeni officials.
* The casualties included guards and civilian employees, while Prime Minister Shaya Al-Zindani and cabinet members were unharmed.
* Ansarallah, which claimed responsibility for the attack, said it had targeted a Saudi military headquarters in Aden as part of its campaign against Saudi military reinforcements.
* **Saudi-led attacks kill at least 107, wound 278 across Yemen since September 3:** At least 107 people have been killed and 278 wounded in Saudi-led [attacks](https://substack.com/redirect/618828a7-d8d8-4c84-8931-29bd1f182aff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) across Yemen since September 3, according to the health ministry in Sana'a. Women and children account for more than 60% of casualties.
* Between October 3 and October 12, the death toll rose from 72 to 107, with Taiz, Saada and Al-Jawf the hardest-hit of 13 affected governorates.
* **UN Security Council condemns Ansarallah attacks on Saudi Arabia, demands cessation of Yemen hostilities:** The UN Security Council condemned Ansarallah's escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia in a presidential [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/fed7ef98-1104-4d00-975b-ca782c8ef667?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday, pointing to strikes on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and attacks on other airports and Saudi Aramco facilities. The Council also affirmed Saudi Arabia's "right to self-defense."
* Ansarallah must "immediately cease their military escalation and their attacks impacting civilians and civilian objects," the Council said, reiterating its support for a negotiated, inclusive, Yemeni-led political settlement. Saudi Arabia welcomed the statement, while calling for international cooperation to prevent Ansarallah from obtaining weapons and other forms of support.

# Palestine
* **Israeli attacks kill one Palestinian, wound five in Gaza:** One Palestinian [died](https://substack.com/redirect/49461f47-6c50-44f9-ae2b-b8ea7dd82f22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Friday after sustaining injuries in an Israeli attack on the Sheikh Radwan neighborhood of Gaza City Thursday night, according to WAFA. Five others were injured in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip.
* Israeli forces continued shelling and gunfire across the Strip. In Shujaiya and eastern Gaza City, forces detonated explosive-laden robots to destroy remaining homes.
* **Israeli settlers tear through Palestinian olive groves, assault Washington Post journalist amid widespread attacks near Ramallah:** Israeli settlers severely beat Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine, 63, during widespread attacks on Palestinian olive harvesters across villages east and north of Ramallah on Friday.
* The attacks left numerous Palestinians injured, including one shot with live ammunition, while settlers burned vehicles and olive trees, stole crops, and forced farmers off their land.
* Israeli soldiers also fired live ammunition and tear gas, causing dozens of cases of suffocation, according to the Palestinian Red Crescent.
* Levine suffered fractures and wounds after settlers repeatedly clubbed and kicked her, dragged her across the ground, and stole her equipment, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/4ce52605-d4bf-4470-8ea7-54f57e1f0671?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to journalist Jasper Nathaniel. Footage of the attack captured by journalist Andrey X can be seen **[here](https://substack.com/redirect/c607aa96-ef16-4fc1-9917-925dbf813c62?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
* Levine was hospitalized in Ramallah following the assault. "I don't understand how parents can raise such monsters," she said. "Yes, they are Jewish terrorists, and they're giving everyone in this country [Israel] a horrible reputation... And they won't be prosecuted. I'm sure of it."
* The Washington Post condemned the attack on its photographer. "She was wearing visible markings clearly identifying her as a journalist," the Post said in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/372399c4-134d-4da2-ae54-72fae05b231d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "We are outraged by this unwarranted attack on a journalist doing her job," it added, calling for "a thorough investigation and follow-through from authorities."
* Elsewhere, settlers attacked olive harvesters in Turmus Ayya, northeast of Ramallah, burning vehicles and olive trees, and injuring a Civil Defense volunteer, while Israeli forces fired tear gas.
* Four Palestinians were injured in Burqa and three in Deir Jarir, where Israeli forces also restricted access to farmland. Near Birzeit and Burham, a 70-year-old man suffered fractures and after being beaten by settlers.
* **Israeli settlers attack Palestinian olive harvesters across other areas of the occupied West Bank, injuring three:**
* **Nablus:** Three Palestinians were [injured](https://substack.com/redirect/400db8c8-6264-4fe6-ac50-6bba98d70cf7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after settlers assaulted them while harvesting olives in Asira Al-Qibliya on Friday, WAFA reported. Settlers also stole olives from farmland in Aqraba and Al-Lubban Al-Sharqiya, where Israeli soldiers separately expelled farmers and confiscated their harvest.
* **Salfit:** Settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/7b982908-12ce-4d55-87ad-25dbe0a9a2ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) olive harvesters west of Deir Ballut and seized a farmer's vehicle key. Israeli forces subsequently ordered farmers to leave their land, threatening to shoot them if they returned.
* **Jenin:** Israeli forces and settlers [forced](https://substack.com/redirect/0a23c0ea-89e3-45c0-abfb-a8d2260329e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) farmers off their land in Jalbun, east of Jenin. Settlers also fired live ammunition and threw stun grenades toward homes.

* **Record-breaking 200+ Israeli settler attacks on Palestinian olive harvest in West Bank, UN says:** Israeli settlers [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/a311b313-e36d-47d6-ba1f-92ac36710f4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more than 200 attacks against Palestinians during the current olive harvest season in the occupied West Bank, surpassing the 185 recorded in the 2025 season, the UN said Thursday. Approximately 80% of incidents have occurred over the past two weeks.
* The attacks have killed at least four Palestinians since the harvest began, the Associated Press [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/b940ecb3-bb6b-4b99-acc2-0ccdd48f4476?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). More than 120 others have been wounded in the attacks, which have damaged over 2,500 olive trees and saplings.
* **Israeli advertising firm helped place "zero-click" spyware on Al Jazeera devices:** Israeli advertising technology company Discover-Tech helped place sophisticated spyware on dozens of devices used by Al Jazeera and other companies, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/8ee5cbb8-02bb-41d4-8ca9-b18d921158c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to an investigation by The Citizen Lab, a research unit at the University of Toronto.
* Spyware from Israeli firm Candiru was planted on journalists' devices using the first-known instance of "zero-click" targeted advertising, according to the Citizen Lab investigation, which was prompted by an internal Al Jazeera probe.
* The spyware collects a wide range of data: files, documents, and browser data like cookies, bookmarks, and saved credentials. It also captures keystrokes, takes screenshots, records microphone and webcam input, and extracts emails and messages from popular communication platforms.
* Some of the Israeli spyware-ads were also discovered in critical networks used by the Pentagon, the United Nations International Atomic Energy Agency, and the International Criminal Court, Al Jazeera said, citing a [report](https://substack.com/redirect/e8034cc1-ecc1-4198-8b19-3332b20b1fd8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by security firm Confiant.

# Iran
* **Iranian president accuses U.S. and Israel of "ecocide": **U.S. and Israeli military campaigns in Iran and Gaza have caused widespread environmental destruction that amounts to "ecocide or environmental genocide," President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Friday, during an address at the COP17 biodiversity summit in Armenia..
* Widespread U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iranian fuel storage facilities and related infrastructure have contaminated soil and water, Pezeshkian said,warning that the deterioration of Iran's ecosystems could persist for decades. As for Israel's obliteration of Gaza, he added, it "stands as a stark testament to ecocide, with devastation whose horrific impacts will endure for generations."
* He called for international mechanisms to assess environmental damage, fund ecosystem restoration, and ensure that countries subjected to war and sanctions do not bear the recovery costs alone.
* **Iranian navy reports oil tanker on fire after entering "restricted" waters near Hormuz: **An oil tanker caught fire in a "restricted" area of the Sea of Oman after reportedly switching off its tracking systems and attempting to cross a prohibited route, Iran's navy said Friday.
* The cause of the fire and the condition of the crew were not immediately clear.
* **Bloomberg:** **Pentagon to delay report on Iran school bombing until after midterms:** Senior Pentagon officials intend to delay the release of an internal report into the bombing of a school in southern Iran on the first day of the war until after the U.S. midterm elections, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/5c85c9ca-7521-486f-95c1-5a268926a8f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Bloomberg.
* The U.S. bombing of the Shajareh Tayyebeh school in Minab on February 28 killed at least 156 people, including 120 children and 26 teachers, in one of the single worst massacres committed by the U.S. government since the Vietnam War.
* Several of War Secretary Pete Hegseth's advisers conveyed to Pentagon personnel the plan to delay publication of the report, according to Bloomberg.
* New York Senator Kirsten Gillibrand said in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/2793ca7c-2fb8-4c30-9e29-4f3f6b0b9773?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "Withholding this report until after the election is not only disgraceful, it is cowardly. We have waited months--release the report. Congress and the American people deserve full transparency and accountability around this attack."
* **Read Drop Site 's in-depth investigation into the Minab school bombing [here](https://substack.com/redirect/d586f0aa-9821-4491-ac2c-1489be5fafcb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* **U.S. sanctions Iraqi bank and 26 individuals, entities over Iran ties:** On Thursday, the U.S. [imposed](https://substack.com/redirect/e37d444c-c380-4b9e-adda-7669248e7aab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) sanctions on the Iraq Development Bank, nine other entities, and 16 individuals over alleged financial ties to Iran, as part of the Trump administration's "Economic Outcast" campaign that aims to sever Tehran's remaining economic lifelines.
* The Treasury Department accused the bank, which Iraq barred from U.S. dollar transactions in 2024, of exploiting Iraq's former dollar auction system and maintaining ties to Iranian government entities and Iran-aligned militias.
* Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent [said](https://substack.com/redirect/bcbd7de0-0530-4b22-bd58-9d43eeac0cda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the department "will not relent until the Iranian regime's coffers are empty." He added, "the noose is tightening around Iran's economy, and not even Iran's so-called allies can save it."
* **Reuters: Iran conducted precision strikes on critical infrastructure in Gulf Arab countries:** Iran's precision strikes on critical infrastructure in the Persian Gulf during the war included at least 135 drone and missile attacks on at least 84 infrastructure sites across seven countries--Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Iraq, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, and Bahrain--according to a Reuters [investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/b9ec7a60-9ca6-48ef-9310-9d258aec41e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* Despite Gulf governments' repeated statements that the damage was the result of falling debris from intercepted Iranian missiles or drones, Reuters found that the Iranian strikes were in fact pinpoint attacks on critical equipment.
* Some of the targets were hidden beneath rooftops and sunshades, and invisible to space satellites. Two Gulf officials and one Iranian official told Reuters that Iran relied on networks of informants to conduct the attacks.
* After reviewing Reuters' findings, Ryan Stevens, a former U.S. Marine Corps special operations airstrike coordinator, said Iran's strikes showed "precision, targeting expertise, and patience."

# Lebanon
* **Israeli forces strike residential building, school, religious seminary across southern Lebanon amid "ceasefire":**
* **Nabatieh:** An Israeli quadcopter [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/80755a8c-9e0b-4138-b378-b686c05ed40b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two missiles at the roof of an inhabited residential building in Mefdoun, with the first failing to explode, on Friday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Emergency crews evacuated residents before the second strike, and no injuries were reported.
* Israeli forces also carried out two large, simultaneous explosions near a school in Kfar Tebnit and in Zawtar Al-Sharqiya at dawn.
* **Bint Jbeil:** An Israeli tank [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/eaad5e25-b60e-4fa4-9861-50fa9f3010ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a shell directly at a religious seminary building on the outskirts of Aita Al-Jabal.
* **Tyre (Sour):** Israeli warplanes [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/78099ab7-cb0b-4890-9657-506aea3e0319?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an airstrike on Mansouri.

# U.S. News
* **Teen gunman kills four, including three children, at Oregon elementary school:** A 16-year-old [opened](https://substack.com/redirect/9ed6296d-3d0e-4fe7-b6c7-34b765c1596b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) fire Thursday at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, killing four children aged 5, 8 and 11, and one teacher, police said. A 7-year-old student and a 54-year-old teacher were hospitalized in critical condition. The shooter entered by firing through locked doors. An armed community member who saw him enter pursued him into the school and killed him, according to Gov. **Tina Kotek,** who**** thanked that individual for "heroically" intervening to stop further loss of life. Police have not made the identity of the shooter public, nor have they identified the community member.
* **Trump cancels livestream of firing-squad execution, reversing Hegseth:** Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/12146917-2fd7-4bd8-b2f5-fe0da199523b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday on Truth Social that the government will not stream Fort Hood shooter **Nidal Hasan 's** Dec. 3 execution, canceling the plan War Secretary **Pete Hegseth** announced last week. Trump said streaming "might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan," but that "many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device." He said Hasan "will die, as scheduled, by firing squad," and that family members of his victims will be able to view it in person.
* **AOC gives $1 million to El-Sayed 's Senate campaign: **On Friday, Rep. **Alexandria** **Ocasio-Cortez**(D-NY) transferred $1 million to the Senate campaign of Dr. **Abdul** **El-Syed** , the Democratic candidate in Michigan, the New York Times [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/615f4af4-3695-4c7c-ab93-5b61f18eee70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "I'm not waking up on November 4th wishing I did more to combat the smears aimed at Abdul," Ocasio-Cortez said in a statement to the Times. "I'm leaving everything I can on the field."
* Ocasio-Cortez, one of the most influential Democrats in the country, joined El-Syed at campaign events across northern Michigan on Thursday. On Friday, she will hold her own rallies in the Detroit area.
* **Democratic senators move to block U.S.-Saudi nuclear cooperation deal:** Sens. **Jeff Merkley** of Oregon and **Edward Markey** of Massachusetts [filed](https://substack.com/redirect/beba7a87-9dd6-4014-a0ce-83b368865f5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a resolution Thursday that would block the U.S.-Saudi "123 agreement," invoking the Atomic Energy Act as their justification. The resolution will force a debate and a vote when lawmakers return next month. Both chambers would have to adopt it to block the deal, and it faces steep odds in the Republican-controlled House.
* **Trump officials reviewed Omar 's immigration file in 2019 and found no citizenship issues**: A political appointee in the first Trump administration [asked](https://substack.com/redirect/863470a7-8f03-42a4-a373-e16ec668ec0d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) immigration authorities in 2019 to review Rep. **Ilhan Omar 's** records for fraud, three former officials told the Washington Post. Career staffers found it highly unusual. Homeland Security Investigations concluded there was insufficient evidence of wrongdoing and dropped the idea of a full investigation. A USCIS officer's one-page memo, printed and hand-delivered because of its sensitivity, found no issues. USCIS said then it couldn't determine her age reliably because refugees often lack birth records, and examined her father's file without finding problems.
* The marriage allegations were also reviewed: her former husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, withdrew a green card application after USCIS asked for more evidence. One former official said, "I think her citizenship is solid and there wasn't any fraud there."
* **DOJ sues California and LA County officials to stop counting ballots of 20,000+ alleged noncitizens:** The Justice Department [sued](https://substack.com/redirect/8a957fee-eba5-41a6-9e40-44c817e2409e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) California Secretary of State **Shirley Weber** , Los Angeles County Registrar **Dean Logan ,** and the state on Thursday, asking a federal judge to block officials from counting ballots of voters it identified until their citizenship is verified. It claims officials plan to count ballots from more than 20,000 alleged noncitizens. The suit followed a Tuesday letter by Deputy Attorney General **R. Trent McCotter** demanding that Logan agree within 48 hours. Logan replied that he hadn't opened a thumb drive containing the names of the alleged noncitizens because doing so would violate privacy and data-security protocols, and that canceling registrations requires verifiable information, "not assertions of unconfirmed data matching."
* **Rep. Andy Harris threatens reporter with prosecution for recording him after Maryland debate:** Maryland Republican Rep. **Andy Harris** [told](https://substack.com/redirect/d73a5dbb-d0cb-470d-84ef-7e10287a852b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a reporter Tuesday, "You do not have my permission to record. If you record, we will refer you to prosecutors," in a gaggle after his debate with Democrat **Dan Schwartz** in Cambridge, Maryland, according to video shot by a Baltimore Banner photojournalist. The reporter, **Cat Murphy** of Capital News Service, said, "Everyone in here is recording. Why am I not allowed to?" Harris cited Maryland's all-party consent wiretapping law, which carries up to five years in prison and a $10,000 fine. He then called for an officer and left the room without waiting for one. The video shows at least eight journalists in the gaggle. Murphy said she is credentialed through a Capitol gallery and that the debate required no press registration.

# Other International News
* **Reuters: White House gave the order to limit Ukraine 's SpaceX satellite access:** An order to impose limitations on Ukraine's access to SpaceX's Starshield service, used for navigation by Ukrainian drones, came from inside the White House, Reuters [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/84612be5-cf91-44aa-9852-88878f2ff163?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The sudden outage disrupted Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia as well as defensive interceptors used to shoot down Russian drones Ukrainian officials said. The outage came as President Donald Trump was pressuring Ukraine to limit its strikes on Russian refineries.
* **Philippines rebukes Chinese ambassador over "thinly veiled threat":** The Philippines rebuked the Chinese ambassador Jing Quan for saying China could "easily win" a confrontation with the Philippines, Reuters [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/780363f6-ee4b-4644-9239-ea389eb11b57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Quan, who added that China would not use force because "we love peace," was responding to the Philippines defense secretary's remark that China is a "troublemaker," The Beijing envoy's comments "very much sound like a threat," said Philippines President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
* **Poland scrambles jets as Russian strikes hit western Ukraine; Bulgaria asks NATO for military support:** Poland's armed forces [scrambled](https://substack.com/redirect/ea3d7c64-07e0-4270-82a0-b4d0777c4ac1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) fighter jets during overnight Russian attacks near the Polish border of Ukraine. No airspace violation was recorded. The Russian strikes injured two people and cut power to 370,000 others, the Volyn Oblast governor said.
* A Russian drone attack killed three people and injured five others in Kharkiv. Strikes in Uman injured several people..
* Also on Friday, Ukrainian attacks killed two people in Russian-occupied Luhansk, according to . Russian authorities In Russia, air defenses blocked a Ukrainian drone attack on a heating plant in the Vladimir region, officials said.
* **Ebola spreads to Congolese province bordering Central African Republic:** The Ebola outbreak has [reached](https://substack.com/redirect/1aa29117-cf19-4d9c-bfa9-1f9f9a9a7caa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an eighth province of the Democratic Republic of Congo, where two cases have been confirmed, Reuters reported. The province, North Ubangi, borders the Central African Republic, which has not yet recorded a case. The outbreak is the second-largest on record, with more than 9,000 confirmed cases and over 4,000 deaths.
* **Ethiopian forces deepen control over Tigray:** Ethiopian forces [extended](https://substack.com/redirect/4c95c53b-9a65-4231-bd5f-bf725e3e2981?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their control of Tigray, entering the historic city of Aksum, while rival Tigrayan fighters remain in mountains surrounding the city. Eritrean troops retreated toward the border after sustaining significant casualties, according to a spokesperson with the Ethiopia-aligned militia Tigray Peace Force. Eritrea's Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel denied the claims.
* **Ethiopian PM announces temporary government for Tigray, promises election:** Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed [appointed](https://substack.com/redirect/46820756-de42-4354-8722-f9a5af3d3979?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a temporary administration for northern Tigray and announced elections would be held within six months, Reuters reported. Tigray's ruling party, the Tigray People's Liberation Front, led an offensive last month against Abiy's government, reigniting a war that killed hundreds of thousands of people from 2020 to 2022 Ethiopian forces have since taken control of large portions of Tigray, including the capital city of Mekelle.
* **Somalia announces 2027 elections:** Elections for both chambers of parliament will be held April 15, 2027, followed by a May 15 presidential vote, Abdikarim Ahmed Hassan, head of Somalia's Independent National Elections and Boundaries Commission, [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/c686ec47-e200-4f5f-a4b1-2d39036d21c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday. The ruling President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term, which began in 2022, ended earlier this year, but his government declared a "transition period," despite an agreement with the opposition to hold elections.
* **Two Syrian pipelines damaged; one attributed to sabotage:** A gas pipeline in the southern Syrian province of Hasakah was struck and exploded on Thursday, the state-owned Syrian Petroleum Company [said,](https://substack.com/redirect/b28c418f-41db-4d70-9da8-bd20325fae26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) The company called it a "sabotage attack." Separately, a fuel leak was reported in the Baniyas-Homs oil pipeline. The leak is suspected to be the result of an attempted theft, according to state media.
* **U.S. discussing "denuclearization" with Russia and China, Trump says: **The U.S. has engaged Russia and China in "denuclearization" talks," Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/218ca307-129d-4667-a166-efc6d75b2d18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday. The U.S. and Russia each possess about 4,000 nuclear warheads. China possesses about 620 warheads, but is expected to "catch up" within years, Trump said. "The whole thing is a shame because I'd love to denuclearise if possible," he added.
* **French police accused of excessive violence against youth protesters in multiple cases:** Police in France have launched internal investigations into 36 allegations of officer violence against demonstrators, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/da33bf33-49a7-48f8-96d8-e109fb2aac06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the interior minister, Laurent Nuñez.
* The accusations include four children allegedly being "mutilated" by explosive weapons, such as stun grenades, and six sustaining "significant injuries," as well as other complaints, including physical beatings and sexual assault.
* An unprecedented number of children have been arrested since the protests began in mid-September, with a total of 6,773 children under 18 taken into police custody, according to the justice ministry.
* France is in the fourth week of its biggest youth protest movement in decades, launched by high school students demonstrating for better conditions and the replacement of absent teachers.
* **El Salvador 's Bukele announces plan to release detainees: **El Salvador's Nayib Bukele unexpectedly announced plans to [potentially release](https://substack.com/redirect/2c13f204-9804-4f47-96f4-7fc981282a9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) up to 50% of the more than 93,000 detained under El Salvador's state of exception, framing the proposal as an amnesty for those accused of a lesser degree of "collaboration" with the country's gangs. Bukele made the surprise announcement only after a journalist interrupted a carefully managed press conference to ask about comments made by the president's brother, Ibrajim Bukele, about a commission to review cases. Bukele also floated the possibility of eventually lifting the state of exception, which has been in effect since March 27, 2022 and has been extended 55 times.

This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Yemen Ansarallah attack on presidential palace in Aden kills five, wounds 16: Five people were killed and 16 wounded Thursday in a missile and drone attack on the Al-Maashiq presidential palace complex of Yemen's Saudi-backed government in Aden, according to Yemeni officials. The casualties included guards and civilian employees, while Prime Minister Shaya Al-Zindani and cabinet members were unharmed. Ansarallah, which claimed responsibility for the attack, said it had targeted a Saudi military headquarters in Aden as part of its campaign against Saudi military reinforcements. Saudi-led attacks kill at least 107, wound 278 across Yemen since September 3: At least 107 people have been killed and 278 wounded in Saudi-led across Yemen since September 3, according to the health ministry in Sana'a. Women and children account for more than 60% of casualties. Between October 3 and October 12, the death toll rose from 72 to 107, with Taiz, Saada and Al-Jawf the hardest-hit of 13 affected governorates. UN Security Council condemns Ansarallah attacks on Saudi Arabia, demands cessation of Yemen hostilities: The UN Security Council condemned Ansarallah's escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia in a presidential Thursday, pointing to strikes on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and attacks on other airports and Saudi Aramco facilities. The Council also affirmed Saudi Arabia's "right to self-defense." Ansarallah must "immediately cease their military escalation and their attacks impacting civilians and civilian objects," the Council said, reiterating its support for a negotiated, inclusive, Yemeni-led political settlement. Saudi Arabia welcomed the statement, while calling for international cooperation to prevent Ansarallah from obtaining weapons and other forms of support. Palestine Israeli attacks kill one Palestinian, wound five in Gaza: One Palestinian Friday after sustaining injuries in an Israeli attack on the Sheikh Radwan neighborhood of Gaza City Thursday night, according to WAFA. Five others were injured in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip. Israeli forces continued shelling and gunfire across the Strip. In Shujaiya and eastern Gaza City, forces detonated explosive-laden robots to destroy remaining homes. Israeli settlers tear through Palestinian olive groves, assault Washington Post journalist amid widespread attacks near Ramallah: Israeli settlers severely beat Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine, 63, during widespread attacks on Palestinian olive harvesters across villages east and north of Ramallah on Friday. The attacks left numerous Palestinians injured, including one shot with live ammunition, while settlers burned vehicles and olive trees, stole crops, and forced farmers off their land. Israeli soldiers also fired live ammunition and tear gas, causing dozens of cases of suffocation, according to the Palestinian Red Crescent. Levine suffered fractures and wounds after settlers repeatedly clubbed and kicked her, dragged her across the ground, and stole her equipment, to journalist Jasper Nathaniel. Footage of the attack captured by journalist Andrey X can be seen . Levine was hospitalized in Ramallah following the assault. "I don't understand how parents can raise such monsters," she said. "Yes, they are Jewish terrorists, and they're giving everyone in this country [Israel] a horrible reputation... And they won't be prosecuted. I'm sure of it." The Washington Post condemned the attack on its photographer. "She was wearing visible markings clearly identifying her as a journalist," the Post said in a . "We are outraged by this unwarranted attack on a journalist doing her job," it added, calling for "a thorough investigation and follow-through from authorities." Elsewhere, settlers attacked olive harvesters in Turmus Ayya, northeast of Ramallah, burning vehicles and olive trees, and injuring a Civil Defense volunteer, while Israeli forces fired tear gas. Four Palestinians were injured in Burqa and three in Deir Jarir, where Israeli forces also restricted access to farmland. Near Birzeit and Burham, a 70-year-old man suffered fractures and after being beaten by settlers. Israeli settlers attack Palestinian olive harvesters across other areas of the occupied West Bank, injuring three: Nablus: Three Palestinians were after settlers assaulted them while harvesting olives in Asira Al-Qibliya on Friday, WAFA reported. Settlers also stole olives from farmland in Aqraba and Al-Lubban Al-Sharqiya, where Israeli soldiers separately expelled farmers and confiscated their harvest. Salfit: Settlers olive harvesters west of Deir Ballut and seized a farmer's vehicle key. Israeli forces subsequently ordered farmers to leave their land, threatening to shoot them if they returned. Jenin: Israeli forces and settlers farmers off their land in Jalbun, east of Jenin. Settlers also fired live ammunition and threw stun grenades toward homes. Record-breaking 200+ Israeli settler attacks on Palestinian olive harvest in West Bank, UN says: Israeli settlers more than 200 attacks against Palestinians during the current olive harvest season in the occupied West Bank, surpassing the 185 recorded in the 2025 season, the UN said Thursday. Approximately 80% of incidents have occurred over the past two weeks. The attacks have killed at least four Palestinians since the harvest began, the Associated Press . More than 120 others have been wounded in the attacks, which have damaged over 2,500 olive trees and saplings. Israeli advertising firm helped place "zero-click" spyware on Al Jazeera devices: Israeli advertising technology company Discover-Tech helped place sophisticated spyware on dozens of devices used by Al Jazeera and other companies, to an investigation by The Citizen Lab, a research unit at the University of Toronto. Spyware from Israeli firm Candiru was planted on journalists' devices using the first-known instance of "zero-click" targeted advertising, according to the Citizen Lab investigation, which was prompted by an internal Al Jazeera probe. The spyware collects a wide range of data: files, documents, and browser data like cookies, bookmarks, and saved credentials. It also captures keystrokes, takes screenshots, records microphone and webcam input, and extracts emails and messages from popular communication platforms. Some of the Israeli spyware-ads were also discovered in critical networks used by the Pentagon, the United Nations International Atomic Energy Agency, and the International Criminal Court, Al Jazeera said, citing a by security firm Confiant. Iran Iranian president accuses U.S. and Israel of "ecocide": U.S. and Israeli military campaigns in Iran and Gaza have caused widespread environmental destruction that amounts to "ecocide or environmental genocide," President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Friday, during an address at the COP17 biodiversity summit in Armenia.. Widespread U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iranian fuel storage facilities and related infrastructure have contaminated soil and water, Pezeshkian said,warning that the deterioration of Iran's ecosystems could persist for decades. As for Israel's obliteration of Gaza, he added, it "stands as a stark testament to ecocide, with devastation whose horrific impacts will endure for generations." He called for international mechanisms to assess environmental damage, fund ecosystem restoration, and ensure that countries subjected to war and sanctions do not bear the recovery costs alone. Iranian navy reports oil tanker on fire after entering "restricted" waters near Hormuz: An oil tanker caught fire in a "restricted" area of the Sea of Oman after reportedly switching off its tracking systems and attempting to cross a prohibited route, Iran's navy said Friday. The cause of the fire and the condition of the crew were not immediately clear. Bloomberg: Pentagon to delay report on Iran school bombing until after midterms: Senior Pentagon officials intend to delay the release of an internal report into the bombing of a school in southern Iran on the first day of the war until after the U.S. midterm elections, to Bloomberg. The U.S. bombing of the Shajareh Tayyebeh school in Minab on February 28 killed at least 156 people, including 120 children and 26 teachers, in one of the single worst massacres committed by the U.S. government since the Vietnam War. Several of War Secretary Pete Hegseth's advisers conveyed to Pentagon personnel the plan to delay publication of the report, according to Bloomberg. New York Senator Kirsten Gillibrand said in a : "Withholding this report until after the election is not only disgraceful, it is cowardly. We have waited months--release the report. Congress and the American people deserve full transparency and accountability around this attack." Read Drop Site 's in-depth investigation into the Minab school bombing . U.S. sanctions Iraqi bank and 26 individuals, entities over Iran ties: On Thursday, the U.S. sanctions on the Iraq Development Bank, nine other entities, and 16 individuals over alleged financial ties to Iran, as part of the Trump administration's "Economic Outcast" campaign that aims to sever Tehran's remaining economic lifelines. The Treasury Department accused the bank, which Iraq barred from U.S. dollar transactions in 2024, of exploiting Iraq's former dollar auction system and maintaining ties to Iranian government entities and Iran-aligned militias. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent the department "will not relent until the Iranian regime's coffers are empty." He added, "the noose is tightening around Iran's economy, and not even Iran's so-called allies can save it." Reuters: Iran conducted precision strikes on critical infrastructure in Gulf Arab countries: Iran's precision strikes on critical infrastructure in the Persian Gulf during the war included at least 135 drone and missile attacks on at least 84 infrastructure sites across seven countries--Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Iraq, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, and Bahrain--according to a Reuters . Despite Gulf governments' repeated statements that the damage was the result of falling debris from intercepted Iranian missiles or drones, Reuters found that the Iranian strikes were in fact pinpoint attacks on critical equipment. Some of the targets were hidden beneath rooftops and sunshades, and invisible to space satellites. Two Gulf officials and one Iranian official told Reuters that Iran relied on networks of informants to conduct the attacks. After reviewing Reuters' findings, Ryan Stevens, a former U.S. Marine Corps special operations airstrike coordinator, said Iran's strikes showed "precision, targeting expertise, and patience." Lebanon Israeli forces strike residential building, school, religious seminary across southern Lebanon amid "ceasefire": Nabatieh: An Israeli quadcopter two missiles at the roof of an inhabited residential building in Mefdoun, with the first failing to explode, on Friday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Emergency crews evacuated residents before the second strike, and no injuries were reported. Israeli forces also carried out two large, simultaneous explosions near a school in Kfar Tebnit and in Zawtar Al-Sharqiya at dawn. Bint Jbeil: An Israeli tank a shell directly at a religious seminary building on the outskirts of Aita Al-Jabal. Tyre (Sour): Israeli warplanes an airstrike on Mansouri. U.S. News Teen gunman kills four, including three children, at Oregon elementary school: A 16-year-old fire Thursday at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, killing four children aged 5, 8 and 11, and one teacher, police said. A 7-year-old student and a 54-year-old teacher were hospitalized in critical condition. The shooter entered by firing through locked doors. An armed community member who saw him enter pursued him into the school and killed him, according to Gov. Tina Kotek, who** thanked that individual for "heroically" intervening to stop further loss of life. Police have not made the identity of the shooter public, nor have they identified the community member. Trump cancels livestream of firing-squad execution, reversing Hegseth: Trump Thursday on Truth Social that the government will not stream Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan 's Dec. 3 execution, canceling the plan War Secretary Pete Hegseth announced last week. Trump said streaming "might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan," but that "many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device." He said Hasan "will die, as scheduled, by firing squad," and that family members of his victims will be able to view it in person. AOC gives $1 million to El-Sayed 's Senate campaign: On Friday, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez(D-NY) transferred $1 million to the Senate campaign of Dr. Abdul El-Syed , the Democratic candidate in Michigan, the New York Times . "I'm not waking up on November 4th wishing I did more to combat the smears aimed at Abdul," Ocasio-Cortez said in a statement to the Times. "I'm leaving everything I can on the field." Ocasio-Cortez, one of the most influential Democrats in the country, joined El-Syed at campaign events across northern Michigan on Thursday. On Friday, she will hold her own rallies in the Detroit area. Democratic senators move to block U.S.-Saudi nuclear cooperation deal: Sens. Jeff Merkley of Oregon and Edward Markey of Massachusetts a resolution Thursday that would block the U.S.-Saudi "123 agreement," invoking the Atomic Energy Act as their justification. The resolution will force a debate and a vote when lawmakers return next month. Both chambers would have to adopt it to block the deal, and it faces steep odds in the Republican-controlled House. Trump officials reviewed Omar 's immigration file in 2019 and found no citizenship issues: A political appointee in the first Trump administration immigration authorities in 2019 to review Rep. Ilhan Omar 's records for fraud, three former officials told the Washington Post. Career staffers found it highly unusual. Homeland Security Investigations concluded there was insufficient evidence of wrongdoing and dropped the idea of a full investigation. A USCIS officer's one-page memo, printed and hand-delivered because of its sensitivity, found no issues. USCIS said then it couldn't determine her age reliably because refugees often lack birth records, and examined her father's file without finding problems. The marriage allegations were also reviewed: her former husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, withdrew a green card application after USCIS asked for more evidence. One former official said, "I think her citizenship is solid and there wasn't any fraud there." DOJ sues California and LA County officials to stop counting ballots of 20,000+ alleged noncitizens: The Justice Department California Secretary of State Shirley Weber , Los Angeles County Registrar Dean Logan , and the state on Thursday, asking a federal judge to block officials from counting ballots of voters it identified until their citizenship is verified. It claims officials plan to count ballots from more than 20,000 alleged noncitizens. The suit followed a Tuesday letter by Deputy Attorney General R. Trent McCotter demanding that Logan agree within 48 hours. Logan replied that he hadn't opened a thumb drive containing the names of the alleged noncitizens because doing so would violate privacy and data-security protocols, and that canceling registrations requires verifiable information, "not assertions of unconfirmed data matching." Rep. Andy Harris threatens reporter with prosecution for recording him after Maryland debate: Maryland Republican Rep. Andy Harris a reporter Tuesday, "You do not have my permission to record. If you record, we will refer you to prosecutors," in a gaggle after his debate with Democrat Dan Schwartz in Cambridge, Maryland, according to video shot by a Baltimore Banner photojournalist. The reporter, Cat Murphy of Capital News Service, said, "Everyone in here is recording. Why am I not allowed to?" Harris cited Maryland's all-party consent wiretapping law, which carries up to five years in prison and a $10,000 fine. He then called for an officer and left the room without waiting for one. The video shows at least eight journalists in the gaggle. Murphy said she is credentialed through a Capitol gallery and that the debate required no press registration. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Reuters: White House gave the order to limit Ukraine 's SpaceX satellite access: An order to impose limitations on Ukraine's access to SpaceX's Starshield service, used for navigation by Ukrainian drones, came from inside the White House, Reuters . The sudden outage disrupted Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia as well as defensive interceptors used to shoot down Russian drones Ukrainian officials said. The outage came as President Donald Trump was pressuring Ukraine to limit its strikes on Russian refineries. Philippines rebukes Chinese ambassador over "thinly veiled threat": The Philippines rebuked the Chinese ambassador Jing Quan for saying China could "easily win" a confrontation with the Philippines, Reuters . Quan, who added that China would not use force because "we love peace," was responding to the Philippines defense secretary's remark that China is a "troublemaker," The Beijing envoy's comments "very much sound like a threat," said Philippines President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Poland scrambles jets as Russian strikes hit western Ukraine; Bulgaria asks NATO for military support: Poland's armed forces fighter jets during overnight Russian attacks near the Polish border of Ukraine. No airspace violation was recorded. The Russian strikes injured two people and cut power to 370,000 others, the Volyn Oblast governor said. A Russian drone attack killed three people and injured five others in Kharkiv. Strikes in Uman injured several people.. Also on Friday, Ukrainian attacks killed two people in Russian-occupied Luhansk, according to . Russian authorities In Russia, air defenses blocked a Ukrainian drone attack on a heating plant in the Vladimir region, officials said. Ebola spreads to Congolese province bordering Central African Republic: The Ebola outbreak has an eighth province of the Democratic Republic of Congo, where two cases have been confirmed, Reuters reported. The province, North Ubangi, borders the Central African Republic, which has not yet recorded a case. The outbreak is the second-largest on record, with more than 9,000 confirmed cases and over 4,000 deaths. Ethiopian forces deepen control over Tigray: Ethiopian forces their control of Tigray, entering the historic city of Aksum, while rival Tigrayan fighters remain in mountains surrounding the city. Eritrean troops retreated toward the border after sustaining significant casualties, according to a spokesperson with the Ethiopia-aligned militia Tigray Peace Force. Eritrea's Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel denied the claims. Ethiopian PM announces temporary government for Tigray, promises election: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed a temporary administration for northern Tigray and announced elections would be held within six months, Reuters reported. Tigray's ruling party, the Tigray People's Liberation Front, led an offensive last month against Abiy's government, reigniting a war that killed hundreds of thousands of people from 2020 to 2022 Ethiopian forces have since taken control of large portions of Tigray, including the capital city of Mekelle. Somalia announces 2027 elections: Elections for both chambers of parliament will be held April 15, 2027, followed by a May 15 presidential vote, Abdikarim Ahmed Hassan, head of Somalia's Independent National Elections and Boundaries Commission, Thursday. The ruling President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term, which began in 2022, ended earlier this year, but his government declared a "transition period," despite an agreement with the opposition to hold elections. Two Syrian pipelines damaged; one attributed to sabotage: A gas pipeline in the southern Syrian province of Hasakah was struck and exploded on Thursday, the state-owned Syrian Petroleum Company The company called it a "sabotage attack." Separately, a fuel leak was reported in the Baniyas-Homs oil pipeline. The leak is suspected to be the result of an attempted theft, according to state media. U.S. discussing "denuclearization" with Russia and China, Trump says: The U.S. has engaged Russia and China in "denuclearization" talks," Trump Thursday. The U.S. and Russia each possess about 4,000 nuclear warheads. China possesses about 620 warheads, but is expected to "catch up" within years, Trump said. "The whole thing is a shame because I'd love to denuclearise if possible," he added. French police accused of excessive violence against youth protesters in multiple cases: Police in France have launched internal investigations into 36 allegations of officer violence against demonstrators, to the interior minister, Laurent Nuñez. The accusations include four children allegedly being "mutilated" by explosive weapons, such as stun grenades, and six sustaining "significant injuries," as well as other complaints, including physical beatings and sexual assault. An unprecedented number of children have been arrested since the protests began in mid-September, with a total of 6,773 children under 18 taken into police custody, according to the justice ministry. France is in the fourth week of its biggest youth protest movement in decades, launched by high school students demonstrating for better conditions and the replacement of absent teachers. El Salvador 's Bukele announces plan to release detainees: El Salvador's Nayib Bukele unexpectedly announced plans to up to 50% of the more than 93,000 detained under El Salvador's state of exception, framing the proposal as an amnesty for those accused of a lesser degree of "collaboration" with the country's gangs. Bukele made the surprise announcement only after a journalist interrupted a carefully managed press conference to ask about comments made by the president's brother, Ibrajim Bukele, about a commission to review cases. Or, how I came to public service

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141553441/653943682/1239926708?refcode=ea.96ef8b76-76c9-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ms=ea.96ef8b76-76c9-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NmVmOGI3Ni03NmM5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kIFg4CF8M8HLYJHuY5fdgyfmjx-R2O00k9hwAYaEzmg=&emci=9c942623-52c8-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=96ef8b76-76c9-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=51844520) [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141553447/653943687/1839755661?refcode=ea.96ef8b76-76c9-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ms=ea.96ef8b76-76c9-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NmVmOGI3Ni03NmM5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kIFg4CF8M8HLYJHuY5fdgyfmjx-R2O00k9hwAYaEzmg=) Friend, it's Phil. Growing up, I never dreamed of holding elected office. I never imagined that one day, I'd earn the official Democratic nomination for governor of Colorado. Truth be told, when I got to college, I thought I'd be a doctor like my dad. But after trying _(and struggling through)_ some science classes, I realized that wasn't my future. **What really caught my interest was public service. And, I am so grateful it did, because it has become my life's work to _fight like hell_ for the kind of future we deserve.** [**I truly couldn't be prouder of how far this campaign has come. I hope you'll chip in to sustain us in these final weeks, but I also hope you'll stick with me so I can explain why I'm asking today.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141553454/653943697/-147829035?refcode=ea.96ef8b76-76c9-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ms=ea.96ef8b76-76c9-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NmVmOGI3Ni03NmM5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kIFg4CF8M8HLYJHuY5fdgyfmjx-R2O00k9hwAYaEzmg=) It has been my honor to serve as Colorado's attorney general for the past seven years. This experience has been essential preparation to take on the challenges we're facing: Attacks on our most essential rights and freedoms, especially from the bullies in the Trump administration. Sky-high costs across child care, health care, and housing — costs that push teachers out of the communities they work in, place obstacles between Coloradans and their dream of homeownership, and put desperately needed care out of reach for too many. And a lack of opportunity for our young people, who are forced to leave the state they love in order to build a life they can afford. **I have had enough. I believe we can and must do better. And I will be ready to get to work on day one, on behalf of _all_ Coloradans — not just the wealthy or powerful few.** Being grassroots means _you_ are the power behind this campaign. I was back on the Pastor's Office podcast at Calvary Chapel Greater Portland this week with Pastor Travis Carey. Travis opened by noting that plenty of people would call me a Christian nationalist. I corrected him. Christo-Fascist is actually the proper term leftists use to describe those of us who hold the same view of sex, gender, and life that Barack Obama espoused in 2008.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/481902f1-6321-4de4-ae45-4107fdcfac21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
My view: the left uses "Christian nationalist" as a weapon, and what it conjures for half the country is The Handmaid's Tale (a crappy book, Orwell rip off). For me it is something much more boring. It's the political philosophy of a Christian in a self-governing society. If you believe Jesus was Who He said He was, some beliefs about politics flow from that. That's it. I've yet to meet a Christian who wants some government force mandating that every person believe in Christ's claims.
We talked about the myth of the value-free state. Secular humanists, in my opinion, treat their own morality (and by extension, the moral ethic they attempt to legislate) as the neutral default and everyone else's as some radical departure from a non-controversial, reasonable norm. Their positions are "settled science" and "settled law," and everything else is, well, Christo-Fascism! (We really should print the t-shirts over at MaineWireMerch.com...)

Right now, my mom, Deb, is on the phone with her team talking about how our midnight deadline is less than six hours away, but she’s still short of her $25,000 goal.

If you've been following what's happening in Minnesota, here's where we're at now:
1. The latest polls now have me and my Far Left opponent, Peggy Flanagan, DEAD EVEN in the home stretch. Voters are clearly demanding change.

3. The Democrat political machine has invested thousands in bogus attack ads in Minnesota against me because they're terrified of us pulling off the upset.

It's clear now, more than ever, that the tides are turning in our direction. I wanted to show you, in these points above, some of the fruits of all of our hard work together.

**We won 't be that team.**
If anything, we're itching to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat. We've known since the start of this movement that we're the clear underdog in this race.
But we're FAR from throwing in the towel.
Now that we're in the home stretch, your direct support to me and this movement becomes even more important.
Truth be told, it'd be a disaster if we lost you, Peter.

The latest poll shows MAGA Governor Joe Lombardo and I are statistically tied, with nearly 1 in 10 voters still not knowing who they’re supporting.

Lombardo is outspending us on the airwaves, and we can’t let him dominate the narrative of this race. If the only thing Nevadans hear is his side of the story, we lose.

name: Gabby Giffords
subject: Oregon
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
#

Friends —
**A shooting at an elementary school should shock us.**
Yesterday, children in Bend, Oregon, experienced the terror of gunfire inside their elementary school. Three children and one teacher were killed.
For decades, school shootings have left an unimaginable trail of grief across this country. We still carry the heartbreak of the children and educators killed at Columbine, Sandy Hook, and Uvalde—and of far too many other lives stolen by gun violence in our schools.
We promised after each of these tragedies that we would do better. Yet too many leaders have watched shooting after shooting devastate our communities and still refused to do enough to keep guns out of the wrong hands.
**This is not inevitable. Thoughts and prayers will not stop the next school shooting. We need action.**
Our children deserve to go to school without the fear of being shot. Elementary school should be about jungle gyms, math class, and making new friends—not learning where to hide from a shooter.
My heart is completely broken for the children, families, teachers, and entire Silver Rail Elementary community in Bend, Oregon today.
Gabby Giffords

**Please, take a second to read this...**
As a victim of political violence, Gabby Giffords has led the fight to save more lives from gun violence for more than a decade, but she can’t do it alone.
If everyone reading this donated just $17, we'd have the resources to pass commonsense gun safety legislation across the country. But not everyone gives — making it even more important for people who care and understand the stakes of our struggle to pitch in what they can.
**If $17 seems worth it to you to change our gun laws in order to make our communities safer from gun violence, we're asking you to contribute to GIFFORDS PAC today.**

name: Christina (personal)
subject: When Iowans come together
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CHRISTINA BOHANNAN FOR CONGRESS
body:
| Peter, I really can't believe how quickly time has flown.

It feels like just yesterday that we launched this campaign last summer. And now, in the blink of an eye, it's October. The election is right around the corner, and the finish line is finally coming into view.

When we started this, I knew I'd give it everything I had. I've never taken anything for granted, and I knew taking on Mariannette Miller-Meeks and the well-funded political establishment backing her would be an uphill battle.

**What I couldn't have predicted, but always hoped for, was just how many people would decide to climb that hill with us.**

Every day, I see Iowans showing up for this campaign in big and small ways. You're knocking doors, making calls, putting up signs, talking to your neighbors, sharing our message and, yes, chipping in to help us reach voters across this district.

**Today, I'm so proud to tell you that we met and exceeded our last mid-month goal of the election.**

My team and I are working harder than ever to bring this thing home. Every dollar you're giving right now is helping us keep reaching voters, keep telling them what's at stake, and keep fighting for the future of our district.

You've been the wind beneath our wings since the very beginning. You believed in this campaign before we knew how far it could go. You've reminded me again and again that when Iowans come together, there is nothing we can't accomplish.

Thank you,

Christina

P.S. We're ending this election cycle with a bang. **My team and I have set an ambitious $100,000 end-of-month goal for October to make sure we have the resources to win on November 3rd. Our new permitting deal is picking up support from labor, energy producers, nonprofits, and more. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141556897/653956975/-272948131?refcode=AU_MTH_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20261016_AM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzM2E5OWM0NC03YmM5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6gm2BzS50ALTJYBlymYqRvs_uS5WgZJ2sZLZWwfjRgQ=&emci=fd158a1d-7bc9-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=33a99c44-7bc9-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=252045)
