The scenario I wanted was simple: Republicans -- the party of the little guy against woke megacorporations -- standing this fall and telling voters, "Your electric bill is exploding because Big Tech's server farms came for your grid, and we're the ones who'll stop them." That issue was sitting there, polling like a dream, native to red states. The evidence of the 2026 campaign is that Democrats picked it up and ran. If red-state Republicans lose in November, this is the autopsy: they left the most visceral affordability issue of the cycle -- the light bill -- unowned, and an issue unowned gets owned against you.
They're running with it. Everywhere.
Politico reported on Sept. 6 that Democrats have "finally figured out" the message: data centers as "giant outposts of megacorporations" that enjoy "undue tax breaks" and "suck up precious water and hog electricity." In Ohio, Sherrod Brown calls Sen. Jon Husted "the face of data centers in Ohio" and pins rising utility bills on state policy -- an attack the NRSC itself warned in an August memo could become a "sleeper issue." In Georgia, Jon Ossoff turned his Oct. 8 debate with Mike Collins into a referendum on the proposed $20 billion OpenAI campus in Effingham County: "No Georgia family or small business should pay a dime more to subsidize the energy consumption of these data centers" -- and, sharper, he charged that the Republican budget bill "gave $70 billion of your money to data center developers." He'd been building the file all year, including an April letter pressing FERC on data-center rate agreements. Down-ballot Democrats in Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Georgia have led on the issue since winter. A Washington Post analysis cited by Brookings found candidate rhetoric flipped from mostly positive in 2024 to sharply negative in 2026 -- Republicans turned negative too, but it's Democrats now holding the consumer-protection end. And in Pataskala, Ohio, the Wall Street Journal found the most common lawn sign backs neither candidate nor party: "VOTE YES TO BAN DATA CENTERS." That's organic anger looking for a claimant.
The polls say it's a winner
About 6 in 10 Americans -- including most Republicans -- support limiting new data centers, per the Associated Press; a majority are "extremely" or "very" concerned about effects on electricity prices and water supply. Pew's 2026 poll found 38% say data centers' effect on home energy costs is "mostly bad" against 6% "mostly good." Nearly half of states have seen double-digit percentage rate increases in 2026 alone (CNBC). The Center Square Voters' Voice Poll found that after general inflation, the top blame falls on "companies using AI data centers as an excuse to raise profits." Nearly half of Americans already expected data-center energy costs to be a campaign issue (Politico). Bloomberg reports local opposition blocked or delayed 120 projects worth nearly $200 billion in the first half of 2026 -- before a single ad aired in most districts. And the 2025 governors' races in New Jersey and Virginia were the preview: electricity costs were central, and Democrats won on affordability.
Red-state Republicans had the claim -- and let it go
This is tailor-made populist ground for the GOP: red states host the building boom, "your light bill vs. their server farm" is their native idiom, and the polling is bipartisan. But President Trump embraced the AI build-out, the budget bill really did fund data-center developers, and Republican governors and utility commissioners spent a decade waving the projects through with tax abatements -- making incumbents the industry's face whether they liked it or not. The late scramble -- the Ratepayer Protection Act, passed in the House and forced onto the Senate floor Sept. 30 -- was too little, too late. The tell: the issue is so hot that when Senate Democrats blocked the bill, Ossoff and Warnock were among just four Democrats willing to vote yes, while Ossoff brands himself a ratepayer champion back home. Smart politicians in both parties know a winning issue when they poll one.
The verdict
If red-state Republicans go down in November, it won't be because data centers were a niche grievance. It will be because the party of the little guy ceded the one kitchen-table cost voters touch every single month -- and learned the oldest rule of populism: you either own the people's issue, or the other party owns you.

name: Greisa, United We Dream
subject: One year ago, we made a promise, Peter​
body:
Here’s what 7,000 neighbors made possible this year. | | | Peter, One year ago, we said it out loud: community is the only antidote to the threats we’re facing. So United We Dream, the ACLU, and Abundant Futures Fund launched the **Defending Our Neighbors Fund**. It rushes resources to frontline organizations that provide legal representation and bond support to immigrant families. Then you showed up. And you kept showing up. One year later, here’s what we, the people, built together:
* 🎉 **$15 million+ raised**
* 🧡 **56 grants to 35 trusted organizations**
* ✊🏽 **7,000+ everyday people who chose to defend their neighbors**

**Behind every number is a family that didn’t have to face this system alone.** In Texas, the federal government abruptly cut funding to the Galveston-Houston Immigrant Representation Project. The Project kept its team in place anyway, and in just two months it represented 100 children in immigration court and asylum offices. In New York City, Envision Freedom Fund grew into the largest community bond fund in the country. This year alone, it secured the release of 422 people from detention. Detained immigrants with a lawyer are up to _seven times_ more likely to be released and reunited with family.1 That’s what your support makes possible. **[Our year-one impact review is here: the numbers, the stories, and the people who made it possible. Read it now →](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.LMLYNSUutlzZfwLijrhnv_hpfumZrpWD1zzhIDdbOoH1kkj4LsjwZzLQmoXQETC5d9JR_7Ue0S1FyMOA5rnQmW-otN3hf52tZ5CYSU9P_YeVPizQ_ObXQex741dLbU-pJLoNeQ6-IhviKpC4OilMmPuS-TgfGj33d14-xRC_dwIznY2beOahX4Htr62f22PKOIQ5Kg0kzq0TRoR2eChp_OHkPs8U3BkXvgwsbX0tNr33MuOCGPivQKMqdy9i9Y2jpfYDuDxzjkauOCak5Tj8r5uftj7D16cH1LgKzTnsmbLLZmGfZlR2dnvILhVOA18p-Oa6C9WLvMi3P32wAARR_y1B0z0hm3dJkpWfuhEltySDbwpwqOCI8ELW_Y82dPCVrV4qgd-hapMWw6yuZIpk3Nmh71mg255d6PSsxm25iDkkqeaTIC0WItlBQAYcjNw_f4AcAnAVQ-Zv3pUQIwBJ-kzjs6P_wjuiNv3jEKGA8PlMcDkgkXdGWLqslI5k9Yqq/4ux/1owNGGOuS52xvvtW3i88Zg/h0/h001.dgxhCEVIHRqGoaafpVJtXHpheKq3GRDUeTo---LgSvc)** | | [Read the blog post](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.LMLYNSUutlzZfwLijrhnv_hpfumZrpWD1zzhIDdbOoH1kkj4LsjwZzLQmoXQETC5d9JR_7Ue0S1FyMOA5rnQmW-otN3hf52tZ5CYSU9P_YeVPizQ_ObXQex741dLbU-pJLoNeQ6-IhviKpC4OilMmPuS-TgfGj33d14-xRC_dwIznY2beOahX4Htr62f22PKOIQ5Kg0kzq0TRoR2eChp_OHkPs8U3BkXvgwsbX0tNr33MuOCGPivQKMqdy9i9Y2jpfYDuDxzjkauOCak5Tj8r5uftj7D16cH1LgKzTnsmbJE9Jt4HXLwICeYP7uEgwJ43GXdwta3te4olo852CH-sjTcmm8Banx5NHzvByMbBRV5Z6_y5EQcus6mMBD6qRSFkjKY5FZU_Ob64v2yyHdTO8i6OxLcEAlhF1otqpSwVAlvdnvWvtcpReg2vfZLEYFJEAkxNYOYrRCyCty85KlssUcdl2-qJ4KODLj-phHwAU18iUONmCECIZnXqijecTm2/4ux/1owNGGOuS52xvvtW3i88Zg/h1/h001.fJUUiLJRr9gdtnYf3a93oMPMCB2UVhGs_3DA26uPKkE)

As Rosa Santana of Envision Freedom Fund put it: _“It takes a village to be able to do this work. I’m glad to say that the Defending Our Neighbors Fund is part of our village.”_
You’re part of that village too. We’re here, we’re organized, and we’re so proud of what we’ve built together.
— Greisa, United We Dream

Hello Friends,
**Did you know you can vote early, in person, this weekend?** The Allegheny County Elections Division will have a satellite election office at the North Park Ice Rink (1200 Pearce Mill Rd., Wexford) **from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Saturday, Oct. 17, and Sunday, Oct. 18.**
Any registered Allegheny County voter can use this location. **Your ballot will be printed on-site, and you can fill it out and turn it in right there. Be sure to bring your ID**.
**Already have a mail-in ballot? You can drop it off here too.** Just remember that you can only return your own ballot, and you need to sign and date the outer envelope.
Can’t make it this weekend? North Park will be open again next Saturday and Sunday, Oct. 24 and 25, with the same hours.
**

Peter,

We just committed over $1.2 million to 11 states with must-win legislative

Pennsylvania, Texas, and Wisconsin). I’m incredibly proud of the work
we’ve been able to do so far, and I’m grateful to you for supporting our
work. Seriously, none of this would be possible without you.

But we have to keep up our momentum. We’re putting this much into these
states because that’s where the closest fights are. These are the seats
that will be decided by a handful of votes, and the leaders who win them
will shape the lives of everyone living there more than the average voter
is probably aware. These races are also how we break the GOP’s grip on
power. Democrats need to pick up seats in these state legislative chambers
in order to secure a real check on Trump’s dangerous agenda. Protecting
reproductive rights, healthcare, ensuring fair 2028 electoral maps, ending
ICE’s reign of terror – it all hinges on winning these critical state
legislature races on November 3rd.

Whatever we raise in this final stretch is the number Republicans and

That's why I need your support right now. Every dollar we bring in

Brown, leaving in force the FCC notice that lets party and joint fundraising committees buy broadcast time at the lowest unit charge. Justices Sotomayor and Jackson voted against the stay. It holds until the Court decides whether to hear the merits, which it is unlikely to do before November 3, so the committees keep candidate rates through the close. In 2021 the World Economic Forum -- not a movement pamphlet, but the Davos club itself -- announced that the pandemic had stretched its projected wait for global gender parity from 99.5 years to 135.6.
Whatever you make of Davos arithmetic, it put hard numbers on a phrase people usually throw around without paying for it: "set back a century." I want to use that phrase anyway, and aim it at three of the most decorated women's-rights agitators of the American order: Gloria Steinem, died 92; Bernardine Dohrn, 84; and Randi Weingarten, 68.
My opinion, stated plainly: each took a magnificent gift for organizing and spent it on a project adjacent to -- never identical with -- women's freedom, and women have been paying the difference ever since...

Steinem, Dohrn, and Weingarten | | | Oct 16| | | ∙| | Preview ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | In 2021 the World Economic Forum -- not a movement pamphlet, but the Davos club itself -- announced that the pandemic had stretched its projected wait for global gender parity from 99.5 years to 135.6. Whatever you make of Davos arithmetic, it put hard numbers on a phrase people usually throw around without paying for it: "set back a century." I want to use that phrase anyway, and aim it at three of the most decorated women's-rights agitators of the American order: Gloria Steinem, died 92; Bernardine Dohrn, 84; and Randi Weingarten, 68. My opinion, stated plainly: each took a magnificent gift for organizing and spent it on a project adjacent to -- never identical with -- women's freedom, and women have been paying the difference ever since... | | **Campaigns across the country are recognizing the value of our movement.**

| | | I’m going to ask you to chip in before you sign off for the weekend, and I want to explain why it has to be today, not Monday. _Weekends are when we do the most and raise the least._ Tomorrow, volunteers across Southwest Washington will be up early knocking doors in Longview, Vancouver, Centralia, and everywhere in between. It’s our biggest voter-contact day of the week — especially this week, since ballots are dropping. On Sunday, they’ll do it again.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141574596/654008535/-995582223?refcode=261016-weekend-vols&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5MTg3Mzg0OC05N2M5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6gxHNG3olqfI_Ux50gjnoIFALEWkhKHLz24KWi9wN2U=)
---
**And the whole time, donations slow to a trickle because people are living their lives instead of reading campaign emails. Honestly, good. That’s what weekends are for.** But here’s the problem. Ballots are already reaching people. The latest poll has this race at 48–47. And Republicans are outspending us three to one on TV, with Trump-aligned groups alone putting in more than $3 million. A two-day slowdown right now costs us two days we don’t get back. **[So will you chip in $10 right now, so we can head into this critical weekend with a full tank?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141574597/654008536/-995582223?refcode=261016-weekend-vols&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5MTg3Mzg0OC05N2M5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6gxHNG3olqfI_Ux50gjnoIFALEWkhKHLz24KWi9wN2U=)**

A donation that comes in today is worth more than the same donation on Monday. That’s two more days of planning, two more days of buying, and two more days of doing the work instead of waiting on it. John Braun’s donors aren’t taking the weekend off. Donald Trump’s super PAC sure isn’t. And as ballots reach people, neither are we. **[Click here to donate now so we can reach voters before they fill out their ballots.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141574599/654008538/-995582223?refcode=261016-weekend-vols&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5MTg3Mzg0OC05N2M5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6gxHNG3olqfI_Ux50gjnoIFALEWkhKHLz24KWi9wN2U=)** Thank you so much. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez

And Republicans are outspending us three to one on TV, with Trump-aligned groups alone putting in more than $3 million. A two-day slowdown right now costs us two days we don’t get back. = = A donation that comes in today is worth more than the same donation on Monday. That’s two more days of planning, two more days of buying, and two more days of doing the work instead of waiting on it. John Braun’s donors aren’t taking the weekend off. Donald Trump’s super PAC sure isn’t. And as ballots reach people, neither are we. = Thank you so much. If you ever watched _Star Trek: The Next Generation_ , you probably remember those words...

The Borg – a collective machine intelligence – are frightening because they do not threaten or argue. Their assimilation of all life in the universe is simply an inevitability.

That scene has been on my mind lately because it is about as good a metaphor as I know for the [unstoppable spread of artificial intelligence.](https://links.dpt.deepregimetrends.com/u/click?_t=4a25883d9bf54436b571b8aa9717dcca&_m=5766d717c58c42dc81a955e0e743b5c1&_e=7IXHa_hz5tsAkCXsuOaALk-4dAe0nuGYy-MkPY24pjlh_c6Py6iQzqufbf5v-YkYh6qTkCaDpdQlijxyWknSBI4DwDIgQXIO-P9A-J_SPw4SK87Lih5JrJ7ipr_Kt_4yz3_TE63CwfBotbd96viDT2Jbnj6iIMG4HRLB8UsICFNQsxrDvallRHTLlZWdJUAJQJBVIOWTO8184kx9RA3a6QxgPjb_3oO64Gz6rij7bsZPiFhVw_bF0SLVXI3Sp68y37CqPsMN1XoOQ4XT41vnNP_DCqQ9G42VXrLx9fIgNfZNsCPslrSSbSaSgfe5HGFGoqqxU9eHIbF_jIvtF17NeavwFOMGoT795ZB40gxWzzfgbnUOYfGbv8TZQlHzSRTDV608VE8RAUkjGkn4tN4gKKWoKjdvioFTfwJVkn_fbc7RtrQsaUAm6Yl1xTWR3V7NyZNZ1ngmi_wZ_2HGQfvGNmmN5iGj96PRVr0O3rhD29mRMPEOcZKB7M9iB-cWJ00ci2qaNXKOPH5JUl5ICVgbeyaFeUVYvo-ynfhWFz94Ntw%3D)

Not because machines are about to turn us into mindless servants (we already have TikTok for that)... but because AI is advancing without any need for public agreement or approval. It has reached a Borg-like inevitability.

It’s not waiting for Washington to make up its mind or for the average American to decide whether any of this is a good idea.

Once software or a machine can perform useful work at a fraction of the cost, its adoption becomes an inevitable economic compulsion.

And the speed with which it is tearing through our civilization is staggering.

A study from the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis found that 39% of Americans between the ages of 18 and 64 had used generative AI within roughly two years of its mass-market introduction.

At the comparable point, internet adoption was around 20%. The internet took approximately five years to reach the level AI reached us in less than two.

Until now, nothing in our lifetimes had spread as quickly as the internet. Based on the adoption data cited above, AI is moving nearly twice as fast.
[](https://links.dpt.deepregimetrends.com/u/click?_t=4a25883d9bf54436b571b8aa9717dcca&_m=5766d717c58c42dc81a955e0e743b5c1&_e=7IXHa_hz5tsAkCXsuOaALk-4dAe0nuGYy-MkPY24pjlh_c6Py6iQzqufbf5v-YkYh6qTkCaDpdQlijxyWknSBI4DwDIgQXIO-P9A-J_SPw4SK87Lih5JrJ7ipr_Kt_4yz3_TE63CwfBotbd96viDT2Jbnj6iIMG4HRLB8UsICFOPrtfTTQb2276Aw3UcyBeeZpqt0kx3Q6NYHmVMltj_Nbdwazqh_d7Lm0Y9DlaHppDZH1S4A2igp8rmFXUy5_PnV9eZPol2Oq6BSlfd5IR0bVwD3NYx_syvi0yVSaz17S5XfrIYWjwfbee5whrWtGUlsnVuaezFGaOlNY7xXu75MFj-JTauK5tk0U5i0mdxoJ_nvP954VeWLq7x2OIo8B8GSO8qo8JX3sFhgfAP0uKrcnBzMuoU0_MJ_jV3mimmsSV-97-dKt69kLCrf2MGld1eJ3xJJG7CL16ZijoPPOJDoDGptIld6eQcUSjSctdYE7u38sleYaTrS2gaLCbf-ENgMPaAh9kmU8odOIq4-iJUUxer6U33UqQyjKOaGhMraQo%3D)
Many investors will look at that curve and conclude that it’s time to dump a load of cash into AI stocks.

But that’s where the trouble begins – because recognizing an inevitable technology is not the same thing as understanding [who will make money from it.](https://links.dpt.deepregimetrends.com/u/click?_t=4a25883d9bf54436b571b8aa9717dcca&_m=5766d717c58c42dc81a955e0e743b5c1&_e=7IXHa_hz5tsAkCXsuOaALk-4dAe0nuGYy-MkPY24pjlh_c6Py6iQzqufbf5v-YkYh6qTkCaDpdQlijxyWknSBI4DwDIgQXIO-P9A-J_SPw4SK87Lih5JrJ7ipr_Kt_4yz3_TE63CwfBotbd96viDT2Jbnj6iIMG4HRLB8UsICFOhkjO4Xl-2zLLaN4OfdZMRYK0XsFcEWuwPaBAP3If8jhCIf4gkRGw7Q8oOQylM5Y3FsxrhB5kOW41ZnnxcZfBsogG54fVEN7VQcTSbo6t8cC_zOFbeEOwO7krJNjis2kPqlm8gD38vKioeDtDa1J_2TYm81Uob6FC02UlPubRmUWxmiMZwvMfwbKWsd-wAyGpEOtqbjfLuJQs61xGWCLCGdDTNM-3jUN4fmdNOBg_W9VIziIzxEVDy5dgfbjhcFTd1mHIK5EpGu2ihjKAy9yS7k5UB-ieNObfQPxCBbigUU1GZcunA5kuE0tcBcCFeJxQKC5_Cg6-nK7xAK3ZRhyr_D4a8EAu0PLAyugo9yEbPxp5hwZ65TD5IK6EHG-uP50k%3D)
**Stranded on the wrong side of history**
In 1975, a Kodak engineer named Steve Sasson built the first self-contained digital camera. It weighed eight pounds, required 23 seconds to record a black-and-white image, and stored the result on a cassette tape.

Sure, the device was crude, but its potential impact was enormous. Kodak’s own engineer had invented a future in which people would no longer need film.

The management understood that potential perfectly well – and it terrified them. Because Kodak’s very existence depended on selling film. So, the company spent years defending the economics that its own invention was destroying.

By the time digital photography became impossible to resist, Kodak had lost both the habit and the ability to adapt. It entered bankruptcy in 2012.

Blockbuster had even less of an excuse to get steamrolled by technology. In 2000, Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph offered to sell Netflix to Blockbuster for $50 million. The Blockbuster executives reportedly struggled not to laugh.

Roughly a decade later, Blockbuster was bankrupt and Netflix was fast becoming the new distribution system for filmed entertainment. That was one of the more expensive chuckles in business history.

The internet boom taught me that history acts without mercy to people who can see a technological change in front of them but continue on in futility, unwilling to accept or embrace it.

In hindsight, the rise of the online world was obviously unstoppable.

Yet even some of the most respected publications of the day were deeply skeptical of the companies at the frontier.

In May 1999, Barron’s famously ran a cover story titled “Amazon.bomb,” declaring: _“Investors are beginning to realize that this storybook stock has problems.”_

I recommended Amazon two months before Barron’s ran that story. I saw something different I guess. I saw that Amazon had an undeniable business model. The shares have since risen more than 7,000%.

Years later, after using Shopify to operate one of my own businesses, our research recommended the stock in March 2016. We closed the position 18 months later with a 256% gain.

My interest in Bitcoin came from the same basic observation. The internet had created a genuinely scarce digital asset that could move around the world without relying on the traditional financial system.

These were very different investments, and the best examples of what can happen when everything goes right for us. I’m not claiming that happens every time. And, of course, past performance doesn’t tell us what will happen in the future.

But the question was always the same simple one: _What becomes more valuable because this technology exists?_

That is the question investors must answer about AI right now.
**Betting on the inevitable**
AI technology (in many different forms) will touch practically every company in America. But it will not reward all of them equally.

Enormous sums – trillions of dollars – are already pouring into semiconductors and the power-hungry data centers required to run the models.

Some businesses will turn that colossal buildout into decades of cash flow and investment returns for shareholders.

A great many more will discover that spending money on an indispensable technology does not make the spender indispensable.

That was one of the more expensive chuckles in business history. The internet boom taught me that history acts without mercy to people who can see a technological change in front of them but continue on in futility, unwilling to accept or embrace it. In hindsight, the rise of the online world was obviously unstoppable. Yet even some of the most respected publications of the day were deeply skeptical of the companies at the frontier. In May 1999, Barron’s famously ran a cover story titled “Amazon.bomb,” declaring: “Investors are beginning to realize that this storybook stock has problems.” I recommended Amazon two months before Barron’s ran that story. I saw something different I guess. I saw that Amazon had an undeniable business model. The shares have since risen more than 7,000%. Years later, after using Shopify to operate one of my own businesses, our research recommended the stock in March 2016. We closed the position 18 months later with a 256% gain. My interest in Bitcoin came from the same basic observation. The internet had created a genuinely scarce digital asset that could move around the world without relying on the traditional financial system. These were very different investments, and the best examples of what can happen when everything goes right for us. I’m not claiming that happens every time. And, of course, past performance doesn’t tell us what will happen in the future. But the question was always the same simple one: What becomes more valuable because this technology exists? That is the question investors must answer about AI right now. Betting on the inevitable AI technology (in many different forms) will touch practically every company in America. But it will not reward all of them equally. Enormous sums – trillions of dollars – are already pouring into semiconductors and the power-hungry data centers required to run the models. Some businesses will turn that colossal buildout into decades of cash flow and investment returns for shareholders. A great many more will discover that spending money on an indispensable technology does not make the spender indispensable. will not be between people who believe in AI and people who do not. It will be between those who own the scarce, profitable parts of this new economy and those whose livelihoods are being repriced by it. That’s why one of the best technology investors I know. Luke recommended AMD in 2015, and he has spent years studying how these technological shifts create – and destroy – fortunes. Luke and I explain where we believe the durable economics of AI will appear and why several of today’s most popular stocks may disappoint their investors. We also reveal the name and ticker of a little-known spin-off from a century-old American business that we believe could become crucial to the data-center buildout. The Borg were right: resistance is futile. So, for investors, the only useful question that remains is this: Will your capital be positioned before or after AI completely takes over the world? Good investing, Porter Stansberry | | | | Case File No DRT-ED-DIVIDE · Special File · The Great Divide AI Is Spreading Twice as Fast as the Internet Did. That Doesn’t Mean Most AI Stocks Will Win. Within two years of launch, about 4 in 10 working-age Americans were already using generative AI. Big Tech is spending more than $700 billion on AI infrastructure this year. History says a technology this big creates fortunes, but rarely for the companies everyone expects. Threat level 3/5 — Guarded | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|--- | The internet changed everything. It also wiped out a lot of investors who bet on the wrong companies. In 2000, everyone knew the internet would be huge. Most of the stocks they bought to play it never recovered. AI looks like the same kind of moment, only faster. The evidence board | | How Fast This Is Moving ---|--- | EVIDENCE Exhibit A — the adoption. A St. Louis Fed study found that by August 2024, about 39% of Americans aged 18 to 64 had used generative AI, less than two years after it went mainstream. The authors concluded adoption was faster than for the PC or the internet. | EVIDENCE Exhibit B — the money. The four biggest U.S. tech companies are guiding to well over $700 billion in capital spending this year, much of it on AI data centers and the chips and power to run them. | EVIDENCE Exhibit C — the lesson. Kodak’s own engineer built the first digital camera in 1975. The company went bankrupt in 2012. In 2000, Blockbuster passed on buying Netflix for $50 million. Seeing a technology coming isn’t the same as profiting from it. | OUR THEORY When everyone agrees a technology will win, the money floods into the obvious names and their prices run far ahead of their profits. The durable winners are usually the ones that own something scarce the new economy can’t do without. In AI, that increasingly looks like the physical side: power, cooling, connections, the things data centers literally can’t run without. name: Carrie Anne
subject: The final weeks, how is Forward faring?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Forward Party and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
Open me for party news you can use!

| | [ ](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=JgyyvCfQwldlSeD7KJl_Ih7269o_4hwqOhPs1_PHvgI&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_second_edi&n=1)
---
| Hello Forward Friends- Forward Party just keeps growing! Last weekend, the team went to Boise, Idaho in support of US Senate candidate [Todd Achilles.](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=gDz98NJdqG1BxZ1yWkkZaabbmu8XvNqRStzyElUXI6B_fWqevoP3reha4L5qXCiL&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_second_edi&n=2) From the reception while canvassing to our packed town hall, it's clear that communities are ready for a change in Washington, D.C. _Tabling at a Town Hall with Gov Whitman and Todd Achilles at Boise State!_ We loved introducing our federal and gubernatorial candidates to you with our "Meet the Forwardists" series, but we truly are a grassroots movement. It wouldn't be right if we didn't highlight some of our down ballot races as well! Join us on **Tues Oct 27th at 8pm ET** for our final local MTF event. | [](https://home.forwardparty.com/meet_the_forwardists_local_level?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_second_edi&n=3 "RSVP for Meet the Forwardists: Local level") [RSVP for Meet the Forwardists: Local level](https://home.forwardparty.com/meet_the_forwardists_local_level?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_second_edi&n=3)
---
**_Move America Forward_**
****Our partners at[Move America Forward](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=hLf6ra6-T4Ek_sf_A8AjExyKRqRscbrf6yzmfvidBhx0S7-tA_uS0_cjGZOzO3d8&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_second_edi&n=4) are staying on the move! They are canvassing and hosting a Town Hall this **Sat Oct 17th** with Representative Kevin Kiley and Forward CEO Lindsey Williams Drath. Then they're canvassing and hosting a Town Hall in Grand Junction, CO, the following weekend. Join them if you're in the area!
**_Volunteer Spotlight_**
Our Volunteer of the month for October is **Preston Love** from Texas! He has been the secretary for the Texas party and recently moved to Indiana, then he promptly reached out to ask about chairing the Indiana Party. Our movement doesn't grow without dedicated folks like Preston. We appreciate you!
**_Upcoming virtual events:_**
**Mon Oct 19th @ 6:30pm ET-**[ Welcome Team Training](https://home.forwardparty.com/welcome_team_intro_call_20261012?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_second_edi&n=5)
* This is a great time to call other Forwardists and talk about our amazing candidates. Learn how at this training.

**Tues Oct 20th @ 7:30 pm ET** \- [National Volunteer Call](https://home.forwardparty.com/national_volunteer_call_20261013?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_second_edi&n=6)
* Your place to go if you're new to Forward or want to learn how to get more involved. With the election a couple of weeks away we need all hands on deck!

**Tues Oct 20th @ 8pm ET** \- [BVC: Candidate Panel](https://home.forwardparty.com/12578/meet_the_candidates_hosted_by_the_fwd_black_voters_committee?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_second_edi&n=7)
* Join our Black Voters Committee as they introduce some incredible candidates.

**Thurs Oct 22th @ 6:30pm ET** \- [Forward Text Force](https://home.forwardparty.com/fwd_text_force_wk_1_20261022?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_second_edi&n=8)
* It's not too late to get started texting in support of our candidates and make a difference in some of these races!

I have had a blast traveling across the country, meeting supporters and knocking on voters doors. It feels amazing to make an impact on our democracy. I hope you can join me in some outreach these last few weeks!
With hope and gratitude,
Carrie Anne
[https://home.forwardparty.com/](https://home.forwardparty.com/?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_oct_second_edi&n=9)

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Trump isn't going to give up this seat without a fight.
body:

---
Thank you, thank you, thank you, Peter.
You haven’t chipped in to my U.S. Senate campaign yet, but I appreciate that you’re taking the time to read this email.
The momentum is on our side in North Carolina – with experts saying that this is our best chance to flip a Republican-held Senate seat in the entire country. None of our progress would be possible without people like you.
Here’s the problem: **The GOP is now panicking.**
President Trump and MAGA loyalist Stephen Miller have been spreading lies and misinformation about me in an attempt to put their thumbs on the scale for my Republican opponent, Michael Whatley. **Now, we’ve just learned that Trump is coming to North Carolina _next week_ to double down on these attacks.**
Trump is undefeated in North Carolina, so he’s not going to give up this seat without a fight. We can’t let Washington DC insider Michael Whatley and his MAGA allies buy this seat. I need your help to take him on, defeat his MAGA machine – and win.
[**_Peter, if you understand the stakes of this race, I’m asking you to make your first donation to my grassroots campaign today. $5 or any amount will do. Will you chip in to help me win in North Carolina and flip the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1682&amount=5&t=8&akid=4622%2E124072%2ELDTsfo)

CASE DISMISSED, GREGORY NOW FACES CONTEMPT AND ASKS A JUDGE TO
PROSECUTE COLORADO’S JUSTICES
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

The former director of Colorado’s judicial discipline commission
spent years trying to force accountability onto the state’s highest
court. A federal judge has now thrown out his lawsuit, and the state
wants him held in contempt.

Christopher S.P. Gregory sued the Colorado Supreme Court, the
state’s judicial discipline bodies, Gov. Jared Polis, Attorney
General Phil Weiser, and dozens of individual officials in October
2025. RMV first reported on the suit in March, when it was still
pending. The complaint has since been dismissed, and the fight has
turned on Gregory himself.

On Aug. 11, U.S. Senior District Judge Kathryn H. Vratil dismissed the
complaint in full. The Clerk entered final judgment the same day.

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

PUEBLO DEMOCRATS ADMIT BINGO MONEY WENT UNREPORTED, SETTLE FOR $3,202
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_The Pueblo County Democratic Party admitted to leaving nearly $58,000
in bingo income and headquarters spending off its campaign finance
reports, settling for a $3,202 penalty with no order to amend the
filings._

*
A LARGE GAP BETWEEN REPORTED AND ACTUAL MONEY: Across three 2024
disclosure reports, the party reported just over $6,500 in
contributions, while its affiliated committee actually netted
$40,936.74 from bingo and spent $17,109.68 on party headquarters
costs, none of which appeared on any filing.

*
A CASE THAT NEARLY DIED BEFORE IT SUCCEEDED: State officials initially
dismissed the complaint, filed by Republican county treasurer
candidate Jonathan Ambler, ruling bingo funds weren’t reportable,
until a Denver judge reversed that decision in March, finding evidence
of “commingling” and a “lack of separation” between the party
and its gaming committee.

*
UNANSWERED QUESTIONS REMAIN: The settlement imposes no requirement to
amend the reports and doesn’t address over a decade of earlier bingo
proceeds, roughly $3.6 million in gross receipts since 2013 according
to state filings, with Ambler arguing the deal leaves open who the
underlying contributors actually were.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b53e950b-a331-4fc2-81d3-23ab31dc6862?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Photo by [Shawn Day](https://substack.com/redirect/57a6182a-e54c-41a3-a640-9118c0fd3dcc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on [Unsplash](https://substack.com/redirect/4963ec95-ca5d-491c-91be-d2e4e82eb7a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
For most of history, people living with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and related neurological disorders have faced a grim outlook for their ability to communicate. ALS, which [attacks](https://substack.com/redirect/7c427aa3-2f2f-4b00-b9ed-9c89f290e28d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the nerve cells responsible for carrying signals from the brain to the muscles necessary for speech, can make speech slurred, difficult to understand, and eventually impossible for some patients. Over the past several decades, modern assistive communication technology has made major strides toward enabling people with ALS to communicate, but the technology has fallen short of reproducing the ease and spontaneity of natural communication. An experimental AI-powered tool is changing that.
A new AI-powered brain-computer interface (BCI) system [developed](https://substack.com/redirect/3b4fb359-c46c-46a3-a3ba-1d951b572125?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at UC Davis in collaboration with researchers at Brown University and Mass General Brigham Neuroscience Institute appears to represent a major breakthrough in addressing two of the "key challenges" to the real-world adoption of this emerging BCI technology: independent at-home use and reliable long-term performance. A BCI is a system that measures brain activity and translates it into commands for an external device without relying on muscle movements normally required to operate a computer.
The Compute Optimist is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cudGhlY29tcHV0ZW9wdGltaXN0LmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.OGzQ2TtQWIs5qFXeawb5rlXZLLcN17lj-QznUu_OOeY?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=214739812)
What does this breakthrough mean for the everyday lives of ALS patients experiencing severe paralysis? A significant leap toward independence and more natural communication.
The latest BCI breakthrough enabled study participant Casey Harrell to communicate substantially more independently than before, with the study documenting more than 3,800 hours of at-home use. And while a caregiver helped set up the system, at-home use was not dependent on the researcher supervision his earlier BCI use required. This allows for sustained and far more natural communication with friends, family, and colleagues. The BCI also enabled him to control a computer cursor, allowing him to navigate the internet, send messages, and perform work-related tasks. Together, these capabilities allow Harrell to participate considerably more independently in family life and work.
Using a 125,000-word vocabulary, the BCI demonstrated 99.2 percent word accuracy in a controlled word-copying task, according to a [new June 2026 study](https://substack.com/redirect/3b4fb359-c46c-46a3-a3ba-1d951b572125?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). And the pace of this innovation is difficult to overstate. Two earlier studies, one published in [August 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/8e896689-07de-4587-8581-e1cd057399e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with the same participant and the other in [August 2023](https://substack.com/redirect/7940f998-35f0-4b53-be2f-357ca96768ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) involving a different participant, reported 97.5 percent word accuracy and a 23.8 percent word error rate, respectively, under different testing conditions.
In the June 2026 study, Harrell communicated at an average of [56 words per minute (WPM)](https://substack.com/redirect/3de78196-593e-49e1-aa99-cd345b5883aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) using a BCI, compared with roughly [6.3 WPM](https://substack.com/redirect/21ac12fa-846b-4076-ae72-c539172124d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) using head-controlled typing, as documented in an earlier study. For context, conversational English is roughly [160 WPM](https://substack.com/redirect/21ac12fa-846b-4076-ae72-c539172124d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). And while this remains substantially slower than conversational English, it represents a meaningful jump over less than three years.
From a technical standpoint, this BCI works by using implanted electrodes--tiny sensors that record electrical activity in the brain--to send those recordings to AI decoding software capable of translating those signals into text. From there, those words can be displayed or played aloud. This is a break from traditional assistive systems that rely on things like movements of the eyes, head, and other parts of the body to select words and letters.
Recent AI-powered advancements in BCI technology do not stop at helping users communicate with greater speed, accuracy, and independence. Another experimental approach is pushing the boundaries of restoring natural-feeling communication, translating brain activity not only into words, but tone, emphasis, and even _song_. And it's doing so in real time.
Harrell also participated in a [study](https://substack.com/redirect/e983ad10-68c6-4aaa-9201-b6acaf4a2c15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) involving a brain-to-voice BCI, published in June 2025. While both BCIs use brain signals, this system goes beyond translating attempted speech into text, seeking to restore the expressiveness of natural speech. The study's results suggest the future of communication for ALS patients could look remarkably different.
To make this possible, the researchers developed what the report calls a "real-time neural decoding pipeline" capable of synthesizing voice from incoming neural signals in under 10 milliseconds as a person attempts to speak. In other words, instead of waiting for an entire word or sentence to be decoded before generating speech, this model enables near-instantaneous speech synthesis more closely resembling the natural flow of speech.
In this study, researchers developed an AI-generated voice resembling Harrell's [using](https://substack.com/redirect/36089463-b940-42aa-9035-6b8fdcd2cc5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) recordings of him speaking before ALS had severely impaired his speech. The BCI's neural decoder--AI software that translates brain activity into information used to synthesize speech--allowed the system to produce speech from his attempted vocalizations.
The BCI also demonstrated success in reproducing his intended intonation. When he intended to ask a question, for example, the BCI reproduced the rising pitch associated with asking that question.
And this BCI demonstrated the ability to reproduce intended emphasis on words, too. Think about the difference in meaning between "I didn't say _she_ stole the money" and "I didn't say she _stole_ the money." Emphasis may appear to be a small thing on the surface but can go a long way toward making day-to-day communication feel normal again.
And this study's BCI takes speech restoration yet another step further, reproducing musical pitch. Harrell attempted to sing short melodies consisting of six or seven notes and successfully alternated between pitches classified as low, medium, and high.
The latter BCI study illustrates what is already being made possible by AI-powered research: real-time speech synthesis, intonation, emphasis, and even melody. In controlled trials, the system reproduced intended question intonation with 90.5 percent accuracy and intended word emphasis with 95.7 percent accuracy. Researchers also tested how well human listeners could distinguish musical pitches and understand the speech synthesized by the BCI.
When asked to identify which note was higher in 189 pairs of synthesized notes, listeners chose correctly 73.02 percent of the time, on average. When asked to identify the correct transcript of synthesized speech from six written sentence options, listeners chose correctly 94.34 percent of the time. Still, these results carry limitations.
Listeners were also asked to transcribe both the synthesized and unaided speech. Transcription, however, is a more demanding measure of intelligibility than choosing from six sentences. The median word error rate for the synthesized speech was 43.75 percent. And while this is a substantially lower error rate than when listeners were asked to transcribe Harrell's unaided speech (96.43 percent), it remains a ways off from restoring natural conversation. These limitations underscore that while AI is already transforming communication for people living with ALS, accelerating research and innovation could bring us closer to restoring the flow of natural conversation and making these life-changing technologies widely available.
"I do not want to be special any longer," Harrell wrote in a first-person account published by _[Springer Nature](https://substack.com/redirect/e9952e75-80fc-4be2-a82a-b501c05dc56e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_. "I think this is good enough technology that people who have ALS should have access to it right now. Sadly, that is not the case yet." Sergey Stavisky, a neuroscientist at UC Davis who helped lead the BCI research, is optimistic about the future. He told _[Time](https://substack.com/redirect/7060f587-79f7-443e-852c-0be5a3127233?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , "I think motor-speech BCIs will be widely available."
For patients living with ALS, advancements in AI and related emerging technologies are not merely about economic growth or productivity gains. They are about the promise of being able to communicate _ordinarily_ again. And recent advancements in BCI technology illustrate both what AI is already making possible and what it can make possible if we keep going.
Harrell hopes to no longer be an exceptional case study, but one of many regaining the ability to communicate naturally, including those who may have believed they never would. Throughout history, extraordinary technological achievements have transformed what once seemed impossible into the commonplace. With enough research and innovation, Harrell's dream may soon be in reach.

HI EVERYONE,

Get out the Vote Season is Here!

Early voting is now open and we are excited to launch our get out the vote effort. Join us for countless volunteer events across
the state! Every call and every knock brings us closer to an Election Night Victory on November 3rd. We hope you'll join our
effort!

Even if you can't make it to an event, you can always help from home! Calls can be done from anywhere you have Wi-Fi or cell
service, and our app allows you to always see houses near you to knock.

Introducing LinkUp: Text Your Friends to Get Out the Vote

We're excited to launch LinkUp, a new Right Insight feature that lets you personally text your friends and contacts. A message
from someone they know and trust is one of the most powerful ways to get people to the polls.

How to get started:

1. Log in to Right Insight and tap LinkUp at the bottom of your screen.

2. Tap Sync in the top right corner to upload your contacts. Give it a moment to load.

3. You'll now see your contacts, along with their voter registration status and how they're voting.

4. Tap a contact you'd like to message.

5. If you have more than one number for that person, select the right phone number.

6. Set your organization to Minnesota Republican Party.

7. Choose a pre-written message template, or type your own, then tap Send Message.

Texts go out directly from your phone, so your friends see a message from you, just like any other text.

Join the push. Reach out to your friends, remind them to vote, and help our Republican candidates win.

subject: From the Campaign Trail: A Few Lessons Learned
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Maria Jukic
body:
From an unexpected primary win to new friendships and lessons learned along the way. What a journey it's been!

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1C8teKJOQlP?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Hi friend,

Everywhere I go across Ohio's 14th District, I'm reminded of something important: people care deeply about their communities, their families, and their future.
From living rooms and coffee shops to county fairs and community gatherings, I've met some incredible people.
I've heard your concerns about the cost of living, healthcare, Social Security, protecting our communities, and what the future holds for the next generation.And I've heard something else, too. People are ready for change.
Along the way, I've learned a few things myself. Here are two moments that have stayed with me.
###
---
|
---
| |

**Lesson One: Expect the unexpected.**
When I decided to run for Congress, I knew I was taking on a challenge. But winning the Democratic primary with more than 50% of the vote surprised just about everyone — including my supporters, people in the Democratic Party, and, if I'm being completely candid, me.
Election night was one of those moments I'll never forget.
It was also the beginning of a much bigger journey. One that would have me criss-cross six counties and thousands of miles, introduce me to people I might never otherwise have met, and teach me things I couldn't have learned any other way.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/17InK8VwCpR?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
| | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/wwYQVL5cgTm?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
| [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/SQxruTv5qkA?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
|
---
| |

**Lesson Two: We’re not alone in wanting change.**

One of the highlights of this journey was attending the National Courage & Accountability Summit in Washington, D.C.
I met people from across the country who, like me, have a fire in their bellies and a genuine desire to make life better for the people they hope to represent. We came from different places, with different stories, but shared a determination to make a difference.
We also heard from leaders who had once stood in our shoes. Their message was simple: keep working hard, be brave, stay true to yourself, and keep sharing your message.
It was exactly the shot in the arm I needed heading into the final stretch of this campaign.
And it reminded me of something important: none of us has to have all the answers when we begin. We just have to be willing to listen, learn, work together, and keep showing up.

Somewhere in California's Central Valley right now, there are miles of elevated concrete viaducts standing over almond orchards like the aqueducts of a civilization that left. They carry nothing. They connect nothing. Under them is the most expensive unfinished thing in America: California high-speed rail, seventeen-plus years after voters approved it, roughly $15 billion spent, and -- per the federal government's own tally -- not one inch of high-speed track laid and not one train set purchased.
Put it next to the two most famous boondoggles in American history and you get a clean lesson in how government waste evolves. It got smarter...

They carry nothing. They connect nothing. Under them is the most expensive unfinished thing in America: California high-speed rail, seventeen-plus years after voters approved it, roughly $15 billion spent, and -- per the federal government's own tally -- not one inch of high-speed track laid and not one train set purchased. We have troubling news out of Michigan, where Democrats face critical elections this fall, chief among them the U.S. Senate race and the race for the state Supreme Court.
In the MI Supreme Court race, two pro-democracy justices, Megan Cavanagh and Noah Hood, are up for reelection. Both are facing competitive races against MAGA-backed challengers.
Democrats cannot afford to lose these races.
But voter turnout in traditionally Trump dominated territory has surged in the state, narrowing Democrat's projected early vote lead with less than 3 weeks left until election day.

We won't sugarcoat it. This could spell doom for Democrats.
Just last week, Defend Our Courts began contacting thousands of Democratic voters in Michigan. And the conversations we've been having with voters have also been concerning.
While many of the voters we reached are fired up about voting for Dems, a lot of them do not know who the Dem endorsed Supreme Court candidates are, or that a Supreme Court election is even happening.
That's terrible news. Michigan's Supreme Court elections are nonpartisan. There will be no party affiliation listed next to the names on the ballot. If voters don't know who to vote for, they could inadvertently vote for MAGA's candidates.
All of this is creating a perfect storm that could capsize the Dem's blue wave in November. At a time when Dem voter turnout in Michigan needs to increase substantially to stave off MAGA's surge, these voters don't know who to vote for.
This is the exact scenario that cost Democrats in Georgia's nonpartisan Supreme Court races earlier this year. A last-minute surge in turnout produced an electorate that leaned Democratic by eight points. Yet the Democrat-backed candidates still lost, because too many Dems voted for the wrong candidates.
We can't let that happen in Michigan. Right now, our team has identified over 400,000 Democrats we need to contact between now and election day. We've reached less than a quarter of them so far.
To reach everyone before election day, we need to double our efforts. And that means doubling our budget too. But we don't have the resources to do that at the moment. That's why we're sending an urgent plea to Democrats everywhere today:

subject: Did you see Marilyn's message? Your ballot is on its way!

body:
Here's what to do when your ballot arrives.

---
| | Starting today, ballots are going out to every registered voter in Washington. Yours should arrive in the next few days.

When it does, I am asking you to do one thing: **Vote and drop it in a drop box!**

In this year's August primary, Thurston County Auditor Mary Hall reported that _70 valid ballots arrived after the certification deadline._ One took 19 days to be returned.

**Those voters did everything right, and their votes still did not count.**

Pierce County Auditor Linda Farmer put it plainly: there is "no guarantee that your ballot will be there on time."

**Voting is a fundamental right. It is not a privilege and it should not depend on how fast the mail moves. Using an official drop box takes that risk off the table.**
| [FIND AN OFFICIAL BALLOT DROP BOX](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141577709/654018888/76405339?refcode=MS_EM_FR_90DO_261016_1_1&refcode2=95594b01-a0c9-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTQ0OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NTU5NGIwMS1hMGM5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=TK-6d8lzNsl91b7G4EclbHcVBpYbMyEvivqHrLip9zU=&emci=cbb5857e-9fc9-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=95594b01-a0c9-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=54355765)

subject: Years in power. Look at the results.

body:
Florida deserves better than this.
| Friend, Angie Nixon here.

Republicans have controlled Florida for years, and they cannot hold that much power while pretending they bear no responsibility for what working families are experiencing: grocery bills that keep climbing, rent and insurance eating up paychecks, childcare families can't afford, and healthcare that costs too much.

[Can you split $10 between the Voter Protection Project and me right now, with Election Day closing in, to help change that in November?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/138773?t=6&akid=30174%2E878179%2EKNmSgi) | [CHIP IN $10 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/138773?t=7&akid=30174%2E878179%2EKNmSgi)
---
Here's what Republicans understand about me, and why it scares them. I just shocked the political establishment by winning the Democratic nomination despite being dramatically outspent, proving that people-powered organizing can beat big money.

I'm a working-class Black woman who isn't going to Washington to protect wealthy donors or preserve the status quo. I've been clear about why I'm running: I want government to work for working people instead of the wealthy and powerful interests that have dominated Washington and Tallahassee.

The wealthy and powerful keep getting richer while working people are told to make do with less. This campaign exists to ask the question at the center of this race: who is the government working for, the people working to pay the bills, or the wealthy few writing the checks?

[Can you split $10, $25, or whatever you can between the Voter Protection Project and me right now, with Election Day closing in, to help keep building a campaign that answers to voters?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/138773?t=8&akid=30174%2E878179%2EKNmSgi)
[DONATE »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/138773?t=9&akid=30174%2E878179%2EKNmSgi)
---
Their track record got us here. Let's give Florida a different one.

In solidarity,
**Angie Nixon**
Democratic Nominee, Florida U.S. Senate

[](https://substack.com/redirect/7380f14b-0c31-4c8b-be8c-fb96102cd353?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
For those of us who are not disabled, understanding what it's like to be a disabled person, is an abstract concept rather than a practical reality.
I have seen, examined and treated many patients with disabilities. Yet until I broke my leg I never walked in their shoes and never experienced first hand what it is like to have limited mobility.
Thanks for reading The Goldstein Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..vh1ulbL1wT3GC2Z06XftDe7Bt0c5g47okfY-kYqn4EM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=220423071)
I shared my own experience of temporarily disability when I broke my leg in 2020. Initially I couldn't bear weight on my leg. I began with crutches, and then later, moved up to a knee scooter. Getting up and down stairs was a challenge. I learned how to hop up and downstairs with a crutch in one hand, and holding onto a banister with the other. It was the only way I could get up and down the stairs of my house. Because my house is parked on a hill, I have to go up the equivalent of 2 flights of stairs to get to my bedroom.
I navigated the busy streets of New York City to get to my office and on one occasion when going up and down the carve outs in the sidewalk the front wheel of the scooter got stuck and I went flying to the ground. It was very humbling to have strangers help pick me up.
I traveled around supermarkets on an knee scooter, and sometimes used an electric wheelchair. Electric wheelchairs get you around the supermarket. However, some of the shells are too high for you to reach. Bathing is also difficult or not normal for people with disabilities, and they need special accommodations just in order to bathe.
Those who listened understood that for a short while I lived in their shoes and understood the problems. I will never forget my temporary disability experience. It taught me first hand what disabled people have to experience, not on a temporary basis but as permanent one.
I admire the courage that people with disabilities have and respect their strong desires to persevere and remain productive members of our society.
If you see a person in a wheelchair in a supermarket trying to reach for something on the shelves that appears to be out of reach offer them a hand.

| **Math Matters, Vol. 2: A Public Bank? **
**Another _Not_ New Idea with No Math from “Economist” Amanda Janoo ** **_Longtime Democratic State Treasurer Says it’s an “undue risk”_** Part of Amanda Janoo’s “post-growth” economic plan for Vermont is to “create a Vermont Public Bank.”

**Like most of her ideas, a public bank has been proposed, studied, and ultimately discarded as an unaffordable experiment for Vermont ... by Democrats. **

**Here is what former State Treasurer (2011-2023), Beth Pearce (a Democrat),[had to say about a Vermont Public Bank proposal back in 2014](https://us.list-manage.com/NlMZbDHMSUL?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c "https://legislature.vermont.gov/Documents/2014/WorkGroups/Senate%20Finance/Bills/S.204/Witness%20Testimony/S.204~Beth%20Pearce~Memo%20to%20Senate%20Committee%20on%20Government%20Operations~3-18-2014.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com"): **

Treasurer Pierce said a state bank is an “undue risk” to the State’s bond rating; and that damaging Vermont's bond rating would negatively affect the cost of housing, higher education, commercial development and energy projects. She concluded: [“I don't want to put that at risk.](https://us.list-manage.com/OzjBp08_yuA?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c "https://www.pressherald.com/2014/02/28/vermonters_being_asked_to_back_public_bank_/?utm_source=chatgpt.com?copylink=true")”

Treasurer Pearce continued: “**Any losses associated with a state bank's portfolio would ultimately be borne by the taxpayers of Vermont.”** And “the state would be holding onto a higher risk portfolio.”

And then politely concludes, “The presumption that a state bank is the solution to something is premature.”

At 12 years, Beth Pearce is the 6th longest serving State Treasurer in Vermont history. She won reelection handily with some of the widest margins on record.

**But you don’t have to just take her (very experienced) word for it. **

A[ UVM study also determined a public bank would cost Vermont taxpayers - 12 years ago - between $35 million and $70 million](https://us.list-manage.com/dKq3ugSr8ah?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c "https://publicbanking.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/public-banking-1-13-2014.pdf") in startup costs. Adjusted for inflation, a public bank of similar scale would cost taxpayers** _between $50 million and $100 million, just to get it on its feet._**.

Financial experts – and a former Democratic State Treasurer – have studied her policies and determined they’re not good for Vermonters or Vermont’s economy.

**They conclude its high-cost and high-risk. **

In contrast, Governor Scott’s economic vision is workable and affordable. For example, the Governor's proposal (which passed earlier this year) for the [Community and Housing Infrastructure Program (CHIP)](https://us.list-manage.com/RjfwH9B3LGF?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c "https://accd.vermont.gov/press-releases/governor-phil-scott-announces-launch-community-and-housing-infrastructure-program"). This initiative will unlock up to $2 billion in infrastructure investment by 2035, supporting water, sewer, roads, and other improvements necessary for housing.

Additionally, the Vermont Economic Development Authority (VEDA) can now partner with private lenders to finance housing projects of five or more units, helping create more housing.

Experimental proposals where all the risk and financing is on the backs of Vermont’s already over-taxed taxpayers, is not how you grow the economy or make Vermont more affordable. And in the words of one experienced Democratic State Treasurer, it’s an “undue risk” to our economic security.

| | | | JoCasta Zamarripa is a lifelong Milwaukeean, a proud daughter of the city’s south side, and a dedicated public servant who’s never stopped fighting for working people. Born and raised in the very neighborhoods she now represents, JoCasta has spent her life pushing for progress that reflects the realities of everyday Wisconsinites.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/IyeJOuFCODX?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

She made history as the first Latina and first openly bi member of both the Wisconsin State Legislature and the Milwaukee Common Council. But JoCasta’s leadership is defined by more than her historic firsts—it's grounded in results. She served ten years in the State Assembly and is now in her second term as Alderperson for Milwaukee’s 8th District, where she’s led major efforts on affordable housing, small business licensing reform, and community development.

In 2025, she was the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan, a key step in addressing Milwaukee’s housing crisis by expanding affordable options and preventing displacement. Her approach is practical and persistent—building coalitions, navigating political challenges, and staying rooted in the neighborhoods she serves.

Now, JoCasta is running as a Democrat for Wisconsin Secretary of State to use the platform to fight for what matters: more funding for our schools so families aren’t forced into referenda every election, real housing relief for working people, and affordable child care that lets parents breathe.

clean_body: | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hello Peter, I wanted to give you a quick update, because you deserve to know where things stand. This morning, I asked for your help ordering our Election Day yard signs and buying stamps for our volunteers' handwritten postcards. So many of you answered, and I am truly grateful. Every gift, every roll of stamps, and every kind word reminds me why we are in this fight together. But I have to be honest with you: we are still $4,028 short. Our sign order has to go in tonight so the signs arrive before Election Day on Tuesday, November 3. If we come up short, we will have to order fewer signs, and that means fewer yards, fewer street corners, and fewer polling places where our neighbors see that this campaign is theirs. Here's the good news: if just 81 of us give $50, we'll get there. If you can give $25, you'll cover half a share. And if you can give $100, you'll carry two. Will you help us close the gap before midnight tonight? | | | And if you'd rather help with our postcards, you can still donate a roll of Forever stamps. Give us a call, we will pick them up! Or, you can mail them to: Committee to Elect Enoch P.O. Box 1362 West Chester, OH 45071 We have come this far because of people like you. Let's finish today strong, together. With gratitude and hope, Vanessa EnochDemocratic Candidate for Congress, Ohio's 8th District P.S. If you already gave today, thank you from the bottom of my heart. Would you forward this email to one friend who might chip in? That one share could put another sign in the ground. | | | | | | | We have to place our yard sign order today. Sign printers need time to produce and ship, and if we wait even a few more days, we risk our signs arriving after voters have already made up their minds. Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, just 18 days away, and every yard, every corner, and every polling place without a sign is a missed chance to remind our neighbors that real change is on the ballot. | | | Donate now and note "stamps" if you'd like. A roll of stamps are $65. Two rolls are $130. We need thousands. Hi Pro-Life Friend,

As election day nears, James Talarico is letting his "moderate" mask slip.

When asked at a recent campaign event who his favorite drag queen was, he didn't miss a beat - instantly rattling "their" name off like he'd been asked his favorite color.

That video has gone viral online, racking up millions of views on social media.

Talarico has spent this entire campaign trying to sell Texas voters on a moderate, Bible-quoting version of himself, and videos like this are the LAST thing Talarico's campaign wants getting out to Texas voters.

Texas voters outside Austin won't buy his facade, not once they see the real Talarico instead of the campaign-trail version.

And right now in Michigan, Democrat U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is running the same playbook, holding town halls in Lansing, Grand Rapids, Detroit, Flint, and Macomb, hoping moderate suburban voters forget he wants abortion legal through all nine months.

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I'm the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement.

Dear Pro-Life Friend, here's my problem.

You and I can't rely on the national media to tell the truth about these politicians' abortion extremism.

So it's up to grassroots folks like you and me to hold them accountable.
That's exactly what I want to do with my rapid response counter-protests at as many candidate events as possible in our targeted races.

[Will you please chip in right now to keep our rapid response team ready to move the moment we get word of the next public event](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=605d400a92444941b695f095370d5000&_e=-sSkIL_jY3xBNRGd1FT0PHdBzs12VVpSM2T6P5efHWPsXKnCaIuD9wk-p1Sz79_T7gUH8aJe4mEiSwPpwqlIYK0Ze0kfXXneWYiiDRfBHS_B4me4VZprX-f0O2IIPB2yTcQ3kwaUHjS-WfEhQhLCT3KlQBNv9uUkliigZMsE4Qey3zcVm240flTi9d7szZ720fb3J_F6cJZ-IDzetsNGRgw53ksOIt3iDQxg18aZfo5ISpeWj74Fo7XaLoTMHAxVD0iY2Viw8tyFye3rWBJbCAnoXQypPPU5BLPBhxdQ9WQKlon6dBkLdznoGSAKKIvoUujZeqf8szKirLfhWRFzQXFbjJtj-BivzK8RZKOmD-e_6RC9od0NkqEam4hPPWF9kPOSDkqjbawLkS4NlCxCny9V-y60tcM1_AdJZBuk688UN6UGTU67SRiG8HMaIohYMfgDFSjIEzrFYhLSN8lQAZj_PGGgJHGU96G3dI3NqOdeK3FOj7qqyVBX7euZuhhZmwlnVv7yxjMjnyAjuwUAcMnt3qhdQfeBMdVX7-wBCbbp_xdbE6p5HzFbo3mv1p37IvMQ2Fn8SpgoeMpSb4vJaPzzYu9lDQux0u36laTnTlnF1o2h3ToXNIMFX_ovkPtbTaAvY8lAIRGSAz4oYGN_mw%3D%3D)**?**

Last month, our Pro-Life Generation activists launched the first stop of a 100-church flyering campaign at a church right in Talarico's back yard.

Then, when he spoke at Baylor University - a Baptist school - our team was on the ground to ensure attendees heard the truth about his anti-Biblical, pro-abortion stance.

Do you remember, back in 2024, when our students walked into a Kamala Harris rally in Wisconsin, held up a cross, and got mocked from the stage for it?

A video went viral of Kamala on stage, talking about abortion "rights" and overturning Roe v. Wade, denouncing Christians who said "Christ is King," and responding to our students with "You guys are at the wrong rally."

I've seen it time and time again.

These are exactly the moments on the campaign trail that can swing an entire election.

One month from today, on Tuesday, November 3rd, voters across the nation will decide who controls Congress for the next two years - and who has the momentum heading into the critical 2028 presidential cycle.

Talarico, El-Sayed, and all pro-abortion politicians know a camera catching them off-script is worth more than any ad buy. That's exactly why they're not publishing their schedules more than a day or two out.

So my team has to be ready before they announce, not after.

That means canvassers who can redirect on short notice and students who'll show up with signs and cameras of their own.

None of that comes free, and none of it waits for a fundraising deadline.

clean_body: Hi Pro-Life Friend, As election day nears, James Talarico is letting his "moderate" mask slip. When asked at a recent campaign event who his favorite drag queen was, he didn't miss a beat - instantly rattling "their" name off like he'd been asked his favorite color. That video has gone viral online, racking up millions of views on social media. Talarico has spent this entire campaign trying to sell Texas voters on a moderate, Bible-quoting version of himself, and videos like this are the LAST thing Talarico's campaign wants getting out to Texas voters. Texas voters outside Austin won't buy his facade, not once they see the real Talarico instead of the campaign-trail version. And right now in Michigan, Democrat U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is running the same playbook, holding town halls in Lansing, Grand Rapids, Detroit, Flint, and Macomb, hoping moderate suburban voters forget he wants abortion legal through all nine months. My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I'm the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement. Dear Pro-Life Friend, here's my problem. You and I can't rely on the national media to tell the truth about these politicians' abortion extremism. So it's up to grassroots folks like you and me to hold them accountable. That's exactly what I want to do with my rapid response counter-protests at as many candidate events as possible in our targeted races. ? Last month, our Pro-Life Generation activists launched the first stop of a 100-church flyering campaign at a church right in Talarico's back yard. Then, when he spoke at Baylor University - a Baptist school - our team was on the ground to ensure attendees heard the truth about his anti-Biblical, pro-abortion stance. Do you remember, back in 2024, when our students walked into a Kamala Harris rally in Wisconsin, held up a cross, and got mocked from the stage for it? A video went viral of Kamala on stage, talking about abortion "rights" and overturning Roe v. Wade, denouncing Christians who said "Christ is King," and responding to our students with "You guys are at the wrong rally." I've seen it time and time again. These are exactly the moments on the campaign trail that can swing an entire election. One month from today, on Tuesday, November 3rd, voters across the nation will decide who controls Congress for the next two years - and who has the momentum heading into the critical 2028 presidential cycle. Talarico, El-Sayed, and all pro-abortion politicians know a camera catching them off-script is worth more than any ad buy. At Trump's rally in Ohio, a woman stood up wearing a shirt that said _" Release the Epstein Files." _ The men around her shoved her, pulled her hair, and punched her in the face while the crowd chanted _" USA."_

Police escorted her out.
The man who hit her kept his seat and collected high-fives.
And from the stage, a convicted felon president found legally liable for sexual abuse called her scum and mocked her.
American values have never once looked like a pack of grown men throwing fists at one woman standing alone.
That is among the most vile and gutless things a man can do, and an entire section applauded it.
That woman is a patriot in every sense of the word.
She rose in a stadium full of people who despised her, demanding justice for trafficked children, and showed more courage in that moment than every man who swung at her will muster in a lifetime.

That awful scene all flowed downhill from the cowards in charge.
Trump attacks women by reflex, mocking everything from their looks to their intelligence.
Hegseth fired women officers who outranked him in experience, judgment, and honor, because nothing terrifies a small man like a woman who has done more than him.
Keith Self pushes the SAVE Act, which could shut millions of American women out of the voting booth over a married name.
As a veteran, I have watched men be brave, and it looks nothing like that arena.
The men in that video wear patriotism as a costume.
That stadium was packed with camo hats and t-shirts about defending this country, faith, family, women, and children.
Then a woman stood alone in front of them, their promise got its test, and every one of them failed it by joining the mob.
If anything from this extremist movement endures, it will endure as a warning.
That is what became of the photographs of bigots screaming at children integrating schools, and of the crowds who posed, smiling, outside lynchings.
History keeps those images as a record of how low Americans once sank and a vow never to sink there again.
That disgusting rally footage should join the same shameful archive.
In just 18 days, the rest of us hold the power to decide what comes next.

* * *
There was a fascinating new poll from Fox News yesterday. It showed that the number one issue in America today isn't the economy. It isn't this illegal war in Iran. It's not immigration. It's corruption.
After nearly two years of the most corrupt administration in American history, the issue I believe sits at the root of everything fundamentally broken in this country has blasted through the door. It's now top of mind for the overwhelming majority of Americans.
And it's not hard to see why. The president of the United States took a $400 million luxury jet from the government of Qatar. He launched his own meme coin and then auctioned off a private dinner with himself to the people who bought the most of it. His family has turned the White House into a business development office, cutting crypto deals and foreign deals while the rest of us are told to tighten our belts. And his administration is stuffed with incompetent sycophants doing favors for friends like Kimberly Guilfoyle, the former Ambassador to Greece.
That's just what we know. The stories we remember, the ones we've already forgotten, and the ones we still haven't heard about. Honestly, the things I don't know about are what keep me up at night.
This is Banana Republic corruption. And people are pissed.
They understand that their lives are materially worse since Donald Trump took office because of the corruption and criminality in Washington. The economy is bad because of corruption. The war is spiraling out of control because of corruption. Your life is worse because of corruption.
