* * *
Democrats, rightly, are closing their arguments in this election with a killer instinct. Brutal ads tying Republican candidates in every state and every district to the corruption inside this administration. If there's any justice in this world, the American people will punish Republicans for sitting on their hands while Donald Trump and his family stole from them.
But punishing Republicans at the ballot box isn't the same thing as accountability. And accountability is the thing this country has forgotten how to deliver.
Think about everything that's happened in my lifetime.
Did anybody really go to prison for Iran-Contra? No.
Did anybody go to jail for the 2008 financial crisis that ruined so many lives? No.
Did anybody go to prison for the January 6th insurrection? They did. And then Donald Trump sprang them.
Is anybody going to go to prison for all the crimes Trump, his family, and his administration have committed? I worry the answer is no.
And if the answer keeps being no -- if we keep asking people to participate in a democracy where the powerful, the wealthy, and the well-connected are never held accountable because of who they know and how much money they can slip into the back pocket of the right politician -- then why would anyone engage in that democracy?
When people say politics isn't for them, that they don't give a damn, that nothing ever changes, that nobody's fighting for them, that their vote can't make a difference, this is what they're talking about.
So I have a warning for the Democratic Party, which I believe is on the precipice of winning the House and the Senate, and potentially the White House in 2028 if we nominate a candidate who can rise to the moment.
You have to stamp this out. Not with a strongly worded press release. With action.
That means a real investigation into everything this administration has done, run by prosecutors who aren't afraid of who they're investigating, with the full power to follow the money wherever it leads. It means banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks, period. It means no more handing ambassadorships and cabinet posts to the highest bidder. And it means putting teeth back into the ethics laws Trump spent the last two years laughing at, so the next guy can't do it again.
And yes, that includes the corruption inside our own party.
The Epstein files were never a partisan issue. There are plenty of Democrats in there. Congressional insider trading isn't a partisan issue either. Lots of Democrats do it, including a lot of Democrats I like and respect. The self-dealing, the donors getting ambassadorships, all of it happens in both parties.
Now let me be clear: I am not both-sidesing this. Donald Trump is far and away the most corrupt president we've ever seen, and his family is out of control. Comparing the rest of it to Trump is like comparing a hot day in Arizona to the surface of the goddamn sun.
That doesn't make it right.
Trump has thrived in an environment where people fundamentally believe every politician is corrupt. And it's hard to argue with the average American who thinks nobody is fighting for them, when the system is this broken and nobody seems willing to make the hard decisions to fix it.
For all the insider trading, all the corruption, all the grift inside this movement, a lot of people have had to turn a blind eye. A lot of people have had to say it doesn't matter. A lot of strategists have said, "Well, we can't focus on that right now, we have to stay focused on the economy."
Well, the message has broken through. And it's a generational opportunity for the next president of the United States to become a historic figure. To pass historic reform. To bring accountability and gravity back to American politics and society.
What an incredible opportunity to show people the system can work. By actually making it work. By bending it to our will and fixing these problems. Do that, and we'll pull in more people from the sidelines than we've seen in generations.
We can do it if the right person steps up in 2028, and if Democrats in Congress and across this country are prepared to do the work. Not out of petty grievance because Republicans were mean to us and hurt people while Trump was in power. Because it's the right goddamn thing to do.
It could set this country on a new path in a way most people don't yet understand.

Each of these candidates has the background, experience, and drive to win, and your donation will make a critical difference.
**Zach Dembo:** Zach is a Navy veteran, former federal prosecutor, and ninth-generation Kentuckian running in **Kentucky's 6th Congressional District.** He served as a Navy JAG officer, prosecuted civil rights violations at the Justice Department, and worked as a senior adviser to Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear. When he saw the Trump administration politicizing the Justice Department, he resigned rather than compromise his principles. Zach has deep roots in Kentucky, a lifetime of public service, and the courage to stand up for what's right. That's exactly the kind of leader who can win over voters in a tough Republican district.
**Nancy Lacore:** Nancy is a retired three-star Navy admiral running in **South Carolina's 1st Congressional District.** She served our country for 35 years, beginning as a helicopter pilot and eventually becoming Chief of Navy Reserve, where she led more than 60,000 sailors. She also deployed to Afghanistan and Djibouti, raised six children, and founded a nonprofit honoring women killed in action. As a fellow veteran, I have enormous respect for her service. Nancy has spent her life putting country before politics, and I believe that record of leadership gives her a real opportunity to win over voters who are tired of the dysfunction in Washington.
**Blake Gendebien:** Blake is a second-generation dairy farmer, small business owner, and father of three running in **New York's 21st Congressional District.** Born and raised in the North Country, Blake has spent decades running his family's dairy farm, served on his local school board, and co-founded a nonprofit supporting families battling pediatric cancer. He's not a career politician. He's a hardworking New Yorker who understands the challenges facing the people he wants to represent. And he's proving he can win: a new Siena poll has him leading his Republican opponent 46% to 42% in a district Republicans have held for more than a decade.
**Bale Dalton:** Bale is a Navy veteran and former NASA Chief of Staff running in **Florida's 7th Congressional District.** He served 24 years in the Navy and Navy Reserve, including 13 years on active duty, and commanded a special operations support helicopter squadron. He went on to serve as Chief of Staff at NASA, helping lead one of the most important scientific agencies in the world. Bale has spent his career putting service above self, and I believe his experience, integrity, and commitment to getting things done give him a real shot at flipping this Central Florida seat.
**Leela Gray:** Leela is a retired Army brigadier general, business leader, and third-generation veteran running in **Florida's 13th Congressional District.** She served 30 years in uniform, including three deployments, and rose to become Deputy Commanding General of U.S. Army Central. Alongside her military service, Leela built a career in technology and communications, and became a lawyer to help veterans access the benefits they've earned. Now, she's running for Congress with a focus on lowering costs for working families, particularly the skyrocketing insurance premiums facing Florida homeowners.
So I’m about to ask you for support, but not just for me. Instead, I’m asking you to support five patriots running in some of the most competitive, toss-up districts in the country.

And he's proving he can win: a new Siena poll has him leading his Republican opponent 46% to 42% in a district Republicans have held for more than a decade. Bale Dalton: Bale is a Navy veteran and former NASA Chief of Staff running in Florida's 7th Congressional District. He served 24 years in the Navy and Navy Reserve, including 13 years on active duty, and commanded a special operations support helicopter squadron. He went on to serve as Chief of Staff at NASA, helping lead one of the most important scientific agencies in the world. Bale has spent his career putting service above self, and I believe his experience, integrity, and commitment to getting things done give him a real shot at flipping this Central Florida seat. Leela Gray: Leela is a retired Army brigadier general, business leader, and third-generation veteran running in Florida's 13th Congressional District. She served 30 years in uniform, including three deployments, and rose to become Deputy Commanding General of U.S. Army Central. Alongside her military service, Leela built a career in technology and communications, and became a lawyer to help veterans access the benefits they've earned. Now, she's running for Congress with a focus on lowering costs for working families, particularly the skyrocketing insurance premiums facing Florida homeowners. So I’m about to ask you for support, but not just for me. Instead, I’m asking you to support five patriots running in some of the most competitive, toss-up districts in the country. These five leaders embody the movement we’ve been building. They’re pragmatic, pugilistic, and patriotic. They’re smart, hungry, and ready to get the job done and win. = | = Team, I believe in these five patriots. And I believe that if we give them the resources they need to get their message out, they can win. But with just a few days until Election Day, they need our help right now. = | = Let's go win this thing. Pat Pat Ryan for Congress P.O. Tom Shattuck, Steve Robinson, Jon Fetherston and Seamus Othot cover Troy Jackson's debate blowup with Susan Collins. The panel walks through Jackson's on-stage "Oh, shut up" moment, his FEC filings and hybrid ads with the DSCC, and Steve Robinson's read of out-of-state ActBlue money. | | | Voters across the nation face hurdles this fall. But **in North Carolina, voting restrictions are embedded in the very fabric of the state.**

North Carolina voters describe these roadblocks as a feature, not a bug, of the state’s electoral system -- **one that’s littered with so much confusion that some may decide to stay home and not vote at all.**

clean_body: Now is the time for your help. | | | | | | | 6 Days Until Early Vote. Friends, We have run with everything we had and we are not done. We are running to win and through the finish line. "You've run an amazing race!" "You're almost there for the win - keep it up!" Those are the words of encouragement we are hearing all over Maryland. But we have a task to finish - we need a final TV ad buy and we need your help to do it. To date, we've raised and spent over a quarter-million fighting for you. Now we need a final $50,000 to finish the TV ad buy with a new ad for the final election weeks. . Would you tonight? Time is of the essence - we need to finalize this by Monday. Thank you and now it's time to vote - let's win together for our families, our children and for all of Maryland. U.S. Senator Katie Britt, R-Alabama, recently attended the groundbreaking ceremony for the Mobile River Bridge and Bayway Project, the largest infrastructure project in Alabama’s history, which promises to transform transportation around the Gulf Coast after years of delay. Britt delivered remarks at the event, which also featured U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, Alabama Governor Kay Ivey, U.S. Senator Tommy Tuberville, R-Alabama, members of Alabama’s U.S. House delegation and other state leaders.

The U.S. Senate unanimously passed legislation introduced by U.S. Senator Katie Britt, R-Alabama, that would give certain clergy members a limited opportunity to re-enroll in Social Security after opting out. The Clergy Act, sponsored in the Senate by Britt and Senator Maggie Hassan, D-New Hampshire, passed by unanimous consent without amendment on September 30. * * *
# **Katie Zacharia exits as press secretary after just seven days**
Katie Zacharia **[is stepping down](https://substack.com/redirect/c77e3acc-efbd-4b0c-9539-f6b437696e80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as White House press secretary after only a week, with Trump telling reporters he suggested she "reconsider" the role following a rocky debut briefing that lasted just 14 minutes and included several verbal stumbles.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b841ad06-0150-4318-9ab7-4c57dcd3d616?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Zacharia faced scrutiny after acknowledging on "Hannity" that she never passed the bar** or obtained a U.S. law license, despite being introduced as an attorney, and defended her brief, underprepared briefing as her best effort given limited prep time.
* **Trump denied firing her, saying he wants her to have "a good life"** and that she'd been "brutalized by the media," while the White House previously defended her publicly even as comparisons to Anthony Scaramucci's notoriously short 10-day tenure circulated internally.

* * *
# **Armed bystander who killed Oregon school shooter identified as father of two students**
Kaylub Giamanco, a 36-year-old carpenter, has been **[identified as the bystander who confronted and killed the gunman](https://substack.com/redirect/4030b5e0-7b49-482f-8816-a2195cdde440?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** at Silver Rail Elementary School, where his two daughters attend. His brother said Giamanco heard gunshots while driving home for lunch, saw the shooter enter the school, and intervened using a concealed firearm he was carrying.

# **Construction wages rise as deportations tighten migrant labor supply**
Construction wages are **[climbing nationally](https://substack.com/redirect/8cd98aa0-5117-4677-ae46-52a52b9cea1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** following Trump's deportation enforcement, with Florida seeing the sharpest gains -- framing carpenters now earning roughly $42/hour, up from $20, according to a **[Wall Street Journal report](https://substack.com/redirect/e399d2b3-26ab-47a7-bb16-75cc7a7c6a93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** citing industry sources.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8cd98aa0-5117-4677-ae46-52a52b9cea1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Labor shortages have forced contractors to raise rates** and recruit more aggressively; one North Florida subcontractor reported a 70% drop in available crews, while national data shows construction craft worker pay rising around 5% year-over-year as of May 2026.
* **Texas has seen slower wage growth,** with workers there earning about $37/hour as of December 2025, as some construction associations continue lobbying for expanded migrant labor access despite the broader national wage trend favoring domestic workers.

* * *
# **Transgender substitute teacher convicted of threatening "murder spree" at Virginia school**
A Virginia jury convicted 19-year-old former substitute teacher Hadyn Dollery on multiple counts of threatening violence and property damage, facing up to 25 years combined after **[threatening a"murder spree"](https://substack.com/redirect/00519c21-6482-415f-a99d-b9c8d2e82c02?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** at John Champe High School following a breakup with a student.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/00519c21-6482-415f-a99d-b9c8d2e82c02?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Prosecutors said Dollery threatened to kill the ex-boyfriend,** members of both families, cannibalize a victim, and burn down the ex's home, with threats reported via the Safe2Talk app; the defense argued the messages reflected exaggerated "teenage drama" rather than genuine intent.
* **Media coverage varied in referring to Dollery 's gender identity,** with some outlets using female pronouns and the name "Sophie," others using male pronouns, and one omitting gender references entirely. Dollery is being held alone at Loudoun County's detention facility.

body:
This is a long but critically important read.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Across Texas, people are struggling in ways they've never struggled before. Working people donating plasma before their shift just to cover the bills. Families rationing insulin. Small businesses closing because property taxes have gotten so out of hand.
But everywhere Gina goes, she hears something else too:_that this movement is giving them hope._ We’re closer than we’ve ever been before, but we have a long way to go. People still worry if we can actually win here.
We understand that skepticism. Democrats have been saying Texas is turning for years. **But something is different now, and we need you to see the numbers.**
Gina’s campaign manager Amy put together a memo on exactly where this race stands. Six separate polls now show us ahead. Abbott's own strategist is admitting it will be close. Conservatives across Texas are crossing over — on schools, on data centers, on the simple question of whether this state belongs to the people or to Greg Abbott's billionaire donors.
**[Read the memo. Then, if you believe what we believe — that we can actually win this — we’re asking you to pitch in whatever you can.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261016_3_memo.iJukd1&refcode=em20261016-2444&t=1&akid=2444%2E299639%2EK44BD1)**
[Donate »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261016_3_memo.iJukd1&refcode=em20261016-2444&t=2&akid=2444%2E299639%2EK44BD1)
=============================================================
**OCTOBER 2026 CAMPAIGN MEMO ON TX-GOV**
**FROM:** Amy Friedman, Campaign Manager, Gina for Texas
**TO:** Interested Parties
Let me tell you where this race actually stands — because what's happening in Texas right now is something I don't think the national establishment fully understands yet.

**Gina Hinojosa is leading Greg Abbott in six of the most recent polls. That’s never happened before.**
This race is closer than ever but some people still don’t believe we can win — that’s exactly why I'm writing this memo. And it's exactly why this race could slip away if we don't act.
Here's the polling picture. This race has moved steadily and dramatically in Gina's direction since the spring:
* Texas Politics Project (April 2026): Abbott +5
* TPOR (July 2026): Abbott +3, inside the margin of error
* N+ Univision (September 9): Tied 47–47, with Gina leading Latino voters by 12
* ReconMR/Siena (September 17): **Gina leads 49–45** — independents breaking for Gina 65–27
* NPR/Marist (September 23): **Gina leads 49–46** , winning independents 52–39, pulling 9% of self-identified Republicans
* NYT/Siena (October 4):**Gina leads 49–46** , winning independents 55–39, and leading among Latino voters by 31 points
* YouGov (October 2026): **Gina +1**
* GBAO Poll (October 13): **Gina +2**
* UT/Texas Politics Project (October 14): **Gina +1**

Both RealClearPolitics and Nate Silver's Silver Bulletin have the polling average under 2 points. This is a toss-up.
**Abbott is outspending us 10 to 1 — and he still isn’t getting the result he wants.**
Between July 30 and September 8 alone, Abbott outspent Gina $28 million to $2 million on advertising. Over the full race, he's spent $47 million to our $5 million. Despite that, Gina leads in six of the most recent polls. Abbott's favorability has gone deeply negative — 45% favorable, 53% unfavorable — and his job approval has flipped the same way. He's even polling 13% unfavorable among his own Republicans.
Abbott is a damaged incumbent with a nine-figure war chest. The only thing keeping this race from breaking open is the spending gap.
But here’s the truth: The more money Abbott spends lying about Gina’s record, the more vulnerable we are. _We have to raise more money to reach the voters who haven’t heard from us yet._
**Something real is happening on the ground — and Republicans know it.**
Lifelong conservative voters are publicly breaking with Abbott over two issues.
On education: conservative moms who backed Abbott before are now appearing at Gina's events, frustrated by a decade of voucher schemes and defunded public schools. Gina is running an ad featuring a self-described MAGA conservative who protested on January 6 — and is now voting for Gina because of schools.
On data centers: rural Republican protest groups — including one in Lubbock led by Republicans — are furious about unregulated expansion driving up electricity bills. Abbott championed data centers for years, took millions from their developers, and is now scrambling to reverse course. Gina called for a moratorium from day one.
As Gina put it to The Nation: The data-center issue is the latest example of a governor doing the bidding of moneyed interests and not the people of Texas. And it is angering MAGA Republicans — not country-club Republicans, not Chamber of Commerce Republicans. There is an opportunity for alliances to be forged when we are pursuing a populist agenda.
**Even Abbott's own team is admitting this race is close.**
Abbott's longtime political strategist was asked about the tightening polls. His response: "Is it going to be close on Election Day? Yes." That’s Abbott's own guy publicly conceding this goes to the wire. And when pressed on his best argument against Gina? He went to culture wars and lies on income tax votes — not data centers, not schools, not the affordability crisis Abbott has presided over for twelve years. When culture wars are the best attack you can come up with, you're losing ground.
**The coalition winning this race doesn't look like past Texas Democratic coalitions.**
Gina leads independents by 38 points in the Siena poll. She's winning women 57–40%, voters under 45 by 60–33%, and Gen Z 71–19%. She's pulling 9% of self-identified Republicans. In TX-15 — a district Trump carried 58–41 — a House Majority PAC poll shows Gina leading 52–47.
This is a cross-partisan, cross-regional majority being built in real time. _Gina is earning support from Texans who have never voted for a Democrat before in their lives._
**When Texas Democrats run strong, the whole map shifts.**
In 2018, when Beto lost the Senate race by just 2.6 points, that wave energy flipped 12 State House seats, 2 State Senate seats, and 2 congressional seats. And the stakes this cycle go even further: if Abbott wins another term, Republicans will redraw the congressional map again. Combined with seats Texas gains after the next Census, that could put nine or ten congressional seats permanently out of Democratic reach — one-party control of Congress, likely for a generation. A governor who vetoes rigged maps changes all of that. As Gina said: _"We flip Texas, and it's over."_
**The bottom line.**
Six polls show Gina leading. One has us tied. Abbott is underwater on favorability and approval. Conservatives are crossing over to support our campaign. The polling average is under 2 points. Abbott's own strategist admits this race will be close.
_This race is winnable._ But Abbott is going to spend over $106 million to try to buy his lead back in the final few weeks of this race.
Gina has raised a fraction of Abbott’s war chest. The only thing that closes the spending gap is donors who understand what's actually happening in Texas right now — and decide this race is worth their investment.
We can win this. But only if people show up.
=============================================================
Peter, we'll leave you with this.
Greg Abbott has been in statewide office for 30 years. He has 98 percent name recognition. He has raised over $106 million to run this campaign. And he still can’t grab onto an insurmountable lead in this race.
Texans know his record. They know who he works for. And they're ready for something different.
The only question is whether we have what it takes to close this out — whether the people who believe Texas can change are willing to put real resources behind it in these final weeks.
We have people working in every corner of this state who are hungry for this. Abbott's own team is bracing for a close race. Six polls have us ahead.
We can win this. But not without you.
**[Will you rush a donation to our campaign right now?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261016_3_memo.iJukd1&refcode=em20261016-2444&t=3&akid=2444%2E299639%2EK44BD1)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261016_3_memo.LusP5m&amount=5&refcode=em20261016-2444&t=4&akid=2444%2E299639%2EK44BD1)
Thank you for believing in what we're building together.
— Team Gina

[ Donate » ](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_gh_footer?refcode=em20261016-4&t=5&refcode2=2444_299639_K44BD1&akid=2444%2E299639%2EK44BD1)
[ Donate Weekly » ](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_gh_footer?refcode=em20261016-4&recurring=1&t=6&refcode2=2444_299639_K44BD1&akid=2444%2E299639%2EK44BD1)

Austin, TX 78703

body:
He's throwing money at our democracy to try buying the outcome he wants. [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/87341?t=1&akid=9923%2E22930333%2EOhHI1D)
---
Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to flip Congress in 18 days. If you need help checking your voter registration or making a plan to vote, please visit [iwillvote.com](https://ak.democrats.org/go/9784?t=2&akid=9923%2E22930333%2EOhHI1D). If you'd prefer to [receive fewer emails](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=3&akid=9923%2E22930333%2EOhHI1D) or [stop receiving our emails](https://ak.democrats.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=4&akid=9923%2E22930333%2EOhHI1D), you can click [here](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=5&akid=9923%2E22930333%2EOhHI1D). Derek, he isn’t stopping, and we cannot afford to wait. Elon Musk, the first trillionaire in history, has spent _**$366 million**_ so far to keep Republicans in control of the House and Senate. **_That’s more than he spent in 2024 to get Trump elected._** And frankly, that’s an insane amount of money for one person to spend in a lifetime, let alone in one year. _But to Elon, it’s just a drop in the bucket._ **In fact, it’s the equivalent of the median American household spending just $32.** Elon Musk is treating America’s elections like an investment to boost **_his bottom line_** — not a democracy that should work for all of us. But here’s the truth, Derek: _He’s doing this because he’s scared._ Elon Musk is seeing what we’re seeing: Democrats standing up and fighting back against Donald Trump’s destructive agenda and Republican poll numbers dropping by the day. That’s why he’s throwing money at Republicans trying to buy the outcome he wants. [**Derek, we know you (probably) don’t have $366 million to donate. We’ll never ask _anyone_ to donate that much. But if you can spare $32, or any amount that makes sense to you, we’ll put it to work right away helping Democrats win the midterms. name: Tobias Read
subject: my thoughts on yesterday's tragedy
body:
| | |
---
| | | I was sitting in my office in the State Capitol yesterday, going over my calendar for the next few weeks, when my Chief of Staff stepped in to alert me of the school shooting at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend. We turned on the television and watched the news unfold. I knew that eventually I would need to share my thoughts. Just as I have had to do every time this horrible situation plays out far too commonly across our state and our country. My first thoughts were dominated by my emotions. Anger. Frustration. Fatigue. Helplessness. Sadness. Shaped not only by experiences as an elected official, but as a father of two teenagers. In 2022, I decided that I had grown tired enough of these preventable tragedies that I joined a bunch of Oregonians at a press conference in support of what was then IP17 and what would become Ballot Measure 114. It was the first time I stood in front of a microphone and choked up as I explained my support for this measure. Here is what I said then: _I’m a parent of two wonderful kids...whose laughter and kindness bring me more joy than any other accomplishment in my life. But like most parents, I hold my breath a bit when they leave for school. _ _And my heart breaks a bit when my wife and I have to carefully explain the latest school shooting and how they need to pay attention during their school’s active shooter drills._ _By many, many measures—this being just the most visceral and immediately dangerous—we are failing our kids. _ _I’m sad, I’m angry and I’m frustrated... _ _You're either willing to help get guns off the streets and out of the hands of young people who are killing each other at an alarming rate in this state, or you are not. _ _It’s quite simple..._ _And while I’m angry and frustrated, I’m not willing to give into cynicism. We have choices, and we can do better. _ _We must do better. And we must prioritize the wellbeing of our kids._ So while I’m angry, and frustrated and sad today I still refuse to give into cynicism. We still have choices. And we must choose to put our kids first. Safer schools, more counseling and mental health support, fewer guns in the hands of kids...all of it. Focused more on outcomes and less on politics. I’m also usually asked by other Oregonians what we can do to support our neighbors and friends in moments like this. Here are some general guidelines that are worth keeping in mind: **Prevent misinformation** : Please avoid sharing unverified reports, images or identifying information about victims; **Support children and families** : Check in with loved ones, and provide emotional support; **Respect privacy** : Give affected families and the school community time and space to process this tragedy. Also, direct those around you who need some extra help to these free and confidential mental health resources: **988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline**: Call or text **988** for free, confidential emotional support, available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. clean_body: | | | | | | I was sitting in my office in the State Capitol yesterday, going over my calendar for the next few weeks, when my Chief of Staff stepped in to alert me of the school shooting at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend. We turned on the television and watched the news unfold. I knew that eventually I would need to share my thoughts. Just as I have had to do every time this horrible situation plays out far too commonly across our state and our country. My first thoughts were dominated by my emotions. Anger. Frustration. Fatigue. Helplessness. Sadness. Shaped not only by experiences as an elected official, but as a father of two teenagers. In 2022, I decided that I had grown tired enough of these preventable tragedies that I joined a bunch of Oregonians at a press conference in support of what was then IP17 and what would become Ballot Measure 114. It was the first time I stood in front of a microphone and choked up as I explained my support for this measure. Here is what I said then: I’m a parent of two wonderful kids...whose laughter and kindness bring me more joy than any other accomplishment in my life. But like most parents, I hold my breath a bit when they leave for school. And my heart breaks a bit when my wife and I have to carefully explain the latest school shooting and how they need to pay attention during their school’s active shooter drills. By many, many measures—this being just the most visceral and immediately dangerous—we are failing our kids. I’m sad, I’m angry and I’m frustrated... You're either willing to help get guns off the streets and out of the hands of young people who are killing each other at an alarming rate in this state, or you are not. It’s quite simple... And while I’m angry and frustrated, I’m not willing to give into cynicism. We have choices, and we can do better. We must do better. And we must prioritize the wellbeing of our kids. So while I’m angry, and frustrated and sad today I still refuse to give into cynicism. We still have choices. And we must choose to put our kids first. Safer schools, more counseling and mental health support, fewer guns in the hands of kids...all of it. Focused more on outcomes and less on politics. I’m also usually asked by other Oregonians what we can do to support our neighbors and friends in moments like this. Here are some general guidelines that are worth keeping in mind: Prevent misinformation : Please avoid sharing unverified reports, images or identifying information about victims; Support children and families : Check in with loved ones, and provide emotional support; Respect privacy : Give affected families and the school community time and space to process this tragedy. Also, direct those around you who need some extra help to these free and confidential mental health resources: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: Call or text 988 for free, confidential emotional support, available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Spanish-language support is also available. YouthLine : Call 877-968-8491 or text teen2teen to 839863 for support designed for teens and young adults. 211info : Dial 211 or visit for information about community services and available support resources. Yet as our chances of winning an outright majority grow by the day, the president, his party, and the billionaires bankrolling their races are growing increasingly desperate to keep their grip on power.

Between now and Election Day, Republicans are on track to outspend our candidates on the airwaves in eight of the top 10 Senate battlegrounds – in Texas, we’re at a disadvantage of 8-to-1! That’s thanks in no small part to the staggering $366 million Elon Musk has personally spent this cycle, with just under half going to the top super PAC for the Senate GOP.

In some states (including Washington!), ballots are out and people are already voting – but unless folks like you chip in today, we will not have the grassroots resources to help at-risk Democratic incumbents and challengers compete. **That’s why I’m extending the deadline until 11:59 p.m. tonight.**
